ingredients: 2 cups cooked rice, 200g chicken breast (diced), 2 eggs, 2 tbsp soy sauce, 3 cloves garlic (minced), 1 medium carrot (diced), 1/2 cup frozen peas, 2 tbsp vegetable oil, 1/2 tsp salt, 1/4 tsp white pepper, 2 green onions (sliced)
instructions: Heat 1 tbsp oil in a wok over high heat until smoking | Scramble the 2 beaten eggs until just set, then remove and set aside | Add remaining oil and stir-fry diced chicken breast until golden brown and cooked through, about 4-5 minutes | Add minced garlic and stir-fry for 30 seconds until fragrant | Add cold cooked rice and break up any clumps with a spatula, stir-frying for 3 minutes | Drizzle soy sauce evenly over rice and toss well to combine | Add diced carrots and frozen peas, cooking for another 2 minutes until vegetables are tender | Return scrambled eggs to the wok and break them apart while mixing | Season with salt and white pepper | Garnish with sliced green onions and serve immediately while hot

ingredients: 400g spaghetti, 200g guanciale or thick-cut bacon (diced), 4 large egg yolks, 2 whole eggs, 100g Pecorino Romano cheese (finely grated), 50g Parmesan cheese (finely grated), 2 tsp freshly ground black pepper, 1 tbsp salt (for pasta water)
instructions: Bring a large pot of water to a rolling boil and add 1 tbsp salt | Cook spaghetti until al dente, about 8-9 minutes | While pasta cooks, fry diced guanciale in a cold pan over medium heat until fat renders and meat is crispy, about 8 minutes, then remove from heat | In a bowl, whisk together egg yolks, whole eggs, grated Pecorino, grated Parmesan, and black pepper until smooth | Reserve 1 cup of pasta water before draining | Drain spaghetti and immediately add to the pan with hot guanciale, tossing well off the heat | Pour egg-cheese mixture over hot pasta and toss vigorously for 1-2 minutes, adding splashes of reserved pasta water as needed to create a silky, creamy sauce | The sauce should coat each strand and have a glossy appearance | Plate immediately and top with extra grated Pecorino and a crack of black pepper | Serve at once while hot and creamy

ingredients: 600g chicken thighs (bone-in, skinless), 1 can (400ml) coconut milk, 2 tbsp curry powder, 2 medium onions (finely diced), 4 cloves garlic (minced), 1 tbsp ginger (grated), 2 tbsp vegetable oil, 2 medium tomatoes (diced), 1 tsp turmeric powder, 1 tsp cumin powder, 1 tsp salt, 1/2 tsp chili powder, fresh cilantro for garnish
instructions: Heat vegetable oil in a heavy-bottomed pot over medium heat | Saut? finely diced onions for 8-10 minutes until deeply golden brown, stirring frequently | Add minced garlic and grated ginger, cooking for 1 minute until fragrant | Add chicken pieces and brown on all sides for about 5-6 minutes | Stir in curry powder, turmeric, cumin, and chili powder, cooking for 1-2 minutes to bloom the spices | Add diced tomatoes and cook until they soften and release their juices, about 3 minutes | Pour in the can of coconut milk and stir well to combine | Bring to a gentle simmer, then cover and cook on low heat for 25-30 minutes until chicken is tender and falling off the bone | Remove lid and simmer for 5 more minutes if sauce needs thickening | Season with salt and adjust spices to taste | Garnish with fresh chopped cilantro and serve hot over steamed basmati rice

ingredients: 500g ground beef (80/20), 2 tbsp taco seasoning, 1/3 cup water, 8 small corn or flour tortillas, 1 cup iceberg lettuce (shredded), 2 medium tomatoes (diced), 1 cup shredded cheddar cheese, 1/2 cup sour cream, 1 small onion (diced), 1 lime (cut into wedges), 1 tbsp vegetable oil, salt to taste
instructions: Heat vegetable oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat | Add ground beef and cook, breaking it apart with a wooden spoon, until browned all over, about 6-7 minutes | Drain excess fat carefully from the skillet | Sprinkle taco seasoning evenly over meat and add 1/3 cup water, stirring to combine | Reduce heat to low and simmer for 5 minutes until sauce thickens and coats the meat | While meat simmers, warm tortillas in a dry pan or microwave for 20-30 seconds until pliable | Shred iceberg lettuce finely and dice tomatoes and onion | Fill each warm tortilla with a generous scoop of seasoned beef | Top with shredded lettuce, diced tomatoes, diced onion, and shredded cheddar cheese | Add a dollop of sour cream and a squeeze of fresh lime juice | Fold tortillas and serve immediately

ingredients: 1 1/2 cups dried red lentils, 1.5 liters vegetable broth, 2 medium carrots (diced), 3 celery stalks (diced), 1 large onion (diced), 4 cloves garlic (minced), 3 tbsp olive oil, 1 tsp ground cumin, 1/2 tsp turmeric, 1 bay leaf, salt and black pepper to taste, lemon wedges for serving
instructions: Rinse red lentils thoroughly under cold running water until water runs clear, about 2 minutes | Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium heat | Saut? diced onion and minced garlic for 5 minutes until softened and translucent | Add diced carrots and celery and cook for another 5 minutes, stirring occasionally | Stir in ground cumin and turmeric, cooking for 1 minute to release their aroma | Pour in vegetable broth and add rinsed lentils and the bay leaf | Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low and cover partially | Simmer for 25-30 minutes, stirring occasionally, until lentils are completely tender and falling apart | Remove bay leaf and season generously with salt and black pepper | For a smoother texture, blend half the soup with an immersion blender and return to pot | Serve hot in bowls with a squeeze of fresh lemon juice and a drizzle of olive oil

ingredients: 1 pizza dough ball (250g), 1/2 cup San Marzano tomato sauce, 200g fresh mozzarella cheese, 8-10 fresh basil leaves, 2 tbsp extra virgin olive oil, 1/2 tsp salt, semolina flour for dusting
instructions: Preheat oven to its highest setting (475?F / 245?C) with a pizza stone or inverted baking sheet inside for at least 30 minutes | Dust a clean work surface with semolina flour and stretch pizza dough by hand into a 12-inch round, keeping edges slightly thicker | Transfer stretched dough onto a floured pizza peel or parchment paper | Spread tomato sauce in a thin, even layer leaving a 1-inch border around the edges | Tear fresh mozzarella into small pieces and distribute evenly across the pizza | Drizzle 1 tbsp of olive oil over the top and sprinkle with a pinch of salt | Carefully slide pizza onto the preheated stone and bake for 10-12 minutes until crust is golden brown and cheese is bubbling | Remove from oven and immediately scatter fresh basil leaves over the hot pizza | Drizzle remaining olive oil and let rest for 1 minute | Slice into 8 wedges and serve immediately

ingredients: 2 cups sushi rice (uncooked), 2 1/2 cups water, 4 tbsp rice vinegar, 1 tbsp sugar, 1 tsp salt, 6 sheets nori seaweed, 200g fresh salmon (sushi-grade, sliced into strips), 1 ripe avocado (sliced), 1 small cucumber (julienned), soy sauce for serving, wasabi for serving, pickled ginger for serving
instructions: Rinse sushi rice in cold water until water runs clear, about 3-4 rinses | Cook rice with 2 1/2 cups water in a rice cooker or covered pot until tender | While still hot, fold in a mixture of rice vinegar, sugar, and salt using a cutting motion, then fan rice to cool to room temperature | Place a sheet of nori shiny side down on a bamboo rolling mat | With wet hands, spread an even thin layer of cooled sushi rice over nori leaving a 2cm strip empty at the top edge | Lay strips of fresh salmon, avocado slices, and cucumber along the center of the rice | Using the bamboo mat, roll firmly from the bottom edge, tucking the filling as you go, applying even pressure | Once rolled, gently squeeze the mat around the roll to seal tightly | Using a sharp knife dipped in water, slice roll into 8 even pieces, wiping the blade between cuts | Arrange on a plate and serve with soy sauce, wasabi, and pickled ginger

ingredients: 1 1/2 cups all-purpose flour, 3 1/2 tsp baking powder, 2 tbsp granulated sugar, 1/2 tsp salt, 1 1/4 cups whole milk, 1 large egg, 3 tbsp melted butter (plus extra for cooking), 1 tsp vanilla extract, maple syrup for serving, fresh berries for garnish (optional)
instructions: In a large bowl, sift together flour, baking powder, sugar, and salt | In a separate bowl, whisk together milk, egg, melted butter, and vanilla extract until well combined | Pour wet ingredients into dry ingredients and stir gently until just combined ? batter should be slightly lumpy, do not overmix | Let batter rest for 5 minutes while the pan heats up | Heat a griddle or non-stick pan over medium heat and lightly brush with melted butter | Pour about 1/4 cup batter per pancake onto the hot surface, spacing them apart | Cook until bubbles form on the surface and edges look set, about 2-3 minutes | Flip carefully and cook the other side until golden brown, about 1-2 minutes more | Transfer cooked pancakes to a warm plate and repeat with remaining batter | Serve in a stack topped with a pat of butter and a generous drizzle of maple syrup, with fresh berries on the side if desired

ingredients: 4 cod fillets (150g each), 1 1/2 cups all-purpose flour, 1 tsp baking powder, 1 tsp salt, 1/2 tsp black pepper, 1 large egg, 1 1/4 cups cold beer or sparkling water, 4 large russet potatoes, vegetable oil for deep frying, malt vinegar for serving, lemon wedges for serving, salt for seasoning
instructions: Peel potatoes and cut into thick chips about 1cm wide | Soak chips in cold water for 30 minutes to remove excess starch, then drain and pat completely dry | Heat oil in a deep fryer or heavy pot to 160?C (320?F) | Blanch chips in oil for 4-5 minutes until cooked through but not colored, then remove and drain on paper towels | Increase oil temperature to 190?C (375?F) | Pat cod fillets dry and season with salt and pepper | In a bowl, whisk together flour, baking powder, salt, and pepper | Beat in egg and cold beer/sparkling water until a smooth batter forms | Dip each cod fillet into the batter, letting excess drip off | Carefully lower battered fish into hot oil and fry for 5-6 minutes until golden and crispy | While fish fries, return chips to oil and fry for 2-3 minutes until golden and crisp | Drain everything on paper towels and season chips generously with salt | Plate fish and chips together and serve immediately with malt vinegar and lemon wedges

ingredients: 2 cups dried chickpeas (soaked overnight), 1 small onion (roughly chopped), 4 cloves garlic, 1 cup fresh parsley, 1/2 cup fresh cilantro, 2 tsp ground cumin, 1 tsp ground coriander, 1 tsp salt, 1/2 tsp baking soda, vegetable oil for deep frying, 4 large pita breads, 1/2 cup tahini sauce, 1 cup lettuce (shredded), 2 tomatoes (sliced), pickled turnips for serving
instructions: Drain and rinse chickpeas that have been soaked for at least 12 hours ? do not use canned | In a food processor, combine chickpeas, onion, garlic, parsley, cilantro, cumin, coriander, and salt | Pulse until mixture is finely ground and holds together when pressed, scraping down sides as needed | Transfer mixture to a bowl, stir in baking soda, cover, and refrigerate for 1 hour | Heat vegetable oil in a deep pot to 175?C (350?F) | Shape falafel mixture into small balls or patties about 2 tablespoons each, pressing firmly | Carefully lower falafel into hot oil in batches and fry for 3-4 minutes until deep golden brown and crispy | Drain on paper towels | Warm pita breads in a dry pan or oven for 1-2 minutes | Spread a generous amount of tahini sauce inside each pita | Add shredded lettuce, sliced tomatoes, and pickled turnips | Place 3-4 falafel balls inside each pita, wrap tightly, and serve immediately

ingredients: 1 1/2 cups Bomba or Arborio rice, 4 cups chicken broth, 1/2 tsp saffron threads, 400g chicken thighs (bone-in, cut into pieces), 200g large shrimp (peeled and deveined), 12 fresh mussels (cleaned and debearded), 1/2 cup frozen peas, 1 red bell pepper (sliced into strips), 1 medium onion (diced), 4 cloves garlic (minced), 2 medium tomatoes (grated), 1 tsp smoked paprika, 3 tbsp olive oil, salt to taste, lemon wedges for serving, fresh parsley (chopped)
instructions: Heat olive oil in a large paella pan or wide shallow skillet over medium-high heat | Season chicken pieces with salt and brown them on all sides until golden, about 8-10 minutes, then push to edges of pan | Saut? diced onion in the center for 3 minutes until softened | Add sliced bell pepper and minced garlic, cooking for 2 more minutes | Stir in grated tomatoes and smoked paprika, cooking until tomato reduces, about 3 minutes | Add rice to the pan and stir to coat every grain with oil, toasting for 2 minutes | Warm chicken broth and steep saffron threads in it for 5 minutes, then pour evenly over rice | Gently shake the pan to distribute rice evenly ? do not stir from this point | Bring to a vigorous boil, then reduce heat to medium-low and simmer for 10 minutes | Nestle shrimp and mussels (hinge side down) into the rice and scatter peas on top | Continue cooking for another 8-10 minutes without stirring until rice is tender and liquid is absorbed | If bottom isn't crispy enough, increase heat for the final 2 minutes to create socarrat (crispy bottom) | Remove from heat, cover with a clean kitchen towel, and rest for 5 minutes | Garnish with chopped parsley and lemon wedges, then serve directly from the pan

ingredients: 1 3/4 cups all-purpose flour, 2 cups granulated sugar, 3/4 cup unsweetened cocoa powder, 2 tsp baking soda, 1 tsp baking powder, 1 tsp salt, 2 large eggs, 1 cup whole milk, 1/2 cup vegetable oil, 2 tsp vanilla extract, 1 cup hot coffee or hot water, 1/2 cup unsalted butter (softened, for frosting), 3 cups powdered sugar, 1/4 cup cocoa powder (for frosting)
instructions: Preheat oven to 350?F (175?C) and grease and flour two 9-inch round cake pans | In a large bowl, sift together flour, sugar, 3/4 cup cocoa powder, baking soda, baking powder, and salt | In a separate bowl, beat eggs, milk, vegetable oil, and vanilla extract until well combined | Gradually add wet ingredients to dry ingredients, mixing on medium speed for 2 minutes | Slowly pour in hot coffee (or hot water) while mixing on low speed ? batter will be thin, this is normal | Divide batter evenly between prepared pans | Bake for 30-35 minutes until a toothpick inserted in the center comes out clean | Cool cakes in pans for 10 minutes, then turn out onto wire racks to cool completely | For frosting: beat softened butter until creamy, then gradually add powdered sugar and 1/4 cup cocoa powder, alternating with 2-3 tbsp milk until smooth and spreadable | Place one cake layer on a serving plate and spread frosting on top | Place second layer on top and frost the top and sides evenly | Slice and serve at room temperature

ingredients: 1 large eggplant (cut into 1/2-inch rounds), 2 medium zucchini (cut into 1/2-inch rounds), 4 ripe tomatoes (cut into 1/2-inch rounds), 1 medium onion (diced), 1 red bell pepper (diced), 1 yellow bell pepper (diced), 4 cloves garlic (minced), 4 tbsp olive oil, 1 tsp dried thyme, 1 tsp dried oregano, 1/2 tsp dried rosemary, salt and black pepper to taste, fresh basil leaves for garnish
instructions: Preheat oven to 375?F (190?C) | Heat 2 tbsp olive oil in a skillet over medium heat and saut? diced onion and bell peppers for 8 minutes until soft | Add minced garlic, thyme, oregano, and rosemary, cooking for 1 minute until fragrant | Spread this onion-pepper mixture evenly on the bottom of a large baking dish | Slice eggplant, zucchini, and tomatoes into uniform 1/2-inch rounds | Arrange sliced vegetables in the baking dish in alternating overlapping rows (eggplant, zucchini, tomato, repeat) for a visually appealing spiral or striped pattern | Drizzle remaining 2 tbsp olive oil generously over the arranged vegetables | Season with salt and black pepper | Cover dish with parchment paper or foil and bake for 30 minutes | Remove cover and continue baking for another 15-20 minutes until vegetables are tender and lightly caramelized on top | Let rest for 5 minutes, then garnish with fresh torn basil leaves | Serve hot, warm, or at room temperature ? flavors improve the next day

ingredients: 2 liters beef broth, 500g rice noodles (banh pho, flat), 300g beef sirloin (very thinly sliced), 2-inch piece fresh ginger (halved and charred), 2 onions (halved and charred), 3 star anise pods, 1 cinnamon stick, 3 cloves, 1 tbsp coriander seeds, 2 tbsp fish sauce, 1 tbsp sugar, 1 cup fresh cilantro (chopped), 1 cup fresh Thai basil leaves, 2 limes (cut into wedges), 2 cups bean sprouts, 2 fresh chili peppers (sliced), hoisin sauce for serving, sriracha for serving
instructions: Char ginger and onion halves under a broiler or over an open flame until blackened, about 5 minutes | In a large pot, bring beef broth to a gentle simmer | Add charred ginger, onion, star anise, cinnamon stick, cloves, and coriander seeds | Simmer for 30-45 minutes to infuse flavors | Strain broth through a fine mesh sieve, discarding solids, and return clear broth to pot | Season broth with fish sauce and sugar, adjusting to taste, and keep hot | Cook rice noodles according to package directions until al dente, then drain and rinse under cold water to stop cooking | Slice beef sirloin as thinly as possible against the grain ? almost paper-thin | Divide cooked noodles among large serving bowls | Arrange raw beef slices in a single layer on top of noodles | Ladle boiling hot broth directly over the raw beef ? the heat will cook it instantly | Serve immediately with a platter of fresh cilantro, Thai basil, bean sprouts, lime wedges, and sliced chilies | Each person adds herbs and condiments to taste, along with hoisin and sriracha

ingredients: 500g ground beef (80/20), 1 can (400g) kidney beans (drained and rinsed), 1 can (400g) crushed tomatoes, 1 large onion (diced), 4 cloves garlic (minced), 2 tbsp chili powder, 1 tbsp ground cumin, 1 tsp smoked paprika, 1/2 tsp cayenne pepper (optional), 1 cup beef broth, 1 tbsp tomato paste, 1 tbsp vegetable oil, salt and black pepper to taste, shredded cheddar cheese for topping, sour cream for serving, fresh cilantro (chopped)
instructions: Heat vegetable oil in a large heavy-bottomed pot over medium-high heat | Add ground beef and cook, breaking it apart with a wooden spoon, until browned all over, about 8 minutes | Add diced onion and cook for 5 minutes until softened | Stir in minced garlic, chili powder, cumin, smoked paprika, and cayenne, cooking for 1-2 minutes until spices are fragrant | Add tomato paste and stir for 1 minute to caramelize slightly | Pour in crushed tomatoes, drained kidney beans, and beef broth, stirring well to combine | Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low and cover partially | Simmer for 30-40 minutes, stirring occasionally to prevent sticking, until thick and rich | If too thick, add a splash of water; if too thin, simmer uncovered for 10 more minutes | Season generously with salt and black pepper | Ladle into bowls and top with shredded cheddar, a dollop of sour cream, and fresh cilantro | Serve with steamed rice, cornbread, or tortilla chips on the side

ingredients: 250g flat rice noodles (dried), 200g large shrimp (peeled and deveined), 150g firm tofu (pressed and cubed), 2 large eggs, 3 tbsp fish sauce, 2 tbsp tamarind paste, 2 tbsp sugar, 1 tbsp rice vinegar, 1/2 tsp chili flakes, 3 tbsp vegetable oil, 3 cloves garlic (minced), 1/4 cup roasted peanuts (crushed), 2 cups bean sprouts, 3 green onions (cut into 2-inch pieces), 1 lime (cut into wedges), fresh cilantro for garnish
instructions: Soak dried rice noodles in warm water for 30 minutes until softened but still firm, then drain well | In a small bowl, mix fish sauce, tamarind paste, sugar, rice vinegar, and chili flakes into a sauce ? stir until sugar dissolves | Heat 1 tbsp oil in a wok over high heat and stir-fry tofu cubes until golden on all sides, about 3 minutes, then remove and set aside | Add another tbsp oil to wok and stir-fry shrimp until pink, about 2 minutes per side, then remove and set aside | Add remaining oil and saut? minced garlic for 30 seconds until fragrant | Push garlic to side, crack in eggs, and scramble until just set | Add drained noodles and the prepared sauce to the wok, tossing with tongs for 2 minutes until noodles are coated and tender | Return tofu and shrimp to the wok, add green onions and half the bean sprouts, and toss for 1 more minute | Transfer to serving plates and top with crushed peanuts, remaining bean sprouts, and fresh cilantro | Serve immediately with lime wedges on the side for squeezing over

ingredients: 6 thick slices day-old brioche or challah bread, 3 large eggs, 2/3 cup whole milk, 1 tsp ground cinnamon, 1 tsp vanilla extract, 1 tbsp granulated sugar, pinch of salt, 2 tbsp unsalted butter (for frying), maple syrup for serving, fresh berries for topping (optional), powdered sugar for dusting
instructions: In a shallow wide bowl, whisk together eggs, milk, cinnamon, vanilla extract, sugar, and a pinch of salt until fully combined and smooth | Cut bread into thick 1-inch slices ? slightly stale bread works best as it absorbs custard without falling apart | Heat 1 tbsp butter in a large non-stick skillet or griddle over medium heat until melted and foaming | Quickly dip each bread slice into the egg mixture, letting it soak for 15-20 seconds per side ? don't oversoak or it will become soggy | Let excess custard drip off before placing bread in the hot pan | Cook for 3-4 minutes per side until deeply golden brown and crispy on the outside with a slight give in the center | Sprinkle a little extra sugar on each side while cooking for a caramelized crust | Add remaining butter to pan as needed for subsequent batches | Transfer to a warm plate and keep in a low oven while cooking remaining slices | Serve in a stack dusted with powdered sugar, topped with fresh berries if desired, with warm maple syrup on the side

ingredients: 600g beef chuck (cut into 2-inch cubes), 2 large onions (diced), 3 tbsp sweet Hungarian paprika, 1 tsp caraway seeds, 2 medium tomatoes (diced), 1 green bell pepper (diced), 3 medium potatoes (peeled and cubed), 2 carrots (sliced into rounds), 4 cups beef broth, 3 tbsp vegetable oil, 3 cloves garlic (minced), 1 bay leaf, salt and black pepper to taste, crusty bread for serving, sour cream for garnish
instructions: Season beef cubes generously with salt and pepper | Heat 2 tbsp oil in a large Dutch oven or heavy pot over high heat | Brown beef in batches, searing on all sides until deep brown, about 3-4 minutes per batch ? don't crowd the pot | Remove beef and set aside | Reduce heat to medium, add remaining oil, and saut? diced onions for 8-10 minutes until golden and soft | Add minced garlic and caraway seeds, cooking for 1 minute | Remove pot from heat, stir in paprika (this prevents it from burning and turning bitter), then return to low heat | Add diced tomatoes and bell pepper, cooking for 3 minutes | Return beef to pot, pour in beef broth, add bay leaf, and bring to a boil | Cover, reduce heat to low, and simmer for 1 hour | Add cubed potatoes and sliced carrots, then continue simmering for another 30-40 minutes until beef is fork-tender and vegetables are cooked through | Remove bay leaf and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper | Ladle into deep bowls, add a dollop of sour cream on top, and serve with thick slices of crusty bread for dipping

ingredients: 1 large cucumber, 2 cups full-fat Greek yogurt, 3 cloves garlic (minced), 2 tbsp extra virgin olive oil, 2 tbsp fresh dill (finely chopped), 1 tbsp fresh lemon juice, 1/2 tsp salt, 1/4 tsp white pepper
instructions: Grate cucumber using the large holes of a box grater ? no need to peel unless skin is very thick | Place grated cucumber in a clean kitchen towel or cheesecloth and squeeze firmly to remove as much excess water as possible ? this prevents tzatziki from becoming watery | In a medium bowl, combine Greek yogurt, minced garlic, olive oil, chopped dill, and lemon juice | Stir in the squeezed cucumber until evenly distributed | Season with salt and white pepper, tasting and adjusting as needed | Cover bowl with plastic wrap and refrigerate for at least 1 hour, preferably 2-3 hours, to allow flavors to meld and texture to firm up | Before serving, stir once more and drizzle with a tiny amount of olive oil on top | Serve chilled as a dip with warm pita bread, as a sauce for grilled meats, or as a side with falafel and vegetables

ingredients: 600g boneless chicken thighs (cut into bite-size pieces), 1 cup plain yogurt, 2 tbsp lemon juice, 2 tsp garam masala, 1 tsp turmeric, 1 tsp cumin, 1 tsp chili powder, 1 tbsp grated ginger, 4 cloves garlic (minced), 2 tbsp butter, 1 tbsp vegetable oil, 1 medium onion (finely diced), 1 can (400g) crushed tomatoes, 1 cup heavy cream, 1 tsp sugar, salt to taste, fresh cilantro for garnish, steamed basmati rice or naan for serving
instructions: In a large bowl, combine yogurt, lemon juice, 1 tsp garam masala, turmeric, cumin, chili powder, half the grated ginger, and half the minced garlic | Add chicken pieces and coat well, then cover and marinate in the refrigerator for at least 1 hour, preferably 4-6 hours | Thread marinated chicken onto skewers or spread on a baking sheet and grill/broil for 10-12 minutes until slightly charred on edges, turning once ? chicken can also be pan-fried in batches | In a large deep pan, melt butter with vegetable oil over medium heat | Saut? finely diced onion for 6-8 minutes until soft and golden | Add remaining ginger and garlic, cooking for 1 minute until fragrant | Pour in crushed tomatoes, remaining 1 tsp garam masala, and sugar, then simmer for 15 minutes until sauce thickens and oil separates at edges | Use an immersion blender to blend sauce until smooth and velvety (or transfer carefully to a blender) | Return blended sauce to pan, stir in heavy cream, and bring to a gentle simmer | Add cooked chicken pieces to the sauce and simmer together for 10 minutes until chicken is fully cooked and flavors meld | Season with salt to taste | Garnish with fresh chopped cilantro and serve hot with steamed basmati rice or warm naan bread

ingredients: 1 large head romaine lettuce (chopped), 2 boneless skinless chicken breasts, 1 cup croutons, 1/2 cup Parmesan cheese (freshly grated or shaved), 1/2 cup Caesar dressing, 2 tbsp olive oil, 1 tsp garlic powder, salt and black pepper, 1 lemon wedge, 2 anchovy fillets (optional, for dressing)
instructions: Season chicken breasts with olive oil, garlic powder, salt, and pepper | Heat a grill pan or skillet over medium-high heat and cook chicken for 6-7 minutes per side until golden brown and internal temperature reaches 165?F (74?C) | Transfer chicken to a cutting board and let rest for 5 minutes, then slice into thin strips | Wash romaine lettuce thoroughly, spin dry, and chop into bite-size pieces | Place chopped lettuce in a large salad bowl | Pour Caesar dressing over lettuce and toss thoroughly until every leaf is evenly coated | Add most of the grated Parmesan and toss again | Top with croutons and arrange sliced chicken strips across the top | Sprinkle remaining Parmesan over the salad | Squeeze fresh lemon juice over the top for brightness | Serve immediately on chilled plates

ingredients: 4 salmon fillets (150g each, skin-on), 1/3 cup soy sauce, 3 tbsp mirin, 2 tbsp sugar, 1 tbsp honey, 1 tbsp grated fresh ginger, 3 cloves garlic (minced), 1 tbsp sesame oil, 1 tbsp vegetable oil, 1 tbsp sesame seeds (toasted), 2 green onions (thinly sliced), steamed white rice for serving
instructions: In a small bowl, whisk together soy sauce, mirin, sugar, honey, grated ginger, and minced garlic until sugar dissolves to make teriyaki sauce | Place salmon fillets in a shallow dish and pour half the sauce over them, reserving the other half | Marinate salmon in the refrigerator for 30 minutes, turning once ? do not marinate longer or the fish will become too salty | Heat vegetable oil in a non-stick skillet over medium-high heat | Remove salmon from marinade, letting excess drip off, and pat skin dry with paper towel | Sear salmon skin-side down for 4 minutes until skin is crispy and golden | Carefully flip and cook the other side for 2-3 minutes until salmon is just cooked through but still moist in the center | Transfer salmon to a plate and pour the reserved unused sauce into the hot pan | Simmer sauce for 2-3 minutes until it reduces and thickens to a glossy glaze | Return salmon to pan briefly and spoon glaze over the top | Sprinkle with toasted sesame seeds and sliced green onions | Serve immediately over a bed of steamed white rice

ingredients: 1 head broccoli (cut into florets), 1 red bell pepper (sliced into strips), 1 yellow bell pepper (sliced into strips), 2 medium carrots (julienned), 200g firm tofu (pressed and cubed), 3 tbsp soy sauce, 1 tbsp oyster sauce (optional), 1 tbsp cornstarch mixed with 2 tbsp water, 3 cloves garlic (minced), 1 tbsp grated ginger, 2 tbsp vegetable oil, 1 tsp sesame oil, 1 tbsp sesame seeds, steamed jasmine rice for serving
instructions: Press tofu for 20 minutes by wrapping in paper towels and placing a heavy object on top, then cut into 1-inch cubes | Heat 1 tbsp vegetable oil in a wok over high heat until shimmering | Stir-fry tofu cubes for 4-5 minutes until golden and crispy on all sides, then remove and set aside | Add remaining oil to the wok | Add julienned carrots first (they take longest) and stir-fry for 2 minutes | Add broccoli florets and stir-fry for another 2 minutes | Add bell pepper strips, minced garlic, and grated ginger, tossing constantly for 1-2 minutes until vegetables are tender-crisp | In a small bowl, mix soy sauce, oyster sauce, and cornstarch slurry | Return tofu to the wok, pour sauce over everything, and toss for 1 minute until sauce thickens and coats all ingredients evenly | Remove from heat and drizzle with sesame oil | Sprinkle sesame seeds on top | Serve immediately over steamed jasmine rice

ingredients: 600g beef sirloin or tenderloin (cut into thin strips), 300g cremini mushrooms (sliced), 1 large onion (thinly sliced), 3 cloves garlic (minced), 2 tbsp butter, 1 tbsp vegetable oil, 1 tbsp all-purpose flour, 1 cup beef broth, 1 tbsp Dijon mustard, 1 cup sour cream, 1 tsp paprika, salt and black pepper to taste, 400g egg noodles or pasta, fresh parsley (chopped) for garnish
instructions: Pat beef strips completely dry with paper towels and season generously with salt and pepper | Heat 1 tbsp butter and vegetable oil in a large skillet over high heat | Sear beef strips in a single layer (in batches to avoid crowding) for 1 minute per side until browned ? do not overcook | Remove beef and set aside on a plate | In the same pan, reduce heat to medium and add remaining butter | Saut? sliced mushrooms for 5 minutes until they release their liquid and turn golden | Add sliced onion and cook for 4-5 minutes until softened | Stir in minced garlic and paprika, cooking for 30 seconds | Sprinkle flour over the mushroom mixture and stir for 1 minute to cook out the raw flour taste | Gradually pour in beef broth while stirring constantly to create a smooth sauce | Stir in Dijon mustard and bring to a simmer, cooking for 3-4 minutes until sauce thickens slightly | Reduce heat to low and stir in sour cream until fully incorporated ? do not let it boil or it may curdle | Return beef strips (and any accumulated juices) to the pan and simmer gently for 2-3 minutes just to reheat | Meanwhile, cook egg noodles in salted boiling water according to package directions and drain | Season stroganoff with salt and pepper to taste | Serve beef mixture over hot buttered egg noodles and garnish with chopped fresh parsley

ingredients: 1 can (400g) black beans (drained and rinsed), 1 cup rolled oats, 1/2 small red onion (finely diced), 2 cloves garlic (minced), 1 tsp ground cumin, 1 tsp smoked paprika, 1/2 tsp chili powder, 1 tbsp soy sauce, 1 tbsp tomato paste, 1 large egg (or flax egg for vegan), salt and black pepper, 2 tbsp vegetable oil, 4 burger buns, 4 slices cheddar cheese (optional), lettuce leaves, sliced tomato, sliced red onion, pickles, ketchup and mustard for serving
instructions: Drain and rinse black beans thoroughly, then spread on paper towels to dry slightly | In a large bowl, mash black beans with a fork or potato masher until mostly broken down but still with some chunky texture | Add rolled oats, finely diced red onion, minced garlic, cumin, smoked paprika, chili powder, soy sauce, tomato paste, and egg | Season with salt and pepper and mix thoroughly with your hands until mixture holds together when pressed | Divide mixture into 4 equal portions and shape into patties about 1/2-inch thick | Place patties on a parchment-lined plate, cover, and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes to firm up | Heat vegetable oil in a non-stick skillet over medium heat | Cook patties for 5 minutes per side until a dark crust forms and burgers are heated through | In the last minute, top each patty with a slice of cheese if using, cover to melt | While patties cook, slice burger buns in half and toast in a dry pan or under a broiler until golden | Assemble burgers: spread ketchup and mustard on bottom bun, add lettuce, tomato slice, bean patty, sliced red onion, and pickles | Close with top bun and serve immediately with fries or a side salad

ingredients: 2 tbsp olive oil, 1 medium onion (diced), 1 red bell pepper (diced), 3 cloves garlic (minced), 1 can (400g) crushed tomatoes, 2 tsp ground cumin, 1 tsp smoked paprika, 1/2 tsp chili flakes (optional), 1 tsp sugar, 4-6 large eggs, salt and black pepper, 1/2 cup crumbled feta cheese (optional), fresh cilantro or parsley (chopped), crusty bread for dipping
instructions: Heat olive oil in a large deep skillet or cast-iron pan over medium heat | Saut? diced onion for 5 minutes until softened | Add diced red bell pepper and cook for another 5 minutes until peppers are soft | Stir in minced garlic, cumin, smoked paprika, and chili flakes, cooking for 1 minute until fragrant | Pour in crushed tomatoes, add sugar, and season with salt and pepper | Stir well and bring to a gentle simmer | Reduce heat to low and cook sauce for 15-20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until it thickens to a chunky consistency | Using the back of a spoon, make 4-6 small wells in the sauce evenly spaced across the pan | Carefully crack one egg into each well, keeping yolks intact | Cover the pan with a lid and cook for 6-8 minutes until egg whites are set but yolks remain runny ? adjust time for firmer yolks if preferred | Remove from heat, sprinkle crumbled feta over the top (if using), and garnish with fresh chopped cilantro or parsley | Serve immediately straight from the pan with warm crusty bread for dipping into the sauce and yolks

ingredients: 4 large ripe tomatoes, 400g fresh mozzarella cheese, 1 bunch fresh basil leaves (about 20 leaves), 3 tbsp extra virgin olive oil, 1 tbsp aged balsamic vinegar, 1/2 tsp flaky sea salt (Maldon preferred), 1/4 tsp freshly ground black pepper
instructions: Select tomatoes and mozzarella that are roughly the same diameter for even layering | Slice tomatoes into 1/4-inch thick rounds using a sharp serrated knife to avoid crushing | Slice fresh mozzarella into rounds of the same thickness as the tomatoes | On a large serving plate or individual plates, arrange tomato and mozzarella slices in alternating overlapping rows or a circular pattern | Tuck whole fresh basil leaves between tomato and mozzarella slices throughout the arrangement | Drizzle extra virgin olive oil evenly over the entire salad, making sure each slice gets some | Drizzle aged balsamic vinegar in thin ribbons over the top ? a little goes a long way | Sprinkle generously with flaky sea salt and freshly ground black pepper | Let the salad sit at room temperature for 10-15 minutes before serving to allow flavors to meld | Serve as a starter or light meal ? do not refrigerate as tomatoes lose flavor when cold

ingredients: 4 portions fresh or dried ramen noodles, 2 liters rich pork broth (tonkotsu), 4 soft-boiled eggs, 300g pork belly or chashu (braised and sliced), 4 green onions (thinly sliced), 4 sheets nori seaweed, 2 tbsp soy sauce, 1 tbsp miso paste (white or red), 1 tbsp sesame oil, 2 cloves garlic (minced), 1 tsp grated ginger, 1 cup corn kernels (optional), 1 cup bean sprouts (optional), shichimi togarashi (Japanese chili powder) for serving
instructions: Prepare soft-boiled eggs: bring water to a boil, gently lower eggs in, and cook for exactly 6? minutes, then transfer to ice water, peel, and halve | Slice pre-braised pork belly into 1/4-inch thick rounds and gently warm in a separate pan or in the broth | In a large pot, heat sesame oil over medium heat and briefly saut? minced garlic and grated ginger for 30 seconds | Pour in pork broth, add soy sauce and miso paste, and whisk until miso dissolves completely | Bring broth to a gentle simmer and keep hot, but do not boil vigorously | Bring a separate pot of water to a boil and cook ramen noodles according to package directions ? fresh noodles usually take 2-3 minutes | Drain noodles thoroughly and divide among 4 large deep ramen bowls | Ladle the steaming hot broth over noodles | Arrange 2 soft-boiled egg halves, several slices of pork, green onions, corn, and bean sprouts neatly on top of each bowl | Tuck a sheet of nori halfway into the broth on one side | Sprinkle with shichimi togarashi for heat if desired | Serve immediately ? ramen waits for no one, eat while piping hot

ingredients: 500g fresh white fish fillets (sea bass, tilapia, or snapper, sushi-grade), 1 cup fresh lime juice (about 8-10 limes), 1 small red onion (very thinly sliced), 1-2 fresh chili peppers (serrano or jalape?o, finely chopped), 1 large tomato (seeded and diced), 1/2 cup fresh cilantro (chopped), 1 clove garlic (minced), 1 tsp salt, 1/2 tsp black pepper, 1 avocado (diced, added just before serving), tortilla chips or tostadas for serving
instructions: Inspect fish for any remaining bones or skin and remove, then cut into small uniform cubes about 1/2-inch in size | Place fish cubes in a non-reactive glass or ceramic bowl ? avoid metal as it reacts with lime juice | Pour fresh lime juice over fish, ensuring all pieces are submerged | Cover and refrigerate for 25-35 minutes, stirring once halfway through ? fish is 'cooked' when it turns opaque and firm | While fish marinates, rinse sliced red onion under cold water for 1 minute to reduce sharpness, then drain well | Drain most of the lime juice from the fish, leaving just a small amount to keep it moist | Add sliced red onion, chopped chili peppers, diced tomato, minced garlic, and chopped cilantro to the fish | Season with salt and black pepper and toss gently to combine | Refrigerate for another 10 minutes to let flavors come together | Just before serving, gently fold in diced avocado to keep it intact | Serve immediately in chilled glasses or bowls with tortilla chips or crispy tostadas on the side

ingredients: 2 cups cooked short-grain white rice, 200g beef sirloin (thinly sliced), 2 cups fresh spinach, 2 medium carrots (julienned), 1 zucchini (julienned), 4 large eggs, 4 tbsp gochujang (Korean chili paste), 2 tbsp soy sauce, 1 tbsp sesame oil, 2 tsp sugar, 3 cloves garlic (minced), 1 tbsp vegetable oil, 1 tbsp toasted sesame seeds, 2 green onions (sliced), kimchi for serving (optional)
instructions: Cook short-grain rice in a rice cooker or pot and keep warm | Marinate thinly sliced beef in soy sauce, 1 tsp sesame oil, sugar, and half the minced garlic for 15 minutes | Blanch spinach in boiling water for 30 seconds, drain, rinse with cold water, squeeze out excess moisture, and season with a drop of sesame oil and salt | Heat a pan and saut? julienned carrots with a pinch of salt for 2 minutes until slightly softened, then set aside | Saut? julienned zucchini similarly for 2 minutes and set aside | Heat vegetable oil in the same pan over high heat and stir-fry marinated beef for 2-3 minutes until cooked through and slightly caramelized | Fry eggs sunny-side up in a non-stick pan until whites are set but yolks remain runny | Place a generous mound of warm rice in the center of each serving bowl | Arrange beef, spinach, carrots, and zucchini in neat sections around the rice, creating a colorful wheel | Place a fried egg right in the center on top of the rice | Sprinkle toasted sesame seeds and sliced green onions over everything | Serve with a generous dollop of gochujang on the side ? each person mixes everything together vigorously before eating | Add kimchi on the side if desired

ingredients: 600g boneless skinless chicken thighs, 1 cup plain Greek yogurt, 4 cloves garlic (minced), 2 tbsp olive oil, 1 tbsp lemon juice, 1 tsp ground cumin, 1 tsp smoked paprika, 1/2 tsp turmeric, 1/2 tsp cinnamon, 1/2 tsp salt, 1/4 tsp black pepper, 4 large pita breads, 1 cucumber (diced), 2 tomatoes (diced), 1/2 red onion (thinly sliced), 1/2 cup tahini sauce or garlic yogurt sauce, pickled turnips (optional), fresh parsley (chopped)
instructions: In a large bowl, combine Greek yogurt, minced garlic, olive oil, lemon juice, cumin, paprika, turmeric, cinnamon, salt, and pepper to make the marinade | Add chicken thighs and coat thoroughly, then cover and refrigerate for at least 2 hours, preferably overnight for maximum flavor | Preheat oven to 425?F (220?C) or prepare a grill to medium-high heat | Remove chicken from marinade, letting excess drip off, and place on a lined baking sheet or hot grill | Cook for 22-25 minutes (turning halfway) until chicken is charred at the edges and fully cooked through | Transfer cooked chicken to a cutting board and let rest for 5 minutes, then slice into thin strips against the grain | Warm pita breads in a dry pan, oven, or directly over a gas flame for 30 seconds per side until soft and pliable | Spread a generous layer of tahini sauce or garlic yogurt sauce over each pita | Pile sliced chicken down the center | Top with diced cucumber, diced tomatoes, sliced red onion, and pickled turnips if using | Sprinkle with fresh parsley, fold or roll the pita tightly, and serve immediately

ingredients: 400g elbow macaroni, 3 tbsp unsalted butter, 3 tbsp all-purpose flour, 3 cups whole milk (warmed), 3 cups sharp cheddar cheese (freshly grated), 1 cup Gruy?re cheese (grated), 1/2 cup Parmesan cheese (grated), 1 tsp mustard powder, 1/2 tsp garlic powder, 1/2 tsp salt, 1/4 tsp black pepper, pinch of cayenne pepper, 1/2 cup panko breadcrumbs (optional), 1 tbsp melted butter (for topping)
instructions: Preheat oven to 375?F (190?C) and butter a 9x13 inch baking dish | Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil and cook macaroni until just al dente ? about 1 minute less than package instructions ? then drain and set aside | In the same pot over medium heat, melt 3 tbsp butter | Whisk in flour and cook for 1-2 minutes, stirring constantly, until the roux turns light golden and smells nutty | Gradually pour in warm milk while whisking continuously to prevent lumps | Bring sauce to a gentle simmer and cook for 3-4 minutes, whisking often, until thick enough to coat the back of a spoon | Remove from heat and stir in mustard powder, garlic powder, salt, pepper, and cayenne | Add grated cheddar, Gruy?re, and Parmesan in handfuls, stirring until each addition melts completely before adding more ? the sauce should be silky smooth | Fold cooked macaroni into the cheese sauce until every noodle is evenly coated | Pour mac and cheese into the prepared baking dish and spread evenly | If using, mix panko breadcrumbs with melted butter and sprinkle over the top | Bake for 20-25 minutes until bubbly around the edges and golden brown on top | Let rest for 5 minutes before serving ? this helps the sauce set slightly

ingredients: 500g ground beef (80/20), 1 packet taco seasoning (or 2 tbsp homemade blend), 2 cups cooked Mexican rice or white rice, 1 can (400g) black beans (drained and rinsed), 4 large flour tortillas (10-inch), 1 1/2 cups shredded cheddar or Monterey Jack cheese, 1 cup salsa (red or pico de gallo), 1/2 cup sour cream, 1 avocado (sliced), 1/4 cup fresh cilantro (chopped), 1 lime (cut into wedges), hot sauce to taste
instructions: Heat a skillet over medium-high heat and brown ground beef, breaking it apart, for 6-7 minutes until fully cooked | Drain excess fat from the skillet | Sprinkle taco seasoning over the beef, add 1/3 cup water, stir, and simmer for 3-4 minutes until sauce thickens | Warm black beans in a small pot and season with a pinch of salt and cumin | Heat a large dry skillet over medium heat and warm each tortilla for 20-30 seconds per side until soft and pliable | Lay a warm tortilla flat on a clean surface | Spread a scoop of Mexican rice in a rectangle down the center, leaving a 2-inch border at top and bottom | Add a layer of black beans on top of the rice | Spoon seasoned beef over the beans | Sprinkle generously with shredded cheese so it melts from the heat of the other ingredients | Add a spoonful of salsa and a few slices of avocado | Fold the left and right sides of the tortilla inward over the filling | While holding the sides, fold the bottom edge up and over the filling, then roll forward tightly into a compact cylinder | Repeat with remaining tortillas | Serve burritos with sour cream, extra salsa, lime wedges, and hot sauce on the side

ingredients: 8 rice paper wrappers (22cm), 100g dried rice vermicelli noodles, 1 cup shredded green cabbage, 1 large carrot (julienned), 1 cucumber (julienned), 1/2 red bell pepper (thinly sliced), 1 cup fresh cilantro leaves, 1/2 cup fresh mint leaves, 1/2 cup fresh Thai basil leaves, 12 cooked shrimp (halved lengthwise, optional), 1/4 cup soy sauce, 2 tbsp rice vinegar, 1 tsp sesame oil, 1 tsp sugar, 1 tsp chili garlic sauce (for dipping)
instructions: Cook rice vermicelli noodles according to package directions, drain, rinse with cold water, and set aside | Prepare all vegetables: shred cabbage, julienne carrot and cucumber, thinly slice bell pepper, and wash all herbs | Make dipping sauce by whisking together soy sauce, rice vinegar, sesame oil, sugar, and chili garlic sauce in a small bowl | Fill a large shallow bowl or pie dish with warm water | Working one at a time, dip a rice paper wrapper into warm water for 5-10 seconds until it becomes soft and pliable ? it will continue softening as you work | Place softened wrapper flat on a clean damp kitchen towel or cutting board | Lay a small handful of lettuce or cabbage near the bottom third of the wrapper, leaving 2 inches on each side | Top with a small bundle of rice noodles, followed by carrots, cucumber, bell pepper, cilantro, mint, and basil | If using shrimp, place 2-3 halves (orange side down) on top of the herbs ? they'll show through the transparent wrapper and look beautiful | Fold the bottom edge of the wrapper up over the filling, then fold both sides inward | Roll tightly upward into a neat cylinder, keeping even pressure | Repeat with remaining wrappers and fillings | Serve immediately with dipping sauce on the side ? do not refrigerate or wrappers will harden

ingredients: 4 large bell peppers (any color), 250g ground beef, 1 cup cooked white rice, 1 can (400g) diced tomatoes (drained), 1 small onion (diced), 3 cloves garlic (minced), 1 tsp dried oregano, 1 tsp ground cumin, 1 tsp salt, 1/2 tsp black pepper, 1 cup shredded mozzarella or cheddar cheese, 2 tbsp olive oil, 2 tbsp tomato paste, fresh parsley for garnish
instructions: Preheat oven to 375?F (190?C) and lightly grease a baking dish | Cut bell peppers in half lengthwise through the stem, remove seeds and white membranes, leaving stem intact for structure if desired | Bring a large pot of water to a boil and blanch pepper halves for 3 minutes, then drain and set aside cut-side down on paper towels | Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat and saut? diced onion for 5 minutes until softened | Add minced garlic and cook for 1 more minute | Add ground beef and cook, breaking apart, until browned all over, about 6-7 minutes | Drain excess fat from the pan | Stir in drained diced tomatoes, tomato paste, cooked rice, oregano, cumin, salt, and pepper | Simmer mixture for 5 minutes until heated through and well combined | Arrange blanched pepper halves cut-side up in the prepared baking dish | Spoon the beef and rice mixture generously into each pepper half, pressing down gently and mounding on top | Sprinkle shredded cheese evenly over each stuffed pepper | Pour 1/4 cup water into the bottom of the baking dish (not over peppers) to create steam | Cover dish loosely with foil and bake for 25 minutes | Remove foil and bake for another 10 minutes until cheese is melted, bubbly, and golden | Garnish with fresh parsley and serve hot

ingredients: 4 cups dashi broth (or water with dashi granules), 3 tbsp miso paste (white or awase), 150g soft or silken tofu (cut into small cubes), 2 tbsp dried wakame seaweed, 3 green onions (thinly sliced), 1 tsp soy sauce (optional)
instructions: Prepare dashi broth: either make from scratch with kombu and bonito flakes, or dissolve 1 tsp dashi granules in 4 cups of water and bring to a gentle simmer | Cut tofu into small 1/2-inch cubes by slicing horizontally first, then vertically into even pieces | Add cubed tofu to the simmering broth | Add dried wakame seaweed ? it will expand significantly, so a small amount goes a long way | Let soup simmer gently for 2-3 minutes until tofu is heated through and seaweed has rehydrated | Reduce heat to low ? the broth should be steaming but not bubbling | Place miso paste in a small bowl and ladle some hot broth over it | Whisk the miso and broth together until the paste dissolves completely into a smooth liquid | Pour the dissolved miso mixture back into the pot and stir gently | Taste and add a small splash of soy sauce if needed for depth | Heat for just 1 more minute without letting the soup boil ? boiling destroys miso's delicate flavor and beneficial probiotics | Ladle into serving bowls and top generously with sliced green onions | Serve immediately as a starter or alongside a larger Japanese meal

ingredients: 4 boneless skinless chicken breasts (about 600g total), 1 cup all-purpose flour, 2 large eggs (beaten), 1 1/2 cups Italian-style breadcrumbs, 1/2 cup Parmesan cheese (grated, plus extra for topping), 1 tsp garlic powder, 1 tsp dried oregano, 1/2 tsp salt, 1/4 tsp black pepper, 1 cup vegetable oil (for frying), 2 cups tomato sauce (homemade or good-quality jarred), 250g fresh mozzarella cheese (sliced), 400g spaghetti, fresh basil leaves for garnish
instructions: Preheat oven to 425?F (220?C) | Butterfly chicken breasts or pound them between two sheets of plastic wrap to an even 1/2-inch thickness ? uniform thickness ensures even cooking | Set up breading station: place flour in first shallow bowl, beaten eggs in second, and a mixture of breadcrumbs, grated Parmesan, garlic powder, oregano, salt, and pepper in third | Dredge each chicken cutlet in flour, shaking off excess | Dip floured chicken into beaten eggs, letting excess drip off | Press chicken into breadcrumb mixture, coating both sides thoroughly and patting crumbs on to adhere | Heat vegetable oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat until shimmering (about 350?F / 175?C) | Fry breaded chicken cutlets for 3-4 minutes per side until golden brown and crispy ? do not crowd the pan, cook in batches if needed | Transfer fried cutlets to a paper towel-lined plate briefly to drain excess oil | Spread 1/2 cup of tomato sauce on the bottom of a baking dish | Place fried chicken cutlets on top of the sauce | Spoon more tomato sauce over each cutlet, leaving edges visible for crispiness | Top each cutlet with slices of fresh mozzarella and a sprinkle of grated Parmesan | Bake for 12-15 minutes until cheese is melted, bubbly, and beginning to brown | Meanwhile, cook spaghetti in salted boiling water until al dente, drain, and toss with remaining hot tomato sauce | Serve chicken Parmesan on a bed of sauced spaghetti, garnished with fresh torn basil

ingredients: 400g fresh egg noodles (or dried), 3 large eggs, 3 tbsp soy sauce, 1 tbsp dark soy sauce, 1 tbsp oyster sauce, 1 tsp sesame oil, 3 tbsp vegetable oil, 4 cloves garlic (minced), 1 cup frozen peas, 1 medium carrot (julienned), 3 green onions (cut into 2-inch pieces), 1/2 tsp white pepper, bean sprouts for garnish (optional)
instructions: Bring a pot of water to a boil and cook egg noodles according to package directions until just al dente, then drain and rinse briefly with cold water to stop cooking ? toss with a small drizzle of oil to prevent sticking | In a small bowl, mix together soy sauce, dark soy sauce, oyster sauce, and sesame oil to make the sauce | Beat eggs with a pinch of salt | Heat 1 tbsp vegetable oil in a wok over high heat until shimmering | Pour in beaten eggs and scramble quickly, breaking into small pieces, then remove and set aside | Add remaining 2 tbsp oil to the wok and heat until smoking | Add minced garlic and stir-fry for 15 seconds until fragrant | Add julienned carrots and frozen peas, stir-frying for 1-2 minutes | Add cooked noodles to the wok, spreading them out and letting them sear for 30 seconds before tossing | Pour sauce mixture over noodles and use tongs or chopsticks to toss everything together, ensuring even coating | Add white pepper and continue tossing for 2 minutes until noodles are heated through and slightly charred at the edges | Return scrambled eggs to the wok and toss to distribute | Add green onion pieces and toss for 30 more seconds | Serve immediately on plates or in bowls, topped with fresh bean sprouts if desired

ingredients: 1 kg pumpkin (peeled, seeded, and cubed), 1 medium onion (diced), 3 cloves garlic (minced), 2 tbsp butter, 4 cups vegetable or chicken broth, 1/2 cup heavy cream, 1/2 tsp ground nutmeg, 1/2 tsp ground cinnamon, salt and white pepper to taste, 2 tbsp pumpkin seeds (toasted), fresh chives (chopped), crusty bread for serving
instructions: Peel pumpkin, cut in half, scoop out seeds, and chop flesh into 1-inch cubes | In a large heavy-bottomed pot, melt butter over medium heat | Saut? diced onion for 5-6 minutes until soft and translucent | Add minced garlic and cook for 1 minute until fragrant | Add pumpkin cubes to the pot and stir to coat with butter, cooking for 5 minutes to lightly caramelize the edges | Season with nutmeg, cinnamon, salt, and white pepper | Pour in broth, ensuring pumpkin is just covered ? add a splash more if needed | Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 25-30 minutes until pumpkin is very tender and falls apart when pierced with a fork | Remove pot from heat and let cool slightly for 5 minutes | Using an immersion blender, pur?e soup directly in the pot until completely smooth and velvety ? alternatively, carefully blend in batches in a countertop blender | Return pur?ed soup to low heat and stir in heavy cream, heating gently without boiling | Taste and adjust seasoning with more salt, pepper, or spice as needed | While soup heats, toast pumpkin seeds in a dry pan over medium heat for 2-3 minutes until they pop and turn golden | Ladle soup into bowls, swirl a drizzle of cream on top, and garnish with toasted pumpkin seeds and chopped chives | Serve piping hot with thick slices of crusty bread for dipping

ingredients: 4 medium potatoes (boiled and mashed), 1 cup green peas (cooked), 2 medium tomatoes (finely diced), 1 large onion (finely diced), 1 green bell pepper (finely diced), 2 tbsp pav bhaji masala, 1 tsp red chili powder, 1/2 tsp turmeric, 3 tbsp butter (plus extra for serving), 1 tbsp vegetable oil, 1 tsp ginger-garlic paste, salt to taste, juice of 1/2 lemon, 8 pav buns (soft dinner rolls), fresh cilantro (chopped), 1 small red onion (finely diced, for garnish), lemon wedges
instructions: Boil potatoes until fork-tender, then peel and mash coarsely ? some small chunks are fine for texture | Cook green peas in boiling water for 3 minutes until tender, then drain | Heat 2 tbsp butter and vegetable oil in a large flat skillet or tawa over medium heat | Saut? diced onion for 5 minutes until golden brown | Add ginger-garlic paste and cook for 1 minute until raw smell disappears | Add diced bell pepper and cook for 3 minutes until slightly softened | Add finely diced tomatoes and cook until they break down and become mushy, about 5 minutes | Stir in pav bhaji masala, chili powder, and turmeric, cooking for 1 minute to bloom spices | Add boiled peas and use a potato masher to mash everything directly in the pan | Add mashed potatoes and 1/2 cup water, mashing and mixing until everything is well combined | Simmer bhaji for 10-12 minutes, stirring occasionally, until thick and the butter separates at the edges | Season with salt and squeeze in lemon juice, mixing well | Slice pav buns horizontally, keeping one edge attached | Heat a griddle or pan, spread butter generously, and toast each pav on both sides until golden and crisp | Serve hot bhaji in a bowl topped with a pat of butter, diced raw onion, chopped cilantro, and a lemon wedge, with butter-toasted pav on the side

ingredients: 600g beef sirloin or ribeye (very thinly sliced), 1/2 cup soy sauce, 1/4 cup sugar, 2 tbsp honey, 3 tbsp sesame oil, 6 cloves garlic (minced), 1 tbsp grated ginger, 1/2 small Asian pear or apple (grated, for tenderizing), 3 green onions (sliced), 1 tbsp toasted sesame seeds, 1/2 tsp black pepper, 1 tbsp vegetable oil, butter lettuce leaves for wraps, cooked white rice, ssamjang (Korean dipping paste), sliced raw garlic, sliced green chili peppers
instructions: Place beef in the freezer for 1-2 hours until partially frozen ? this makes slicing paper-thin much easier | Slice beef against the grain into very thin sheets, about 1/8-inch thick | In a bowl, whisk together soy sauce, sugar, honey, sesame oil, minced garlic, grated ginger, grated Asian pear (this natural tenderizer is key), black pepper, and sliced green onions | Pour marinade over beef slices and massage gently with your hands to coat every piece | Cover and refrigerate for at least 2 hours, preferably overnight | When ready to cook, remove beef from refrigerator and let it come to room temperature for 20 minutes | Heat a large cast-iron pan or grill pan over high heat until smoking hot | Add vegetable oil and swirl to coat | Cook beef in a single layer in batches ? do not overcrowd the pan or the beef will steam rather than char | Cook each batch for just 1-2 minutes per side until caramelized and dark at the edges | Transfer cooked beef to a plate and sprinkle with toasted sesame seeds | Serve immediately with steamed rice, crisp lettuce leaves for wrapping, ssamjang dipping paste, sliced raw garlic, and green chili peppers | To eat: place a lettuce leaf in palm, add rice, bulgogi, a dab of ssamjang, and any desired garnishes, then wrap and eat in one bite

ingredients: 1 kg chicken legs and thighs (skin removed, scored deeply), 1 cup thick plain yogurt, 3 tbsp tandoori masala, 1 tbsp Kashmiri red chili powder (for color), 1 tsp turmeric, 1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste, 2 tbsp lemon juice, 2 tbsp mustard oil (or vegetable oil), 1 tsp salt, 1 tsp garam masala, 1 large red onion (sliced into rings), lemon wedges, fresh cilantro, naan bread for serving
instructions: Pat chicken pieces completely dry with paper towels | Using a sharp knife, make 3-4 deep diagonal slashes on each chicken piece ? this allows marinade to penetrate and helps even cooking | In a large bowl, combine yogurt, tandoori masala, Kashmiri chili powder, turmeric, ginger-garlic paste, lemon juice, mustard oil, and salt to make the marinade | Add chicken pieces and massage marinade deeply into every slash and crevice | Cover and refrigerate for at least 4 hours, but preferably overnight for the deepest flavor and color | When ready to cook, preheat oven to its maximum setting (450?F / 230?C) with a rack in the upper third | Line a baking sheet with foil and place a wire rack on top ? this allows air to circulate | Arrange chicken pieces on the rack, spaced apart | Roast for 25-30 minutes, flipping halfway through, until chicken is charred in spots and internal temperature reaches 165?F (74?C) | For extra char, switch to broil for the final 3-4 minutes, watching closely | Sprinkle garam masala over hot chicken as it comes out of the oven | Let rest for 5 minutes, then garnish with onion rings, cilantro, and lemon wedges | Serve sizzling hot with naan bread, mint chutney, and sliced onions

ingredients: 500g large shrimp (peeled and deveined, shells reserved), 4 cups shrimp or chicken broth, 2 stalks lemongrass (bruised and cut into 3-inch pieces), 4 kaffir lime leaves (torn), 3-4 Thai bird's eye chilies (crushed), 200g straw mushrooms or button mushrooms (halved), 2 medium tomatoes (quartered), 1 tbsp nam prik pao (Thai chili paste), 2 tbsp fish sauce, 3 tbsp fresh lime juice, 1 tsp sugar, 1/4 cup fresh cilantro (chopped), 1 small knob galangal (sliced, optional)
instructions: In a pot, simmer reserved shrimp shells in 4 cups of water for 15 minutes to make a quick shrimp stock, then strain and discard shells ? or use pre-made broth | Bring broth to a gentle boil in a large pot | Bruise lemongrass stalks by smashing with the back of a knife, then cut into 3-inch pieces and add to broth | Tear kaffir lime leaves and add them along with sliced galangal if using | Add crushed bird's eye chilies ? adjust number based on your heat tolerance | Simmer for 5 minutes to infuse the broth with aromatic flavors | Add halved mushrooms and quartered tomatoes, cooking for 3 minutes until mushrooms soften | Add shrimp and cook for 2-3 minutes just until they turn pink and curl ? do not overcook | Remove pot from heat immediately | Stir in nam prik pao (chili paste), fish sauce, sugar, and fresh lime juice | Taste and balance flavors ? it should be sour, salty, spicy, and slightly sweet | Remove lemongrass stalks and lime leaves before serving (or leave them as garnish, but warn guests not to eat them) | Ladle into serving bowls and top with fresh chopped cilantro | Serve piping hot as a starter or with steamed jasmine rice as a main

ingredients: 4 slices thick-cut bacon (diced), 2 tbsp unsalted butter, 1 medium onion (diced), 3 celery stalks (diced), 3 tbsp all-purpose flour, 2 cups clam juice, 1 cup fish or chicken broth, 3 medium Yukon Gold potatoes (peeled and diced), 1 bay leaf, 1/2 tsp dried thyme, 2 cans (400g each) chopped clams (drained, juice reserved), 1 cup heavy cream, salt and white pepper to taste, oyster crackers for serving, fresh parsley (chopped)
instructions: In a large heavy-bottomed pot, cook diced bacon over medium heat until crispy and fat is rendered, about 6 minutes | Remove crispy bacon with a slotted spoon and set aside for garnish, leaving fat in pot | Add butter to bacon fat and melt | Saut? diced onion and celery for 6-7 minutes until softened but not browned | Sprinkle flour over vegetables and stir continuously for 2 minutes to cook out the raw flour taste | Gradually pour in clam juice and broth while whisking constantly to prevent lumps | Add diced potatoes, bay leaf, and thyme | Bring to a boil, then reduce heat, cover, and simmer for 15-18 minutes until potatoes are fork-tender | Add drained chopped clams and reserved clam juice to the pot | Stir in heavy cream and heat gently for 5 minutes ? do not let it boil or the clams will toughen and cream may curdle | Remove bay leaf and season with salt and white pepper (white pepper blends better visually than black) | Ladle into soup bowls and top with crispy bacon bits and chopped fresh parsley | Serve immediately with oyster crackers for crumbling on top

ingredients: 400g fettuccine pasta, 2 boneless skinless chicken breasts, 1 tsp Italian seasoning, salt and black pepper, 2 tbsp butter, 1 tbsp olive oil, 4 cloves garlic (minced), 2 cups heavy cream, 1 1/2 cups Parmesan cheese (freshly grated), 1/4 cup cream cheese (optional, for extra silkiness), 1/4 tsp nutmeg, fresh parsley (chopped)
instructions: Bring a large pot of heavily salted water to a boil and cook fettuccine until al dente | While pasta cooks, season chicken breasts on both sides with Italian seasoning, salt, and pepper | Heat olive oil and 1 tbsp butter in a large skillet over medium-high heat | Cook chicken breasts for 6-7 minutes per side until golden brown and internal temperature reaches 165?F (74?C) | Transfer chicken to a cutting board, let rest for 5 minutes, then slice into thin strips | Reserve 1 cup of pasta water before draining pasta | In the same skillet, reduce heat to medium and melt remaining 1 tbsp butter | Add minced garlic and saut? for 30 seconds until fragrant ? do not let it brown | Pour in heavy cream and bring to a gentle simmer, stirring frequently | Add cream cheese if using and whisk until melted and smooth | Reduce heat to low and gradually stir in grated Parmesan, nutmeg, salt, and pepper, whisking until sauce is smooth and thick | Drain pasta and add directly to the sauce, tossing with tongs to coat every strand | Add small splashes of reserved pasta water if the sauce becomes too thick | Add sliced chicken on top and toss again lightly | Plate pasta into bowls, top with chicken slices, and garnish with extra Parmesan and chopped parsley | Serve immediately while hot and creamy

ingredients: 1 1/2 cups Bomba or Arborio rice, 4 cups vegetable broth, 1/2 tsp saffron threads, 1 red bell pepper (sliced into strips), 1 yellow bell pepper (sliced into strips), 1 cup frozen peas, 1 can (400g) artichoke hearts (drained and halved), 1 medium onion (diced), 4 cloves garlic (minced), 2 medium tomatoes (grated), 1 tsp smoked paprika, 3 tbsp olive oil, salt to taste, lemon wedges, fresh parsley (chopped)
instructions: Warm vegetable broth in a saucepan and steep saffron threads in it for 5 minutes | Heat olive oil in a large paella pan or wide shallow skillet over medium heat | Saut? sliced bell peppers for 5 minutes until softened and slightly charred at edges, then remove and set aside | In the same pan, saut? diced onion for 5 minutes until translucent | Add minced garlic and cook for 1 minute | Stir in grated tomatoes and smoked paprika, cooking until tomato reduces and darkens, about 3 minutes | Add rice and stir to coat each grain with oil, toasting for 2 minutes | Pour saffron-infused broth evenly over rice and gently shake the pan to distribute ? do not stir from this point forward | Bring to a vigorous boil, then reduce heat to medium-low | Arrange artichoke halves evenly over the rice | Scatter peas over the top | Simmer for 18-20 minutes without stirring until rice is tender and liquid is absorbed | In the last 5 minutes, arrange reserved bell pepper strips on top | If rice isn't quite done but liquid is gone, add splashes of hot broth or water as needed | Increase heat to high for the final 2 minutes to create socarrat (crispy bottom) | Remove from heat, cover with a clean towel, and rest for 5 minutes | Garnish with parsley and lemon wedges, serve from the pan

ingredients: 4 large pita breads or flour tortilla wraps, 1 can (400g) chickpeas (drained and rinsed, liquid reserved), 1/3 cup tahini, 1/4 cup fresh lemon juice, 2 cloves garlic, 3 tbsp olive oil, 1/2 tsp ground cumin, salt to taste, 1 cucumber (thinly sliced), 2 tomatoes (diced), 2 cups mixed lettuce leaves, 1/4 red onion (thinly sliced), pickled turnips (optional)
instructions: Make hummus: blend chickpeas, tahini, lemon juice, garlic, 2 tbsp olive oil, cumin, and salt in a food processor until smooth | If too thick, add reserved chickpea liquid or cold water 1 tbsp at a time until desired creamy consistency | Taste and adjust lemon/salt as needed ? it should be bright and well-seasoned | Warm pita breads in a dry pan for 30 seconds per side until soft and pliable | Lay each pita flat and spread a generous layer of hummus down the center, about 3-4 tbsp per wrap | Layer cucumber slices evenly over the hummus | Add diced tomatoes and thinly sliced red onion | Top with a handful of lettuce leaves and pickled turnips if using | Drizzle with remaining olive oil | Fold the bottom edge up over the filling, then fold in both sides | Roll tightly upward into a compact wrap | Slice in half diagonally and serve immediately, or wrap in foil for a portable meal

ingredients: 400g linguine or spaghetti, 3 cups fresh basil leaves (packed, about 60g), 1/3 cup pine nuts (toasted), 3 cloves garlic, 1/2 cup extra virgin olive oil, 1/2 cup Parmesan cheese (freshly grated), 1/4 cup Pecorino Romano cheese (grated), salt to taste, 1 cup reserved pasta water, extra Parmesan for serving
instructions: Toast pine nuts in a dry pan over medium heat for 2-3 minutes until golden and fragrant, shaking frequently to avoid burning ? set aside to cool | Bring a large pot of generously salted water to a boil and cook pasta until al dente | While pasta cooks, combine basil leaves, toasted pine nuts, garlic cloves, and a pinch of salt in a food processor | Pulse until coarsely chopped | With the motor running, slowly drizzle in olive oil through the feed tube until the mixture becomes a smooth paste | Transfer pesto to a bowl and stir in grated Parmesan and Pecorino by hand ? this keeps the texture better than blending the cheese | Season pesto with salt to taste | Before draining pasta, reserve at least 1 cup of the starchy pasta water | Drain pasta (do not rinse) and return to the pot off the heat | Add pesto to the hot pasta and toss vigorously with tongs | Add reserved pasta water a splash at a time, tossing continuously, until the sauce becomes creamy and clings to each strand | Taste and adjust seasoning | Serve immediately in warm bowls with extra grated Parmesan on top ? never reheat pesto pasta as it will turn dull and oily

ingredients: For dough: 2 cups all-purpose flour, 1/4 cup vegetable oil or ghee, 1/2 tsp salt, 1/2 tsp carom seeds (ajwain), 1/2 cup water (approx). For filling: 4 medium potatoes (boiled and mashed), 1/2 cup green peas (cooked), 1 tbsp vegetable oil, 1 tsp cumin seeds, 1 tbsp grated ginger, 2 green chilies (finely chopped), 1 tsp garam masala, 1 tsp amchur (dry mango powder) or lemon juice, 1/2 tsp turmeric, 1 tsp coriander powder, salt to taste, oil for deep frying, mint chutney and tamarind chutney for serving
instructions: Make dough: combine flour, salt, carom seeds, and oil/ghee in a bowl, rub with fingers until mixture resembles breadcrumbs | Gradually add water and knead into a stiff, smooth dough ? it should be firmer than roti dough | Cover with a damp cloth and rest for 30 minutes | Prepare filling: heat 1 tbsp oil in a pan and crackle cumin seeds | Add grated ginger and chopped green chilies, saut? for 30 seconds | Add mashed potatoes, cooked peas, garam masala, amchur, turmeric, coriander powder, and salt | Mix thoroughly and cook for 3-4 minutes, then let filling cool completely | After dough has rested, knead briefly and divide into 8 equal balls | Roll each ball into an oval about 6 inches across, then cut in half to create two semi-circles | Take one semi-circle, fold the straight edge to form a cone, and seal the overlapping edge with a dab of water | Fill the cone with 1-2 tbsp of potato mixture, leaving space at the top | Dab water along the open edges and press firmly to seal ? ensure no gaps or oil will seep in during frying | Repeat with remaining dough and filling | Heat oil in a deep pan to 325?F (165?C) ? not too hot or samosas will brown before the inside cooks | Fry samosas in batches for 8-10 minutes, turning occasionally, until deep golden brown and crispy | Drain on paper towels and serve hot with mint chutney and sweet tamarind chutney

ingredients: 600g beef sirloin or tenderloin (cut into 1 1/2-inch cubes), 1 large onion (cut into chunks), 1 green bell pepper (cut into chunks), 1 red bell pepper (cut into chunks), 1/4 cup olive oil, 3 tbsp plain yogurt, 2 tbsp lemon juice, 4 cloves garlic (minced), 1 tsp ground cumin, 1 tsp smoked paprika, 1/2 tsp black pepper, 1/2 tsp dried oregano, salt, wooden or metal skewers, rice pilaf or flatbread for serving
instructions: If using wooden skewers, soak them in water for at least 30 minutes to prevent burning during grilling | Cut beef into uniform 1 1/2-inch cubes ? even sizing ensures even cooking | In a bowl, whisk together olive oil, yogurt, lemon juice, minced garlic, cumin, paprika, black pepper, oregano, and salt to make the marinade | Add beef cubes and toss to coat thoroughly, cover, and refrigerate for at least 2 hours or up to 8 hours | Cut onion and bell peppers into large chunks roughly the same size as the beef cubes | Remove beef from marinade, letting excess drip off | Thread beef cubes alternately with onion and bell pepper chunks onto skewers, packing ingredients snugly but not too tight | Preheat a grill, grill pan, or broiler to high heat | Grill kebabs for 10-12 minutes total, turning every 3 minutes, until beef is nicely charred on the outside but still tender inside ? it should be medium-rare to medium | Let kebabs rest on a plate for 5 minutes | Serve hot over rice pilaf or with warm flatbread, grilled vegetables, and a side of garlic yogurt sauce

ingredients: 3 ripe plantains (yellow with black spots ? not green, not fully black), 1/2 cup vegetable oil (for shallow frying), 1 tsp sea salt, pinch of cayenne pepper (optional)
instructions: Select ripe plantains that are yellow with plenty of black spots ? they should yield slightly when pressed but still hold their shape | Cut off both ends of each plantain, then score the skin lengthwise with a knife and peel it off ? ripe plantain skin comes off more easily than green | Slice plantains diagonally into 1/2-inch thick oval slices | Heat vegetable oil in a large skillet over medium heat until shimmering but not smoking ? oil should be about 1/4-inch deep | Carefully place plantain slices in the hot oil in a single layer, leaving space between them | Fry for 2-3 minutes per side until deep golden brown and caramelized ? ripe plantains have natural sugars that caramelize beautifully | Use a slotted spatula to transfer fried plantains to a plate lined with paper towels | While still hot, sprinkle with sea salt and optional cayenne pepper | Let excess oil drain for 1-2 minutes | Serve immediately as a side dish with rice and beans, stews, or on their own as a sweet-savory snack

ingredients: 1 1/2 cups glutinous (sticky) rice, 1 can (400ml) full-fat coconut milk, 1/2 cup granulated sugar, 1/2 tsp salt, 2 ripe mangoes (Ataulfo/honey mangoes preferred), 1 tbsp toasted sesame seeds or mung beans (for garnish), pandan leaves (optional)
instructions: Rinse sticky rice in cold water several times until water runs clear, then soak in plenty of water overnight or for at least 6 hours | Drain soaked rice and place in a steamer lined with cheesecloth or a banana leaf | Steam over boiling water for 25-30 minutes until rice is tender and translucent ? check halfway and sprinkle with water if needed | While rice steams, warm coconut milk in a saucepan over low heat ? do not let it boil | Stir in sugar and salt until fully dissolved | Set aside 1/4 cup of this sweetened coconut milk for the final drizzle | When rice is done, transfer hot rice to a bowl and pour the main amount of warm sweetened coconut milk over it | Gently fold rice and coconut milk together, then cover and let rest for 30 minutes ? the rice will absorb all the creamy liquid | Peel ripe mangoes and slice the flesh away from the pit, then cut into thin elegant slices | Mound a portion of sticky rice on each serving plate, shaping it neatly | Fan mango slices alongside the rice | Drizzle the reserved sweetened coconut milk over the top | Sprinkle with toasted sesame seeds or crispy mung beans for a crunchy contrast | Serve at room temperature ? do not refrigerate or the rice will harden

ingredients: 2 large flour tortillas (10-inch), 2 boneless skinless chicken breasts (about 300g), 1 1/2 cups shredded Mexican blend cheese or Monterey Jack, 1/2 bell pepper (sliced into thin strips), 1/2 onion (thinly sliced), 1 tsp chili powder, 1/2 tsp cumin, salt and pepper, 1 tbsp vegetable oil, salsa, sour cream, and guacamole for serving
instructions: Season chicken breasts with chili powder, cumin, salt, and pepper on both sides | Heat 1/2 tbsp oil in a skillet over medium-high heat and cook chicken for 6-7 minutes per side until golden and cooked through | Transfer to a cutting board, rest for 5 minutes, then dice into small cubes | In the same pan, add a bit more oil and saut? sliced onion and bell pepper for 4-5 minutes until softened and slightly charred | Wipe out the skillet and return to medium heat ? you'll use the same pan for the quesadilla | Place one tortilla flat in the dry pan | Sprinkle half the cheese evenly over the entire tortilla | On one half, layer diced chicken and saut?ed vegetables | Let cheese begin to melt for 1 minute, then fold the empty half over the filled half, creating a half-moon shape | Press down gently with a spatula | Cook for 2-3 minutes per side until the tortilla is golden brown, crispy, and the cheese inside is fully melted | Transfer to a cutting board and let rest for 1 minute before slicing into 3 wedges | Serve immediately with salsa, sour cream, and guacamole on the side

ingredients: 3 large eggs, 1 cup fresh spinach leaves, 1/4 cup shredded cheddar or Swiss cheese, 1 tbsp diced onion, 1 tbsp butter, salt and black pepper to taste, pinch of nutmeg (optional)
instructions: Crack eggs into a bowl, add salt, pepper, and a pinch of nutmeg if using, then beat thoroughly with a fork until yolks and whites are fully combined and slightly frothy | Heat a small non-stick skillet over medium heat and add half the butter | Saut? diced onion for 2 minutes until softened | Add fresh spinach leaves and cook for 1-2 minutes, stirring, until completely wilted ? spinach will reduce significantly | Remove spinach-onion mixture from the pan and set aside on a plate | Wipe the pan clean and return to medium heat | Add remaining butter and swirl to coat the entire pan surface | When butter is foaming, pour beaten eggs evenly into the pan | Let eggs cook undisturbed for 1 minute until the edges begin to set | Using a spatula, gently lift the edges and tilt the pan so uncooked egg flows underneath | When the surface is nearly set but still slightly glossy, spoon the spinach-onion mixture over one half of the omelette | Sprinkle shredded cheese evenly over the spinach | Fold the empty half over the filling using the spatula | Cook for 30 more seconds, then slide the omelette onto a plate | Serve immediately while hot and the cheese is melted

ingredients: 1 1/2 cups dry couscous, 1 1/2 cups boiling water or vegetable broth, 2 tbsp olive oil, 1 cucumber (diced), 2 medium tomatoes (diced), 1/2 red bell pepper (diced), 1/4 red onion (finely diced), 1/4 cup fresh parsley (chopped), 2 tbsp fresh mint (chopped), juice of 1 large lemon, 3 tbsp extra virgin olive oil, salt and black pepper to taste, 1/2 cup crumbled feta cheese (optional)
