ingredients: 1 kg winter squash (butternut or acorn, peeled and thinly sliced), 2 tbsp extra virgin olive oil (divided), 2 medium onions (thinly sliced), 4 cloves garlic (minced), 1 tsp dried sage, 1 tsp fresh thyme leaves, 1 tsp kosher salt, 1/2 tsp black pepper, 1/2 cup fresh parsley (chopped), 1 cup breadcrumbs (divided), 1 cup part-skim mozzarella cheese (shredded), 1/2 cup Parmesan cheese (grated)
instructions: Preheat oven to 350?F (175?C) | Lightly coat a 2-quart square baking dish with nonstick cooking spray and set aside | In a large skillet, heat 1 tablespoon of the olive oil over medium heat | Add sliced onions and minced garlic and cook about 6 minutes until tender, stirring occasionally | Remove from heat and stir in sage, thyme, kosher salt, and pepper | Place half of the squash slices in the prepared dish, overlapping slightly | Sprinkle evenly with the onion mixture and half of the breadcrumbs | Top with remaining squash slices | Cover dish with foil and bake for about 45 minutes until squash is nearly tender | Meanwhile, in a small bowl, combine the remaining breadcrumbs, remaining 1 tablespoon olive oil, and chopped parsley ? mix well and set aside | Remove foil from baking dish | Sprinkle squash with shredded mozzarella, grated Parmesan, and the breadcrumb-parsley mixture | Bake uncovered for 10 to 15 more minutes until crumbs are golden brown and squash is fully tender | Let stand for 10 minutes before serving ? this allows the gratin to set | Serve warm as a side dish

ingredients: 120ml chilled champagne or sparkling wine, 30ml Hpnotiq liqueur, fresh blueberries for garnish, lemon twist for garnish
instructions: Chill a champagne flute in the freezer for 5 minutes | Pour Hpnotiq liqueur into the chilled flute first ? its vibrant blue color creates the base of the drink | Slowly top with chilled champagne or sparkling wine, tilting the glass slightly to preserve the layering effect | Watch the bubbles rise through the blue liqueur for a beautiful visual effect | Garnish with a few fresh blueberries dropped into the glass and a lemon twist on the rim | Serve immediately while the champagne is still effervescent

ingredients: 1 cup water, 1/2 cup Arborio or short-grain white rice, 2 cups unsweetened rice milk (plus more for reheating), 1/3 cup maple syrup, 1/4 tsp salt, 1 tsp ground cinnamon (plus more for garnish), 1 tsp vanilla extract, 1/3 cup raisins, chopped nuts for topping (optional)
instructions: In a medium saucepan, bring water to a boil | Once boiling, add the rice, reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes until water is mostly absorbed | Add rice milk, maple syrup, salt, and cinnamon | Cover and bring back to just barely boiling, then remove the lid and simmer uncovered until thick and creamy, about 15-20 minutes, stirring once in a while to prevent sticking | The rice should be tender and the mixture should have a creamy, porridge-like consistency | Remove from heat and stir in vanilla extract and raisins | Pour into serving dishes | Sprinkle the top with a dusting of ground cinnamon | Let cool for 5 minutes, then serve warm | If planning to serve later, the pudding will thicken with time ? add a splash more rice milk when reheating to restore creaminess | Top with chopped nuts if desired for added texture

ingredients: 1 1/2 cups graham cracker crumbs, 1/4 cup powdered sugar, 6 tbsp unsalted butter (melted), 24 mini Hershey's chocolate bars, 12 large marshmallows (cut in half)
instructions: Preheat oven to 350?F (175?C) | In a bowl, mix crushed graham cracker crumbs, powdered sugar, and melted butter together until the texture resembles wet sand | Take a mini muffin tray and fill each cup less than halfway with the graham cracker mixture, pressing down firmly with your fingers or the back of a spoon to form a crust | Bake the crusts at 350?F for 4-5 minutes until they are set and slightly golden | Remove tray from oven and place one mini Hershey's chocolate bar on top of each warm crust | Top the chocolate with half a marshmallow (cut side down) | Return to oven and bake at 350?F for 2-4 minutes until marshmallows are puffed and golden ? watch closely as they can burn quickly | Remove from oven and let cool in the pan for 5 minutes | Carefully remove each bite and serve warm for gooey, melted s'more goodness

ingredients: 300g Cheshire cheese (crumbled), 100g unsalted butter (softened), 1/4 tsp ground mace, 1/4 tsp ground allspice, 3 tbsp sweet sherry, 1 tbsp Madeira wine, 60g melted butter (for sealing)
instructions: In a mixing bowl, combine crumbled Cheshire cheese with softened butter and spices (mace and allspice) | Adjust the amount of butter depending on how dry the cheese is ? the mixture should be spreadable but not loose | Beat thoroughly with a wooden spoon until smooth and well blended | Add sweet sherry and Madeira wine, mixing through until fully incorporated | Press the mixture firmly into small ramekins or pots, smoothing down the top with the back of a spoon | Pour a thin layer of melted butter over the top of each pot to seal ? this preserves the cheese and forms a classic seal | Cover with plastic wrap and refrigerate for at least 24 hours to allow the flavors to blend and mature | Remove from refrigerator one hour before serving to bring to room temperature | Serve spread on crusty bread, toast, or crackers

ingredients: 500g white fish fillets (boneless, such as cod or tilapia), 1 small onion (finely chopped), 2 large eggs (beaten), 3 tbsp evaporated milk, 1/2 tsp salt, 1/4 tsp white pepper, vegetable oil for deep frying, sweet chili sauce or tartar sauce for serving
instructions: Steam or gently boil fish fillets until fully cooked and flaky, about 8-10 minutes | Drain fish thoroughly and let cool until easy to handle | Flake the fish finely with a fork, removing any remaining bones | Finely chop onion and mix with the flaked fish in a bowl | Add beaten eggs, evaporated milk, salt, and white pepper | Mix thoroughly until the mixture is well combined and holds together when squeezed | Shape mixture into golf ball-sized balls, squeezing out any surplus liquid as you form them ? the balls should be firm enough to hold their shape | Heat vegetable oil in a deep pot to 350?F (175?C) | Carefully drop fish balls into the hot oil and fry in batches until golden brown on all sides, about 3-4 minutes | Remove with a slotted spoon and drain on paper towels | Serve hot with sweet chili sauce or tartar sauce, or enjoy them cold as a snack

recipe_name: Corn on the Cob With Lemon-Basil Butter
ingredients: 6 ears fresh corn (husks on), 1/2 cup unsalted butter (softened), 1/4 cup fresh basil leaves (packed), 1 tbsp lemon zest, 2 tbsp fresh lemon juice, 1 clove garlic (minced), 1/2 tsp salt, 1/4 tsp ground black pepper
instructions: Make the lemon-basil butter: place softened butter, fresh basil leaves, lemon zest, lemon juice, minced garlic, salt, and pepper in a food processor | Pulse until basil is finely incorporated and the butter turns a light green color | Transfer butter to a small serving bowl and set aside ? can be made up to 3 days ahead and refrigerated | Prepare the corn: carefully pull off the dry outer husks, setting aside several to tear into 1/4-inch-wide strips to use as ties | Gently peel back the inner husks without detaching them from the cob | Remove all silk threads from the corn kernels | Lightly coat each ear of corn with a generous layer of lemon-basil butter | Lay the inner husks back in place around the corn, covering the kernels | Tie the top of each ear with the reserved husk strips to secure | Immerse tied corn in a large bowl of cold water and soak for 20 minutes ? this prevents the husks from burning on the grill | Drain well | Place corn on a preheated hot grill and cook for 20 minutes, turning often with tongs, until husks are charred and corn is tender | Remove ties and husks, and serve immediately with extra lemon-basil butter on the side

ingredients: 2 cups raw walnut halves, 1 tbsp extra virgin olive oil, 2 tbsp agave syrup or maple syrup, 1/2 tsp sea salt, 1 vanilla bean (split lengthwise, seeds scraped), 1/4 tsp ground cinnamon (optional)
instructions: Place walnuts and olive oil in a cast iron skillet and turn heat to high | As soon as you hear the slightest sizzle, immediately turn heat down to medium or low ? nuts burn quickly so monitor closely | Toast walnuts for 3-4 minutes, stirring frequently, until they smell nutty and fragrant | Add agave syrup and stir to distribute evenly around the pan, cooking for another 1-2 minutes | Sprinkle in sea salt and stir | Scrape the seeds from the vanilla bean and stir into the walnuts, ensuring even coating | Remove walnuts from pan and spread on parchment paper to cool ? they will crisp up as they cool | Add just a dash of ground cinnamon if desired | Let cool completely before serving or storing in an airtight container

ingredients: For pastry: 4 oz cream cheese (softened), 1/2 cup unsalted butter (softened), 1 cup all-purpose flour. For filling: 2 large eggs, 3/4 cup granulated sugar, 2 tbsp unsalted butter (melted), 2 tsp lemon zest, 1/4 cup fresh lemon juice, pinch of salt
instructions: Blend together cream cheese and softened butter until smooth and creamy | Stir in flour gradually until a soft dough forms, then shape into a ball, wrap in plastic, and chill for at least 1 hour | Preheat oven to 350?F (175?C) | Divide chilled dough into 24 equal balls | Place each ball in an ungreased miniature muffin tin cup | Using your fingers, press dough evenly against the bottom and up the sides of each cup to form a tart shell | Prepare the filling: whisk together eggs, sugar, melted butter, lemon zest, lemon juice, and salt until smooth and well combined | Divide filling evenly among the 24 tart shells, filling each about 3/4 full | Bake for 25-30 minutes until filling is set and edges are lightly golden | Remove from oven and let tarts cool in the pan for several minutes | Gently run a knife around the edges and carefully remove tarts from tins | Transfer to a wire rack to cool completely | Dust with powdered sugar before serving if desired

recipe_name: Stuffed Green Pepper Soup For A Crowd
ingredients: 500g lean ground beef, 3 large green bell peppers (diced), 1 large onion (diced), 3 celery stalks (diced), 200g fresh mushrooms (sliced), 4 cloves garlic (minced), 2 cans (400g each) tomato sauce, 2 cans (400g each) diced tomatoes, 1 tbsp fresh basil (chopped), 1 tsp dried basil, 1 tsp salt, 1/2 tsp black pepper, 2 cups uncooked white rice, 4 cups water
instructions: In a 12-inch skillet, cook ground beef and diced onion for 10 minutes over medium-high heat until meat is browned and onion is no longer pink ? drain excess fat | Add minced garlic and cook just until fragrant, about 1 minute, then set aside | In a medium saucepan, bring 2 cups water to a boil | Add uncooked rice, cover, and remove from heat | Let sit for 5 minutes, then fluff with a fork and set aside ? the rice will finish cooking in the soup | In a 6-quart crockpot or large Dutch oven, combine the beef mixture, diced green peppers, diced celery, sliced mushrooms, tomato sauce, diced tomatoes with their juices, fresh basil, dried basil, salt, and pepper | Cook at low temperature, stirring occasionally, just until peppers are softened but still have a little crunch to them ? about 2-3 hours on low in a crockpot or 45 minutes on the stovetop | Add the partially cooked rice to the soup and stir to combine | Let cook for another 10 minutes until rice is fully tender and has absorbed some of the soup liquid | Ladle into bowls and serve hot ? this makes enough for a crowd

ingredients: 1 large loaf French or Italian bread, 8 oz cream cheese (softened), 2 tbsp ranch dressing mix (dry), 1 1/2 cups sharp cheddar cheese (shredded), 2 tbsp fresh parsley (chopped, for garnish)
instructions: Preheat oven to 450?F (230?C) | Slice the loaf of bread in half lengthwise and place both halves cut-side up on a baking sheet | Slice each half into 1-inch thick slices, BUT do not slice all the way through to the bottom crust ? leave the slices attached so the loaf still holds together | In a bowl, blend softened cream cheese with dry ranch dressing mix until smooth and well combined | Spread cream cheese mixture generously on top of the sliced loaves, getting some between each cut | Sprinkle shredded cheddar cheese evenly over the top | Bake for 10 to 15 minutes until brown and bubbly, with the cheese fully melted and golden | Remove from oven and let cool for 2-3 minutes | Garnish with chopped parsley | Pull apart individual cheese fingers and serve warm

ingredients: 8 slices thick white bread (crusts removed), 1/2 cup unsalted butter (softened at room temperature), 1/2 cup icing sugar (powdered sugar), 2 tbsp black sesame seeds
instructions: Take butter out of the refrigerator and let it soften at room temperature for about 15 minutes before starting | Preheat oven to 150?C (300?F) | In a bowl, cream softened butter with icing sugar using a wooden spoon or electric mixer until smooth, pale, and fluffy ? this is your buttercream icing | Spread the buttercream icing thinly and evenly over both sides of each slice of bread | Cut the crusts off the bread slices to neaten the edges | Cut each slice into quarters (triangles or squares) and place on a baking tray lined with parchment paper | Sprinkle a few black sesame seeds over the top of each piece | Bake in the low oven at 150?C (300?F) for 15 minutes ? the low temperature allows the bread to dry out and crisp without burning | Remove from oven and let cool on the tray ? the toast will crisp up further as it cools and the icing sugar and butter set | Serve once cooled and crisp, or store in an airtight container for up to 3 days

ingredients: For crust: 2 cups all-purpose flour, 1 cup unsalted butter (softened), 1/2 cup granulated sugar. For cream layer: 8 oz cream cheese (softened), 1 cup powdered sugar, 1 tsp vanilla extract. For filling: 1 can (600g) lemon pie filling. For topping: 1 package Dream Whip or 2 cups whipped topping, 1 cup cold milk, lemon zest for garnish
instructions: Preheat oven to 350?F (175?C) | In a medium mixing bowl, combine flour, softened butter, and sugar with a fork until crumbly and the mixture resembles coarse sand | Press crust mixture firmly into an ungreased 9 x 13 baking dish in an even layer | Bake crust for 20 minutes or until slightly golden brown | While crust is baking, beat softened cream cheese and powdered sugar together until smooth, then mix in vanilla extract | When crust is done baking, place it in the refrigerator for about 30 minutes to cool completely ? this prevents the layers from melting | When the crust is cool to the touch, spread the cream cheese mixture evenly over the crust | Spoon lemon pie filling over the cream cheese layer and spread gently to the edges | Prepare Dream Whip according to package directions (whip with cold milk until peaks form) or use prepared whipped topping | Spread whipped topping over the lemon layer | Garnish with fresh lemon zest | Refrigerate for at least 2 hours before slicing and serving

ingredients: 2 large potatoes (peeled and finely diced), 1 medium onion (finely diced), 2 tbsp Worcestershire sauce, 2 tbsp fresh parsley (chopped), 2 tbsp milk (plus extra for brushing), 1 tsp salt, 1/2 tsp black pepper, 350g beef skirt steak or sirloin (finely diced), 2 sheets ready-rolled shortcrust pastry, beef gravy for serving
instructions: Add diced potato, diced onion, diced beef, Worcestershire sauce, and chopped parsley to a large bowl | Season generously with salt and pepper and mix everything well until thoroughly combined | Roll out pie crusts on a lightly floured surface | Cut into 12 rounds of about 4 inches diameter ? a martini glass works perfectly as a template for cutting | Divide the filling evenly among 6 of the rounds, mounding it in the center | Cover each filled round with one of the remaining 6 rounds | Turn the edges of the bottom round up over the top round and crimp with your fingers or a fork to seal, making little sealed packages | Make 3 small slits in the top of each pasty with a sharp knife to allow steam to escape | Brush the tops lightly with milk for a golden finish | Place pasties on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper | Bake at 425?F (220?C) for about 30 minutes or until the pastry is lightly browned and crisp | Serve hot with beef gravy ? adding a little extra chopped parsley to the gravy complements the filling beautifully

ingredients: 500g kielbasa or Polish sausage, 1 medium onion (diced), 1/2 cup ketchup, 1/3 cup brown sugar, 2 tbsp granulated sugar, 2 tbsp white vinegar, 2 tbsp molasses, 1 tbsp prepared yellow mustard, 2 cans (400g each) great northern beans (drained and rinsed), 1/2 tsp black pepper
instructions: Preheat oven to 350?F (175?C) | Cut kielbasa or Polish sausage in half lengthwise, then slice thinly into half-moons | In a saucepan, cook sliced sausage and diced onion in boiling water for 2 minutes, then drain well | In a large bowl, combine ketchup, brown sugar, granulated sugar, vinegar, molasses, and mustard ? whisk until the sugars dissolve | Stir in the drained great northern beans and the sausage-onion mixture until everything is evenly coated | Transfer to a greased 2 1/2-quart baking dish and spread evenly | Cover dish with foil or a lid | Bake for 1 hour and 30 minutes or until the bean mixture reaches your desired thickness ? the sauce should be rich and sticky | Check halfway through and stir gently | Alternatively, this can be cooked in a slow cooker on low for 6-8 hours | Serve hot as a hearty main dish or side

ingredients: 450g ground pork, 450g ground beef, 2/3 cup water, 1 large onion (finely diced), 3 cloves garlic (minced), 1 tsp salt, 1/2 tsp poultry seasoning, 1/2 tsp dried thyme, 1/2 tsp ground sage, 1/4 tsp ground mustard, 1/4 tsp ground cloves, 1 tbsp Worcestershire sauce, 1 tbsp soy sauce, 3 medium potatoes (peeled, boiled, and mashed), 2 double pie crusts (4 rounds total), 1 egg (beaten, for egg wash)
instructions: Preheat oven to 350?F (175?C) | In a large skillet over medium-high heat, brown ground pork and ground beef together, breaking apart with a spoon, until fully cooked ? drain excess fat | Add water, diced onion, minced garlic, salt, poultry seasoning, thyme, sage, ground mustard, ground cloves, Worcestershire sauce, and soy sauce | Mix thoroughly with the browned meat, reduce heat, and simmer uncovered for 25 minutes, stirring occasionally, until most of the liquid has evaporated | While meat simmers, boil peeled potatoes in salted water until tender, then drain and mash until smooth with no lumps | Place two pie crusts into two pie pans as the bottom layers | Divide the meat mixture evenly between the two pie shells | Spread a layer of mashed potatoes evenly over the meat filling in each pie | Cover each pie with the remaining two crusts, crimping edges to seal | Cut a few small slits in the top crusts to vent steam | Beat the egg and brush generously over the top crusts of both pies for a glossy golden finish | Bake at 350?F (175?C) for 40 minutes until the crust is golden brown | Let pies rest for 10 minutes before slicing | Serve hot, traditionally enjoyed during the Christmas season

ingredients: 1 ripe peach (pitted and sliced), 1/2 cup peach yogurt, 1/2 cup vanilla ice cream, 1/4 cup fresh raspberries, 1/4 cup milk, 1 tsp honey (optional), fresh raspberries for garnish
instructions: Place peach slices, peach yogurt, vanilla ice cream, fresh raspberries, and milk in a blender | Add honey if you prefer extra sweetness | Process on high speed until completely smooth and no fruit chunks remain ? about 30-45 seconds | Check consistency and add a splash more milk if the shake is too thick | Pour into a tall glass | Garnish with a few fresh raspberries on top | Serve immediately while cold and thick

recipe_name: Chicken Balsamico With Yukon Gold Potatoes
ingredients: 800g Yukon Gold potatoes (halved or quartered), 4 slices bacon (diced), 8 bone-in chicken thighs (skin-on), 1 1/2 tsp salt, 1/2 tsp fresh ground black pepper, 2 tbsp fresh rosemary (chopped), 4 cloves garlic (minced), 1/3 cup balsamic vinegar, 1 cup chicken broth
instructions: Place halved Yukon Gold potatoes in the insert of a 5 to 7-quart slow cooker | Cook diced bacon in a large skillet over medium heat until crisp, about 5-6 minutes | Remove bacon with a slotted spoon to paper towels to drain, leaving the bacon drippings in the pan | Sprinkle chicken thighs evenly on both sides with 1 1/2 teaspoons salt and 1/2 teaspoon pepper | Add seasoned chicken to the hot bacon drippings, skin-side down | Brown chicken on all sides until deep golden, about 12-15 minutes total ? do this in batches if needed to avoid crowding | Add chopped rosemary and minced garlic to the skillet and saut? for 1-2 minutes until fragrant | Deglaze the skillet by pouring in balsamic vinegar, scraping up all the browned bits from the bottom with a wooden spoon | Transfer the chicken and all pan contents to the slow cooker insert over the potatoes | Pour chicken broth into the slow cooker | Cover and cook on HIGH for 3 hours or on LOW for 5-6 hours until chicken is tender and potatoes are cooked through | Season with additional salt and pepper to taste | Sprinkle the reserved crispy bacon over the top of the chicken and potatoes just before serving

recipe_name: Quinoa Breakfast With Cranberries and Almonds
ingredients: 1 cup quinoa (rinsed), 2 cups water, 1/2 cup dried cranberries, 1/3 cup sliced almonds, 1/2 tsp ground cinnamon, 1 tbsp maple syrup (optional), pinch of salt, milk or yogurt for serving
instructions: Rinse quinoa thoroughly under cold water in a fine mesh strainer ? this removes the natural bitter coating | Combine rinsed quinoa, water, dried cranberries, sliced almonds, and a pinch of salt in a medium saucepan | Bring to a boil over medium heat | Once boiling, reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 20 minutes until quinoa is tender and water is fully absorbed | Remove from heat | Stir in ground cinnamon and maple syrup if using | Cover again and let sit for 1 minute to allow the cinnamon flavor to bloom | Fluff with a fork and spoon into serving bowls | Serve hot with a splash of milk or a dollop of yogurt on top

ingredients: 4 medium yellow zucchini or summer squash, 2 tbsp canola oil, 1/4 cup unsweetened coconut flakes, 10 fresh curry leaves, 2 dried red chilies, 1 jalape?o (seeded and minced), 1 tsp mustard seeds, 1 tsp cumin seeds, 1/2 tsp turmeric, 1/2 tsp salt (adjust to taste), flatbread for serving
instructions: Cut zucchini lengthwise in half, then slice into 1/3-inch thick half-moons | Heat oil in a large pan or wok over moderate heat until shimmering | Add mustard seeds and cook for about 2 minutes until they begin to pop and splutter | Add coconut flakes, curry leaves, dried red chilies, minced jalape?o, cumin seeds, and turmeric to the pan ? be careful, the curry leaves will pop and splutter when they hit the hot oil | Cook for about 2-4 minutes, stirring frequently, until the coconut begins to brown and becomes fragrant | Add sliced zucchini and mix thoroughly to coat with the spices | Turn the heat up to medium-high and cook, stirring occasionally, for about 8 minutes until zucchini is tender but still has a slight bite | Season with salt to taste and cook for one more minute | Serve hot with your choice of warm flatbread on the side

ingredients: 1 cup white rice, 2 cups low-sodium chicken broth, 1/4 cup fresh orange juice, 2 tbsp fresh lime juice, 2 tbsp olive oil, 4 tbsp fresh cilantro (chopped, divided), 4 cloves garlic (minced), 1 tsp sugar, 1 tsp salt, 1/2 tsp black pepper, 4 tilapia fillets (about 150g each), 1/2 cup salsa, 1 can (400g) black beans (drained and rinsed), 1 cup fresh pineapple (diced), 2 limes (thinly sliced)
instructions: Combine rice and chicken broth in a pot over medium heat and bring to a boil | Reduce heat to low, cover, and cook until rice is tender and has absorbed all the liquid, about 20 minutes | Preheat oven to 400?F (200?C) | In a mixing bowl, whisk together orange juice, lime juice, olive oil, 2 tablespoons of the chopped cilantro, minced garlic, and sugar | Season with salt and pepper | Add tilapia fillets to the marinade, turning to coat both sides | Marinate in the refrigerator for 20 minutes, turning occasionally | Stir together the cooked rice, salsa, drained black beans, diced pineapple, and remaining 2 tablespoons of chopped cilantro in a 2 or 3-quart baking dish | Remove tilapia from the marinade, reserving the marinade | Lay the fish fillets over the rice mixture, overlapping slightly if necessary | Pour the reserved marinade over the fish | Shingle thin lime slices over the top of the fish | Bake for 25 to 30 minutes until the fish flakes easily with a fork, is opaque throughout, and cooked through | Garnish with additional chopped cilantro before serving

ingredients: 1 block (400g) extra firm tofu (pressed and cubed), 3 tbsp sesame oil (divided), 1 medium onion (thinly sliced), 4 cloves garlic (minced), 1/3 cup honey, 3 tbsp soy sauce, 2 tbsp rice vinegar, 1/2 tsp ginger powder, 1/4 tsp cayenne pepper, 1/2 tsp sea salt, 1/3 cup water, 1 tbsp cornstarch or arrowroot powder, 1 tbsp sesame seeds, mixed stir-fry vegetables (broccoli, bell pepper, snap peas)
instructions: Press tofu for 20 minutes by wrapping in paper towels and placing a weight on top, then cut into 1-inch cubes | Make the honey garlic sauce: heat 1 tbsp sesame oil in a small pan over medium heat | Saut? sliced onion until translucent, about 3-4 minutes | Add minced garlic and continue cooking for 1 minute until fragrant | Add honey, stirring gently as it melts | Whisk in soy sauce, rice vinegar, ginger powder, cayenne, and sea salt | Add water and bring to a simmer | Taste and adjust seasoning, adding more honey or salt as desired | Whisk in cornstarch or arrowroot, stirring continuously, adding more as needed until the sauce thickens to a saucy consistency ? it should coat the back of a spoon | Remove sauce from heat and set aside | Heat remaining 2 tbsp sesame oil in a large saut? pan or wok over high heat | Saut? tofu cubes until golden and crispy on all sides, about 5-6 minutes | Add in mixed vegetables one at a time, heartiest ones first (broccoli, then bell pepper, then snap peas), stirring as you go until all vegetables are cooked but still crisp ? this should take about 5 minutes total | Remove pan from heat | Pour the hot honey garlic sauce over the tofu and vegetables, tossing to coat evenly | Garnish with sesame seeds and serve immediately over steamed rice or noodles

ingredients: 4 ripe tomatoes, 2 green bell peppers (diced), 2 red bell peppers (diced), 2 medium eggplants (cubed), 2 medium zucchini (cubed), 4 cloves garlic (minced), 400g fresh tuna steaks (cut into 1-inch cubes), 5 tbsp olive oil (divided), 4 sprigs fresh thyme, 1 tsp dried oregano, 1 small hot chili pepper (minced), 1/2 tsp salt, 1/2 cup water if needed
instructions: Clean all the vegetables thoroughly | Bring a pot of water to a boil and briefly slip the tomatoes in boiling water for 30 seconds to loosen their peels, then remove and peel off the skins | Deseed the tomatoes and cut into chunks | Cut bell peppers, eggplants, and zucchini into uniform bite-sized pieces | Cut fresh tuna into 1-inch cubes and set aside | In a Dutch oven or heavy pot, heat 1 tablespoon olive oil over medium heat | Add bell peppers and cook over low heat for 10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until they begin to soften | Add cubed eggplant with 2 more tablespoons olive oil and continue cooking for another 10 minutes, stirring occasionally | Add cubed zucchini along with fresh thyme sprigs and dried oregano, plus the remaining olive oil | Let this simmer uncovered for 10 minutes, stirring occasionally | Add the peeled tomato chunks, minced hot chili pepper, minced garlic, and cubed tuna | Gently fold everything together with a long wooden spoon, being careful not to break up the tuna too much | Cover and cook over very low heat for 20 minutes, stirring very gently once or twice | If the mixture becomes too dry, add up to 1/2 cup of water as needed | Remove thyme sprigs before serving | This dish is delicious served hot, warm, or even cold ? traditionally enjoyed at any temperature

recipe_name: California Walnut Breakfast and Snack Cookies
ingredients: 1/2 cup unsalted butter (softened), 3/4 cup brown sugar (packed), 1 tsp vanilla extract, 1/2 tsp maple extract, 1 can (230g) crushed pineapple (with juice), 1 1/2 cups all-purpose flour, 1/4 cup skim milk powder, 1/2 tsp baking soda, 1 tsp ground cinnamon, 1/4 tsp salt, 1 1/2 cups quick-cooking oatmeal, 1/2 cup raisins, 1/2 cup chopped dates, 1 cup California walnuts (chopped)
instructions: Preheat oven to 350?F (180?C) and lightly grease a baking sheet | In a large mixing bowl, use an electric mixer to cream together softened butter and brown sugar until light and fluffy, about 2-3 minutes | Beat in maple extract and vanilla extract until fully incorporated | Stir in crushed pineapple along with its juice until combined | In a separate bowl, mix together flour, skim milk powder, baking soda, cinnamon, and salt until well combined | Stir the dry ingredients into the pineapple mixture, mixing just until incorporated ? do not overmix | Stir in oatmeal, raisins, chopped dates, and chopped walnuts until evenly distributed throughout the dough | Drop rounded spoonfuls of dough onto the greased baking sheet, spacing them about 2 inches apart | Bake for 12 to 15 minutes or until the cookies are golden brown around the edges | Remove from oven and let cookies cool on the baking sheet for 5 minutes before transferring to a wire rack to cool completely | Store in an airtight container for up to 1 week

ingredients: 2 cups rye flour, 1 cup white bread flour (plus extra for dusting), 2 tsp salt, 25g fresh yeast cake (or 2 1/4 tsp active dry yeast), 1 tbsp honey, 500ml warm water (divided into 100ml and 400ml)
instructions: Mix rye flour, white flour, and salt together in a large mixing bowl and set aside | In a separate small bowl, dissolve honey and fresh yeast in 100ml of warm water (about 85-95?F) | Let the yeast mixture stand for 10 minutes until it becomes frothy and activated | Add yeast mixture to the flour mixture | Gradually add the remaining 400ml of warm water, little by little, mixing continuously until a dough forms | Turn dough out onto a lightly floured surface and knead for 8-10 minutes until the dough is smooth, elastic, and pliable | Cover the dough with a clean kitchen towel and let it rise in a warm place for 30 minutes | Punch down the dough and knead once more, then cover again and let rise for another 40 minutes | Shape the dough into an oblong loaf and place on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper | Cover loosely and let rest while the oven preheats to 250?C (480?F) | Just before baking, pat the surface of the bread with water using your hands ? this creates a crisp crust | Place in the oven on the second-lowest shelf | Bake for 10 minutes at 250?C, then lower the temperature to 190?C (375?F) and continue baking for approximately 45 minutes | The bread is done when it sounds hollow when tapped on the bottom | Transfer to a wire rack and let cool completely before slicing

ingredients: 2 tbsp peanut oil, 4 cloves garlic (minced), 3 green onions (sliced), 3 cups cooked brown rice (preferably day-old), 300g cooked shrimp (peeled and deveined), 1 can (200g) water chestnuts (drained and chopped), 1/4 cup vegetable broth or water, 2 tbsp soy sauce, 1 tsp sesame oil, 1/4 cup sliced almonds (toasted)
instructions: Heat peanut oil in a large nonstick pan or wok over medium-high heat | Add minced garlic and sliced green onions, saut?ing until soft and fragrant, about 3 minutes | Add cooked brown rice, cooked shrimp, and chopped water chestnuts to the pan | Saut? for another 1 minute, tossing to combine with the garlic and onions | Pour in vegetable broth (or water), soy sauce, and sesame oil | Stir everything together to combine evenly | Cover the pan with a lid and cook until all ingredients are heated through, about 3 to 5 minutes | Remove lid and give it a final toss | Sprinkle toasted sliced almonds over the top | Serve immediately while hot

ingredients: 3 plum tomatoes (diced), 1 English cucumber (diced), 2 small cucumbers (diced), 1/2 red onion (thinly sliced), 1 yellow bell pepper (diced), 1/2 cup Kalamata olives (pitted and halved), 2 cups fresh arugula, 1/4 cup flat-leaf parsley (chopped), 100g soft goat cheese or herb-flavored cream cheese log (crumbled), 1/2 tsp fresh ground black pepper, 3 tbsp light salad dressing or vinaigrette, crusty bread for serving
instructions: Rinse and prepare all vegetables ? dice tomatoes and cucumbers, thinly slice red onion, dice bell pepper, halve olives, and roughly chop parsley | Place arugula in a large plastic mixing bowl as the base | Add diced tomatoes, cucumbers, red onion, bell pepper, and Kalamata olives | Season with fresh ground black pepper | Pour salad dressing over the ingredients and toss gently to coat everything lightly ? use just enough to moisten, not drown, the salad | Crumble the soft goat cheese or cream cheese log over the top ? it will be very soft and will blend into the flavor mix when you toss | Carefully transfer the dressed salad into a pretty serving bowl, being gentle with the ingredients | This makes 4 generous side servings with dinner or 2-3 lunch servings with fresh, crusty continental-style bread on the side | Serve immediately at room temperature

ingredients: 1 cup quinoa (rinsed thoroughly), 2 1/2 cups water, 1/2 tsp salt, 1/3 cup fresh lemon juice, 3 tbsp olive oil (divided), 1 English cucumber (diced), 1/2 red onion (finely diced), 1 cup fresh parsley (chopped), 1/4 cup fresh mint (chopped), 1/2 cup crumbled feta cheese, 1/4 cup Kalamata olives (halved), salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Rinse quinoa thoroughly in a fine mesh strainer under cold water ? this removes the natural bitter coating | Drain and place quinoa in a heavy dry pan | Heat over medium heat, stirring constantly, until the grains separate and begin to toast and turn lightly golden, about 3-4 minutes | Add water and 1/2 tsp salt, bring to a boil while stirring | Reduce heat to low, cover, and cook for 15 minutes or until all the liquid is absorbed | Transfer cooked quinoa to a large bowl and set aside to cool to room temperature | In a small bowl, whisk together fresh lemon juice and 1 tablespoon of olive oil to make the dressing ? set aside | Place the remaining 2 tablespoons olive oil, diced cucumber, diced red onion, chopped parsley, and chopped mint in a separate larger bowl | Add the cooled quinoa and the lemon-oil dressing | Toss everything together gently but thoroughly to combine | Sprinkle crumbled feta cheese and halved Kalamata olives over the top | Season to taste with additional salt and fresh ground black pepper | Serve at room temperature or chilled, as a side dish or light meal

ingredients: 2 tbsp butter, 1 medium onion (diced), 3 cloves garlic (minced), 2 celery stalks (diced), 500g white meat chicken (cubed), 1 can (400g) cream of mushroom soup, 1 can (400g) cream of chicken soup, 1/2 tsp salt, 1/4 tsp black pepper, 1/2 cup sour cream, chow mein noodles or egg noodles for serving, fresh parsley for garnish
instructions: Melt butter in a large skillet over medium heat | Saut? diced onion, minced garlic, and diced celery in the butter until soft and transparent, about 5-6 minutes | Add cubed chicken to the pan and reduce heat to low | Simmer for 5 minutes, stirring constantly, until chicken is cooked through and no longer pink on the outside | Stir in cream of mushroom soup and cream of chicken soup until fully combined with the chicken mixture | Cook for an additional 5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until heated through and bubbling gently | Season with salt and black pepper to taste | Serve hot over a bed of crispy chow mein noodles or buttered egg noodles | Top each serving with a generous dollop of sour cream and garnish with fresh chopped parsley

ingredients: 2 cups cooked chicken (shredded), 1 can (400g) cream of chicken soup, 1/2 tsp black pepper, 2 cups cheddar cheese (shredded, divided), 8 large flour tortillas, salsa for serving, sour cream for serving
instructions: Preheat oven to 425?F (220?C) | In a bowl, mix cream of chicken soup, black pepper, 1/2 cup of the shredded cheese, and shredded chicken until well combined | Lay tortillas flat on a clean work surface | Spread about 1/4 cup of the chicken mixture onto one half of each tortilla, spreading to within 1/2 inch of the edge | Moisten the edges of the tortilla with a little water using your fingertip ? this helps seal the quesadilla | Fold the empty half over the filled half, pressing edges gently to seal | Place folded quesadillas on 2 baking sheets, spacing them slightly apart | Bake for 10 minutes or until hot and starting to crisp | Remove from oven and sprinkle remaining cheese over the tops | Serve immediately with salsa and sour cream on the side | Makes 8 quesadillas

ingredients: For crust: 1 cup unsalted cashews, 1/3 cup light brown sugar, 1 cup all-purpose flour, 1/4 tsp salt, 1/2 cup unsalted butter (cold, cubed), 1 large egg, 2 tbsp candied ginger (finely chopped), ice water as needed. For filling: 3 ripe guavas, 3 packages (250g each) cream cheese (softened), 1 cup granulated sugar, 1 vanilla bean (seeds scraped), 3 large eggs, 1 cup mascarpone cheese. For glaze: 1/2 cup guava jelly, 2 tbsp water
instructions: Make the crust: pulse cashews and brown sugar in a food processor until finely ground | Add flour and salt, pulse to blend | Pulse in cold cubed butter until the largest pieces are pea-sized | Pulse in the egg and chopped candied ginger until a moist, crumbly dough forms | Transfer dough to a bowl and work the egg into the mixture with your fingers until well blended ? if the dough seems too dry, add ice water up to 2 teaspoons | Do not overwork or the crust will be tough | Press dough evenly into the bottom and halfway up the sides of a 9-inch springform pan, keeping it about 1/4 inch thick all around | Cover with plastic wrap and chill for at least 2 hours or overnight | Once chilled, preheat oven to 350?F (175?C) | Unwrap crust and prick it all over with a fork | Bake until partly dried and partly firm, 15 to 25 minutes ? do not overbake | Set aside to cool completely | Prepare the filling: peel guavas with a vegetable peeler, scoop out seeds with a spoon, roughly chop, and pur?e in a food processor until smooth | Measure out 1 cup of guava pur?e and set aside | Beat softened cream cheese with an electric mixer until smooth and creamy | Gradually add sugar and vanilla bean seeds, continuing to beat until fluffy | Add eggs one at a time, beating well after each addition and scraping down the bowl often | Stir in mascarpone cheese and the 1 cup of guava pur?e until smooth | Reduce oven to 300?F (150?C) | Pour filling into the cooled crust and place the pan on the middle oven rack | Place a shallow pan of water on the bottom oven rack below the cheesecake to help prevent cracking | Bake for 1 3/4 to 2 hours until edges are set but the center is still slightly wobbly | As soon as the cheesecake comes out of the oven, run a thin-bladed knife around the edge to loosen it from the pan | Cool for 1 hour on a wire rack, then chill thoroughly in the refrigerator for at least 4 hours, preferably overnight | Make the glaze: melt guava jelly and water in a small saucepan, bring to a boil, and simmer for 1 minute | Pour glaze over the chilled cheesecake, spread evenly, and chill for 1 more hour before serving

ingredients: 2 tbsp olive oil, 1 whole head garlic (cloves separated and peeled, plus extra for roasting), 1 large leek (white and light green parts, sliced), 2 medium potatoes (peeled and diced), 4 cups chicken or vegetable stock, 1/2 tsp salt, 1/4 tsp white pepper, 2 tbsp fresh chives (chopped), crusty bread for serving
instructions: Preheat oven to 400?F (200?C) for roasted garlic garnish: slice the top off an extra head of garlic, drizzle with olive oil, wrap in foil, and roast for 40 minutes until soft ? set aside | Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium-low heat | Add sliced leeks and all the peeled garlic cloves | Cook gently until soft and fragrant, about 8-10 minutes ? do not brown, as this will make the soup bitter | Add diced potatoes and stock, then bring to a boil | Lower heat and simmer gently until the potatoes are tender, about 20 minutes | Remove 1 cup of the soup and pur?e it in a blender until smooth, then pour it back into the pot ? this thickens the soup while leaving some texture | Season with salt and white pepper | Squeeze the roasted garlic cloves out of their skins and stir them into the soup along with fresh chopped chives | Stir well and serve hot with crusty bread on the side for dipping

ingredients: 8 oz cream cheese (softened), 1 cup fresh strawberries (hulled and chopped), 1/4 cup granulated sugar, 1/4 cup sour cream, 1 tsp pure vanilla extract, 1 tbsp strawberry liqueur (optional), graham crackers, vanilla wafers, or fresh fruit for dipping
instructions: Place softened cream cheese, chopped fresh strawberries, sugar, sour cream, vanilla extract, and strawberry liqueur (if using) in a blender or food processor | Process on high speed until very smooth and no strawberry chunks remain ? about 30-45 seconds | Scrape down the sides and process again briefly to ensure everything is fully incorporated | Pour the dip into a serving bowl, cover with plastic wrap, and refrigerate for at least 2 hours to allow the flavors to meld and the dip to firm up slightly | Before serving, stir once and garnish with a fresh strawberry on top | Serve chilled with graham crackers, vanilla wafers, or an assortment of fresh fruit for dipping

ingredients: 1 1/2 cups all-purpose flour, 1 cup granulated sugar, 3 tbsp unsweetened cocoa powder, 1 tsp baking soda, 1/2 tsp salt, 1/3 cup vegetable oil, 1 tbsp white vinegar, 1 tsp vanilla extract, 1 cup cold water. For frosting: 2-3 tbsp heavy cream, 2 tbsp unsalted butter (softened), 1 1/2 cups powdered sugar, 1/2 tsp vanilla extract, or chocolate frosting: 2 tbsp butter, 1/2 cup semisweet chocolate chips, 1 cup powdered sugar
instructions: Preheat oven to 350?F (175?C), or 325?F if using a glass pan | Sift together flour, sugar, cocoa powder, baking soda, and salt directly into an ungreased 9-inch square baking pan ? pressing through a fine sieve works perfectly | Blend the dry ingredients together right in the pan using a fork | Make 3 small wells in the dry mixture using a spoon | Pour vegetable oil into the first well, vinegar into the second, and vanilla extract into the third | Pour 1 cup cold water over everything | Whisk vigorously until the batter is smooth and no lumps remain, making sure to reach the corners of the pan | Bake for 30 minutes until a toothpick inserted in the center comes out clean | Let cake cool completely in the pan before frosting | For vanilla frosting: heat 2-3 tablespoons of heavy cream until warm, then let cool | Blend cooled cream with softened butter and powdered sugar until smooth, adding a splash of vanilla | For chocolate frosting: melt butter and semisweet chocolate chips in a bowl over a pan of hot water, remove from heat, stir in powdered sugar and vanilla, refrigerate until firm, then whip with a mixer to add air and lighten before spreading on cake

recipe_name: Corn Meal Coating for Fish or Chicken
ingredients: 1/2 cup yellow cornmeal, 1/4 cup all-purpose flour, 1 tsp paprika, 1/2 tsp black pepper, 1/2 tsp salt, 1/4 tsp garlic powder, 1/2 cup milk, 1 lb fish fillets or 2 1/2-3 lbs cut-up chicken pieces, 2-3 tbsp vegetable oil (for frying fish) or 3 tbsp melted butter (for baking chicken)
instructions: For Pan-Fried Fish (4 servings): In a shallow bowl, combine cornmeal, flour, paprika, pepper, salt, and garlic powder | Pat fish fillets dry with paper towels | Coat fish fillets in the combined dry ingredients, pressing gently to adhere | Dip coated fish in milk, letting excess drip off | Coat fish again in the dry ingredients for a double coating | Heat 2-3 tablespoons oil in a large skillet over medium heat | Fry fish for 2-3 minutes per side until golden brown and fish flakes easily with a fork | Drain on paper towels and serve immediately | For Oven-Fried Chicken (6 servings): Preheat oven to 375?F (190?C) | Dip cut-up chicken pieces in milk, letting excess drip off | Coat chicken in the combined dry ingredients, pressing to adhere | Place chicken skin-side up on a 15 x 10-inch jelly roll pan | Lightly brush with 3 tablespoons melted butter | Bake for 50-55 minutes until juices run clear when chicken is pierced with a fork

ingredients: 1 medium onion (thinly sliced), 200g mushrooms (sliced), 2 cups cheddar cheese (shredded), 4 large flour tortillas, 2 tbsp butter (for frying), 1 tbsp vegetable oil, salt and pepper to taste, sour cream and salsa for serving
instructions: Heat a skillet over medium heat and add a bit of oil or butter | Fry sliced onion until translucent, about 3-4 minutes | Add sliced mushrooms and cook until mushrooms have released their juices and the onion is lightly browned, about 5 minutes | Season with salt and pepper, then remove from skillet and set aside in a bowl | Using the same skillet, turn the heat down to medium-low | Butter one side of a tortilla and place it buttered-side down on the skillet | Sprinkle a layer of shredded cheddar cheese over the entire tortilla | Add some of the onion-mushroom mixture on one half | Place another tortilla on top with the buttered side facing up | Cook for a couple of minutes until the cheese starts to melt and the bottom tortilla is lightly browned | Flip carefully and cook the other side until golden | Remove from skillet and repeat with remaining ingredients | Cut each quesadilla into quarters and serve with sour cream and salsa on the side

ingredients: 6 large eggs, 1 1/2 cups granulated sugar, 2 tbsp instant coffee powder, 2 tbsp unsweetened cocoa powder, 1 can (354ml) evaporated milk, 1 tbsp vanilla extract, 1 cup chopped almonds (toasted), whole milk (enough to fill 1-gallon freezer)
instructions: Beat eggs well in a large bowl until frothy and light | Add sugar, instant coffee powder, cocoa powder, evaporated milk, vanilla extract, and toasted chopped almonds | Blend all ingredients thoroughly until sugar is dissolved and mixture is smooth | Pour mixture into a one-gallon ice cream freezer canister | Add enough whole milk to fill the freezer canister to the fill line, stirring to combine | Freeze according to your ice cream freezer manufacturer's instructions ? typically 20-30 minutes of churning | Transfer churned ice cream to a freezer-safe container and freeze for at least 2 hours to firm up before serving

ingredients: For syrup: 1 cup honey, 1/2 cup water, 1/2 cup granulated sugar, 1 cinnamon stick, 1 tsp lemon juice, 1 strip orange zest. For filling: 3 cups walnuts (finely chopped), 1/4 cup brown sugar, 1 tsp ground cinnamon, 1/4 tsp ground nutmeg, 1/4 tsp ground cloves. For pastry: 1 package (450g) phyllo dough (thawed), 1 cup unsalted butter (melted)
instructions: In a small saucepan, combine honey, water, sugar, cinnamon stick, lemon juice, and orange zest | Bring to a slow boil, stirring occasionally, until the sugar is dissolved | Cook over medium heat for 10 minutes until slightly thickened | Remove cinnamon stick and orange zest, then allow syrup to come to room temperature before using | Combine chopped walnuts, brown sugar, cinnamon, nutmeg, and cloves in a bowl to make the nut filling | Brush the bottom and sides of a 9x12-inch baking pan generously with melted butter ? lining with parchment paper makes removal easier | Place 8 phyllo sheets on the bottom of the pan, brushing each individual sheet with melted butter | Take an additional 4 sheets of phyllo and place them in the pan allowing the sheets to drape over each of the 4 sides of the pan | Brush these with melted butter | Pour half the nut mixture into the pan and spread evenly | Fold the overlapping phyllo sheets back over the nut mixture, brushing each with butter to envelope the filling | Place 4 more phyllo sheets over the first nut layer, brushing each with butter | Repeat the process: drape 4 sheets over the sides, brush with butter, add remaining nut mixture, fold over, and top with 8 or more phyllo sheets brushing each with butter | Tuck in the buttered phyllo neatly around the edges | Score through the top layers with a sharp knife making 3 strips lengthwise, then 8 strips widthwise, then diagonal cuts to form diamond-shaped pieces | Pour remaining melted butter over the pastry and lightly sprinkle a few drops of water on top | Bake at 325?F (160?C) for 30-40 minutes until nicely golden brown | Allow to cool for 5 minutes, then carefully spoon the cool syrup evenly over the hot pastry | Allow baklava to stand overnight at room temperature uncovered for the syrup to fully absorb | Cut through the scored pieces and serve

ingredients: 1 cup blue cheese (crumbled, divided), 1/2 cup sour cream, 4 oz cream cheese (softened), 2 green onions (finely chopped), 1 tsp lemon zest, 1 tbsp fresh lemon juice, 1/4 tsp garlic powder, 1 small garlic clove (minced), salt and pepper to taste, fresh vegetables or chips for serving
instructions: Combine 3/4 cup of the crumbled blue cheese with sour cream, softened cream cheese, chopped green onions, lemon zest, lemon juice, garlic powder, and minced garlic in a food processor | Pulse to blend to a lumpy-creamy texture ? you want some small blue cheese chunks remaining | Taste for seasoning and add salt, pepper, and more garlic if desired | Transfer mixture to a serving bowl | Stir in the remaining 1/4 cup crumbled blue cheese by hand for texture | Cover and refrigerate for at least 2 hours, preferably overnight, to allow the flavors to develop | Serve chilled with fresh vegetables, chips, or buffalo wings

ingredients: 1/4 cup coconut oil, 1/4 cup unsalted butter, 1/2 cup unsweetened cocoa powder, 1/4 cup honey, 1/4 cup maple syrup, 1/2 tsp liquid stevia (optional), 2 large eggs, 1 tsp vanilla extract, 2 tbsp ground flax seeds, 1/2 cup all-purpose flour, 1/4 tsp salt, 1/2 cup chocolate chips
instructions: Preheat oven to 350?F (175?C) and grease three 8x8-inch baking pans or one 9x13 pan | In a mixing bowl, combine coconut oil, butter, and cocoa powder, stirring until smooth and well blended | Add honey, maple syrup, and stevia if using, mixing well | Blend in the eggs one at a time, beating after each addition | Add vanilla extract, ground flax seeds, flour, and salt, mixing just until combined ? do not overmix | Fold in chocolate chips gently with a spatula | Spread the mixture evenly into the prepared pans | Bake for 25 minutes ? do not overbake | Brownies are done when a toothpick or knife tip inserted in the center comes out with moist crumbs on it (not wet batter) | Remove from oven and let pans cool completely before cutting into squares | Store in an airtight container

ingredients: 4 slices bacon (diced), 1 medium onion (diced), 1/2 cup ketchup, 1/4 cup brown sugar, 1 tbsp Worcestershire sauce, 2 cans (400g each) cut green beans (drained), salt and pepper to taste
instructions: Preheat oven to 350?F (175?C) | Cook diced bacon in a skillet over medium heat until it begins to render its fat | Add diced onion and cook until onions soften and bacon is crisp, about 5-6 minutes | Stir in ketchup, brown sugar, and Worcestershire sauce, mixing well | Simmer the sauce for 10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until it thickens slightly | Add drained green beans to the skillet and mix until beans are well coated with the sauce | Transfer mixture to a greased baking dish | Bake at 350?F for 20 minutes or until beans are tender and the sauce is bubbly | Serve hot as a side dish

ingredients: 2 cups plain flour, 2 tbsp ghee (plus extra for cooking), 1/2 tsp salt, 2/3 cup warm water, cooking oil for handling, curry or dhal for serving
instructions: In a large mixing bowl, combine flour, ghee, and salt, rubbing the ghee into the flour with your fingers until it resembles breadcrumbs | Gradually add warm water while mixing until a soft dough forms | Knead the dough on a clean surface for 8-10 minutes until smooth, elastic, and not sticky | Oil your hands with cooking oil and divide the dough into 8 equal small-sized balls | Coat each ball lightly with oil, place on a plate, and cover with plastic wrap | Rest the dough for at least 2-3 hours at room temperature, or overnight in the refrigerator for the best texture | When ready to cook, generously oil a clean work surface | Take one dough ball and flatten it with your palm, then using your hands, gently stretch and flip the dough in a circular motion until it becomes paper-thin and nearly translucent | Fold the stretched dough into a square by folding the edges inward | Heat a flat griddle or non-stick pan over medium-high heat and add a small amount of ghee | Place the folded dough on the hot griddle and cook for 2-3 minutes per side until golden brown and flaky with visible crispy layers | Remove from pan and gently crush the roti canai with both hands to reveal the flaky layers | Serve immediately with curry or dhal for dipping

ingredients: 2 cups all-purpose flour, 3/4 cup granulated sugar, 1 1/2 tsp baking powder, 1/2 tsp salt, 1/2 tsp baking soda, 1/4 cup margarine or butter (cold), 1 large egg, 3/4 cup orange juice, 1 tbsp orange zest, 1 cup fresh or frozen cranberries (roughly chopped), 1/2 cup chopped walnuts or pecans, 1/2 cup chocolate chips (optional)
instructions: Preheat oven to 350?F (175?C) and spray a 9x5-inch loaf pan with cooking spray | In a large mixing bowl, combine flour, sugar, baking powder, salt, and baking soda | Cut in cold margarine or butter using a pastry cutter or two forks until the mixture resembles coarse crumbs | Stir in egg and orange juice just until all the flour is moistened ? do not overmix | Fold in orange zest, chopped cranberries, nuts, and chocolate chips if using | Pour batter into the prepared loaf pan and spread evenly | Bake at 350?F for 55-65 minutes for a large loaf, or 35-40 minutes for two smaller 1-pound loaf pans, until a toothpick inserted in the center comes out clean | Let bread cool in the pan for 10 minutes, then turn out onto a wire rack to cool completely before slicing | Serve at room temperature or lightly toasted with butter

ingredients: 6 bone-in chicken thighs (skin-on), 1 medium onion (diced), 4 cloves garlic (minced), 2 tbsp margarine or butter, 300g frozen chopped spinach, 1/2 tsp salt, 1 tsp dried basil leaves, 400g spaghetti, 2 cups tomato pasta sauce, 1/4 cup Parmesan cheese (grated)
instructions: Rinse chicken thighs under cold running water and pat completely dry with paper towels, then set aside | Melt margarine in a large skillet over moderately high heat | Cook chicken a few pieces at a time, skin side down, for 5 minutes or until golden brown | Return all chicken to the skillet, add diced onion and minced garlic, cover the skillet, and cook for 5 minutes | Uncover skillet and push chicken to one side | Add the frozen block of spinach to the empty side of the skillet and sprinkle with 1/2 tsp salt and dried basil | Cover skillet and simmer for 15 minutes, separating the spinach with a fork as it cooks | While spinach cooks, heat pasta sauce in a separate pot until warmed through and keep on low | Cook spaghetti in salted boiling water until al dente, then drain | Uncover skillet and stir the spinach together with the onion and butter mixture to combine thoroughly | Turn chicken thighs skin side up and sprinkle with grated Parmesan cheese | Cover skillet and simmer for 10 more minutes or until chicken is tender and thoroughly cooked | Remove skillet from heat | Arrange drained spaghetti on a large serving platter | Pour heated pasta sauce over the spaghetti and top with the cooked spinach mixture | Arrange the cheese-topped chicken thighs on top and serve immediately

ingredients: 500g ground beef, 3 tbsp buffalo wing sauce, 1/4 cup breadcrumbs, 1/2 tsp garlic powder, 1/2 tsp onion powder, 2 tbsp butter (melted), 4 hamburger buns, 4 slices blue cheese, 4 lettuce leaves, extra buffalo sauce for drizzling
instructions: In a mixing bowl, combine ground beef, buffalo wing sauce, breadcrumbs, garlic powder, and onion powder | Mix gently with your hands until just combined ? do not overwork the meat | Form the mixture into 4 equal patties, making a slight indentation in the center of each with your thumb to prevent doming | Brush patties with melted butter | Heat a medium skillet over medium-high heat or prepare a grill to medium-high | Cook patties for 4-5 minutes per side until no longer pink in the center | Drain any excess fat from the pan | Toast hamburger buns lightly on the grill or in a dry pan | Place cooked patties on the bottom buns | Top each patty with a slice of blue cheese and a lettuce leaf | Drizzle with extra buffalo sauce | Close with the top buns and serve immediately

ingredients: 4 boneless skinless chicken breasts (cut into chunks), 2 red bell peppers (diced), 1 large onion (diced), 3 cloves garlic (minced), 1 can (400g) unsweetened pineapple chunks (with juice), 2 tbsp curry powder, 1/3 cup sweet chili sauce, 2 tbsp soy sauce, 1 tbsp rice vinegar, salt and pepper to taste, steamed rice for serving
instructions: Add diced chicken, diced bell peppers, diced onion, minced garlic, pineapple chunks with their juice, curry powder, sweet chili sauce, soy sauce, and rice vinegar to the crock pot | Season with salt and pepper to taste | Stir everything together until well combined | Cover and cook on low for 4-6 hours until chicken is tender and cooked through | Stir once halfway through cooking if possible | Taste and adjust seasoning before serving | Serve hot over steamed rice

ingredients: 2 tbsp olive oil, 1 medium onion (diced), 4 cloves garlic (minced), 1 bell pepper (diced), 2 spicy chili peppers (seeded and minced), 2 large tomatoes (chopped), 1/4 cup almond butter, 1 cup chicken broth, 2 tbsp chili powder, 1 tsp ground cinnamon, 1/2 tsp fresh ground black pepper, 1 tsp salt, 60g dark chocolate (70% cocoa, chopped), 4 boneless skinless chicken breasts, fresh cilantro (chopped), lime wedges, diced avocado, diced tomatoes, shredded cabbage for serving
instructions: Place a pan over medium heat and add olive oil | When heated, add diced onion and minced garlic, stirring to soften for 5 minutes | Add spicy chili peppers and chopped tomatoes, stirring to combine | Bring to a simmer and cook for 10 minutes until tomatoes break down | Carefully pour the mixture into a blender | Add almond butter, chicken broth, chili powder, cinnamon, salt, and pepper | Pur?e the mixture until completely smooth | Return the sauce to the pot over medium heat and cook for 15 minutes, stirring occasionally | Add chopped dark chocolate and stir until fully melted and incorporated | Place chicken breasts in a crock pot and pour the mole sauce over them, ensuring they are covered | Cook on low for 8 hours | About 5 hours into cooking, remove the lid and use two forks to shred the chicken as much as possible | Repeat shredding again 1 hour before cooking time is over | Transfer the shredded chicken mole to a serving dish | Serve with fresh cilantro, lime wedges, diced avocado, diced tomatoes, and shredded cabbage on the side

ingredients: 1/2 cup unsalted butter, 1 cup crunchy peanut butter, 2 cups semi-sweet chocolate chips, 2 cups mini marshmallows, 1 tsp vanilla extract
instructions: Butter a 9x13-inch pan generously and set aside | In a large microwave-safe bowl, combine butter, crunchy peanut butter, and chocolate chips | Microwave on high for about 2 1/2 minutes, stopping to stir every 30 seconds, until everything is melted and smooth | Stir very well until fully combined and glossy | Let mixture cool to room temperature ? it should be cool to the touch but still stirrable | Once cooled, gently fold in mini marshmallows until evenly distributed | Pour the mixture into the buttered pan and spread evenly with a spatula | Place in the refrigerator to set for about 30 minutes until firm | Once set, cut into squares or bars | Return cut bars to the refrigerator to keep firm until ready to serve | Store in an airtight container in the refrigerator

ingredients: 1/4 cup all-purpose flour, 1 tsp baking powder, 10 large eggs, 1/4 cup unsalted butter (melted), 1 cup small curd cottage cheese, 2 cups Monterey Jack cheese (shredded), 1 can (200g) diced green chilies, 1/2 tsp salt, 1/4 tsp black pepper
instructions: Preheat oven to 350?F (175?C) | Butter a 9x13 shallow baking dish generously | In a small bowl, mix flour and baking powder together | In a large bowl, beat eggs thoroughly until light and frothy | Add melted butter to the eggs and blend well | Add the flour mixture and blend until smooth | Blend in cottage cheese, shredded Monterey Jack cheese, diced green chilies, salt, and pepper until evenly combined | Pour the mixture into the prepared baking dish | Bake for 35 to 45 minutes or until the frittata is set in the center and golden on top ? a knife inserted in the center should come out clean | Remove from oven and let rest for 5 minutes | Cut into squares and serve very hot

ingredients: 1 cup semi-sweet chocolate chips, 1/4 cup unsalted butter, 3/4 cup granulated sugar, 1 can (354ml) evaporated milk, 1 tsp vanilla extract, pinch of salt
instructions: In a small but heavy saucepan, combine chocolate chips and butter over low heat, stirring constantly until melted and smooth | Add sugar and stir until dissolved | Gradually pour in evaporated milk while stirring continuously to prevent lumps | Bring the mixture to a gentle boil, then slightly reduce heat while maintaining a boil | Continue to boil for another 6-8 minutes, stirring frequently, until the sauce thickens and becomes glossy | Remove from heat and stir in vanilla extract and a pinch of salt | Let cool slightly ? the sauce will continue to thicken as it cools | Serve warm poured generously over vanilla ice cream | Store any leftovers in the refrigerator and reheat gently before serving

ingredients: 1 cup light whipped topping (thawed), 4 oz fat-free cream cheese (softened), 3 tbsp granulated sweetener or sugar, 10 tsp chocolate syrup, 1/2 tsp vanilla extract
instructions: Using a fork, vigorously mix whipped topping, softened cream cheese, sweetener, and vanilla extract in a bowl until completely smooth and well blended ? the mixture should be uniform with no streaks | Evenly distribute the mixture into 10 sections of an ice cube tray, filling each about 3/4 full | Tap the tray firmly on the counter a few times to get the mixture to settle flat and release air bubbles | Top each section with about 1 teaspoon of chocolate syrup | Tap the tray gently again to settle the syrup | Place the tray flat in the freezer until the bites are completely solid ? at least 2 hours | Once frozen, the cheesecake bites should pop out easily by twisting the tray or running a knife around the edges | If they stick, run the bottom of the tray under warm tap water for a few seconds to loosen them | Serve immediately as a frozen treat

ingredients: 2 cups all-purpose flour, 1 tbsp baking powder, 1/2 tsp baking soda, 1 tsp salt, 1 tbsp sugar, 1/2 cup cold unsalted butter (cubed), 3/4 cup cold buttermilk, 2 tbsp melted butter (for brushing)
instructions: Preheat oven to 425?F (220?C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper | In a large bowl, whisk together flour, baking powder, baking soda, salt, and sugar | Add cold cubed butter and cut it in using a pastry cutter or your fingertips until the mixture resembles coarse crumbs with some pea-sized butter pieces remaining | Pour in cold buttermilk and stir gently with a fork just until the dough comes together ? do not overmix | Turn the dough out onto a lightly floured surface and gently pat it into a rectangle about 1-inch thick | Fold the dough in thirds like a letter, then pat out again to 1-inch thickness ? this creates flaky layers | Use a sharp biscuit cutter or glass to cut out rounds, pressing straight down without twisting | Place biscuits on the prepared baking sheet with sides touching for soft edges or spaced apart for crispy edges | Brush the tops with melted butter | Bake for 12-15 minutes until risen and golden brown | Serve warm with butter, jam, or gravy

ingredients: 1 1/2 cups whole wheat flour, 1/2 tsp salt, 2 1/2 tbsp unsweetened cocoa powder (plus extra for drizzle), 1/2 tsp baking soda, 1/2 cup margarine (softened), 3/4 cup granulated sugar, 1/4 cup brown sugar, 1 tsp vanilla extract, 2 tbsp water. For icing: 1/3 cup creamy peanut butter, 1/2 tsp ground cinnamon, 1 tbsp cocoa powder
instructions: Preheat oven to 350?F (175?C) and line a baking sheet with aluminum foil | In a small bowl, combine flour, salt, 2 1/2 tablespoons cocoa powder, and baking soda | In a separate bowl, cream softened margarine with granulated sugar and brown sugar until light and fluffy | Add vanilla extract and water, beating until combined | Gradually beat in the dry ingredient mixture until a soft dough forms | Drop spoonfuls of cookie dough onto the foil-covered baking sheet, spacing them about 2 inches apart | Bake for 8-10 minutes until a toothpick inserted comes out clean ? do not overbake | Transfer cookies to a wire rack to cool completely | Once cookies are fully cooled, make the icing: microwave peanut butter in a small microwave-safe bowl for about 30 seconds until it turns into a liquid consistency | Stir in ground cinnamon and 1 tablespoon cocoa powder until smooth | Transfer the peanut butter mixture into an icing bag or a plastic bag with a tiny piece of the corner snipped off | Drizzle the peanut butter icing in a criss-cross design over the cooled cookies | Let the icing set for 15 minutes before serving

ingredients: 1/4 cup margarine (melted), 2 large eggs, 1 can (425g) canned pumpkin pur?e, 1/2 cup granulated sugar, 1 tsp vanilla extract, 1/2 tsp salt, 1 tsp ground cinnamon, 2 tbsp all-purpose flour, 1 can (354ml) evaporated milk. Topping: 1/4 cup granulated sugar, 1/8 tsp ground cinnamon
instructions: Preheat oven to 450?F (230?C) | Melt 1/4 cup margarine and pour into a casserole or souffl? dish, tilting to coat the bottom and sides | In a large bowl, beat eggs until well combined | Add pumpkin pur?e, sugar, vanilla extract, salt, cinnamon, flour, and evaporated milk to the beaten eggs | Mix well until all ingredients are fully incorporated and smooth | Pour the pumpkin mixture into the buttered casserole dish and spread evenly | In a small bowl, mix together 1/4 cup sugar and 1/8 teaspoon cinnamon for the topping | Sprinkle the cinnamon-sugar mixture evenly over the top of the pumpkin | Bake at 450?F for 25-30 minutes or until the center is set and a knife inserted comes out clean | Remove from oven and let cool slightly before serving | Serve warm as a side dish or light dessert

ingredients: 4 large eggs, 1 egg white, 1/2 cup shredded cheese (mozzarella or Italian blend), 2 tbsp milk, 2 tbsp fresh cilantro or parsley (chopped), 1/4 tsp salt, 1/4 tsp fresh ground black pepper, 300g fresh spinach (about 6 cups), 4 whole wheat tortillas (9-inch), 1/2 cup roasted red peppers (drained and sliced)
instructions: Preheat oven to 350?F (175?C) | Spray a 9-inch round cake pan with cooking spray | Place spinach in a large microwave-safe bowl, cover with plastic wrap, and prick several holes in the plastic with a fork | Microwave on high until the spinach starts to wilt, about 2 minutes | Let stand covered until the spinach wilts completely, about 5 minutes | Uncover and let cool until easy to handle | Squeeze the spinach firmly with your hands to remove as much excess liquid as possible, then chop coarsely | In a bowl, whisk together eggs, egg white, shredded cheese, milk, chopped cilantro or parsley, salt, and ground pepper until well combined | To assemble: place 1 tortilla in the bottom of the prepared cake pan | Layer with half the chopped spinach, then top with a second tortilla and the roasted red peppers | Top with the third tortilla and remaining spinach, then finish with the fourth tortilla | Pour the egg mixture evenly over the top, letting it seep down the sides | Bake for about 20 minutes until firm and set in the center | Remove torta from the oven and increase heat to broil | Broil 5 inches from the heat until just browned on top, about 1 minute ? watch carefully | Let stand for 5 minutes before carefully inverting onto a cutting board | Slice into 4 wedges and serve warm

ingredients: 4 hot dogs, 8 slices bacon, 100g cheddar cheese (cut into 1/4 x 1/4 inch sticks), toothpicks, hot dog buns and desired toppings for serving
instructions: Heat water in a saucepan, add hot dogs, and bring to a boil | Remove pan from heat and let hot dogs sit in the hot water for 5 minutes | Drain hot dogs and when cool enough to handle, split each almost all the way through lengthwise to open like a book ? do not cut completely in half | Cook bacon strips in a frying pan (not microwave) until almost fully cooked but still pliable ? they should not be crispy yet | Cut cheddar cheese into sticks about 1/4 x 1/4 inch thick and the length of the hot dogs | Place two pieces of cheese into the split of each hot dog | Wrap each cheese-stuffed hot dog with 2 slices of bacon, securing with toothpicks at both ends so the hot dog sits upright with the slit facing up | Heat a grill pan over medium heat and place the wrapped hot dogs slit-side up | Cook for a few minutes until the bottom bacon is crisp, then carefully turn over and cook the other side until bacon is crispy all around | Remove toothpicks before serving | Serve in buns with all your favorite fixings

ingredients: 2 cups frozen sweetened strawberries, 1 cup prepared lemonade, 1 cup ice cubes, fresh strawberries for garnish
instructions: Add frozen sweetened strawberries, lemonade, and ice cubes to a blender | Pulse several times to break up the frozen strawberries and ice | Blend on high speed until the mixture is completely smooth and slushy, about 30-45 seconds | If too thick, add a splash more lemonade | If too thin, add a few more ice cubes and blend again | Pour into glasses and garnish with a fresh strawberry on the rim | Serve immediately while icy cold

ingredients: 1 sugar cube, 2 sprigs fresh mint, 120ml well-chilled champagne or sparkling wine, 15ml bourbon (optional), slices of fresh fruit for garnish (peach, strawberry, or orange), crushed ice or clear ice cubes
instructions: Place one sugar cube and two sprigs of fresh mint into a chilled highball glass or traditional julep cup | Muddle the mint and sugar together gently with a muddler or the back of a spoon to release the mint oils | Add two cubes of clear ice or fill the glass with crushed ice | Slowly pour in well-chilled champagne or sparkling wine while stirring constantly to dissolve the sugar | Add a splash of bourbon if desired for extra depth and a true julep character | Garnish with slices of fresh fruit such as peach, strawberry, or orange | Serve immediately

ingredients: 1 cup cornstarch, 1/4 cup low-sodium instant chicken bouillon granules, 2 tsp onion powder, 1 tsp dried basil, 1 tsp dried thyme, 1/2 tsp black pepper
instructions: Combine cornstarch, chicken bouillon granules, onion powder, dried basil, dried thyme, and black pepper in a small mixing bowl | Blend all ingredients together thoroughly until evenly distributed | Transfer the mixture to an airtight container or jar with a tight-fitting lid | Store at room temperature in a cool, dry place for up to 6 months | When ready to use as a substitute for 1 can of cream of chicken soup: combine 1/3 cup of the dry soup mix with 1 1/4 cups water in a small saucepan | Whisk over medium heat until the mixture comes to a boil and thickens, about 3-5 minutes | Use immediately in any recipe calling for canned cream of chicken soup

ingredients: 4 large eggs, 1 cup granulated sugar (divided), 1/4 cup water, 1 cup all-purpose flour, 1 tsp baking powder, 1 tsp vanilla extract, pinch of salt
instructions: Preheat oven to 350?F (175?C) | Line the bottoms of two 9-inch cake pans with waxed paper or parchment paper ? do not grease the pans | Separate egg yolks from whites if desired, or use the whole-egg method: beat eggs in a large mixing bowl on high speed until thick and lemon-colored, about 3-4 minutes | Gradually add 1/2 cup of the sugar while continuing to beat for 4 more minutes until the mixture is very thick and forms a ribbon when the beater is lifted | Gradually add the remaining 1/2 cup sugar, beating continuously | Stir in water and vanilla extract | In a separate bowl, sift together flour and baking powder | Gradually fold the flour mixture into the egg mixture on low speed of an electric mixer, just until incorporated ? do not overmix | Divide batter evenly between the two prepared pans | Bake for 20 to 25 minutes until the cake springs back when lightly touched and edges begin to pull away from the sides | Remove from oven and immediately invert pans onto wire racks ? let cakes cool completely upside down in the pans before removing | Once cooled, run a knife around the edges, remove cakes from pans, and peel off the waxed paper | Frost or fill as desired

ingredients: 1 green bell pepper (chopped), 1 medium onion (chopped), 3 cloves garlic (minced), 500g ground beef, 1 can (400g) chili beans (with liquid), 1 can (400g) diced tomatoes, 1 can (400g) tomato sauce, 1 tsp seasoned salt, 1 tsp garlic powder, 1/2 tsp black pepper, 1 tbsp chili powder, 1/2 tsp ground cumin, shredded cheddar cheese and crackers for serving
instructions: In a large saucepan or Dutch oven, combine chopped green pepper, chopped onion, minced garlic, and ground beef | Cook over medium to medium-high heat, breaking up the meat with a wooden spoon, until the beef is browned through and vegetables are softened, about 8-10 minutes | Drain any excess fat from the pan | Add chili beans (with their liquid), diced tomatoes (with their juices), and tomato sauce | Add seasoned salt, garlic powder, black pepper, chili powder, and cumin | Mix all ingredients together thoroughly | Bring to a simmer, then cover and reduce heat to low | Simmer for 30 minutes, stirring every 10 minutes to prevent sticking | Taste and adjust seasonings ? add more chili powder for heat or salt to taste | Serve hot in bowls topped with shredded cheddar cheese and crackers on the side

ingredients: For dry rub: 1/4 cup brown sugar, 1 tbsp dry mustard, 1 tsp cayenne pepper, 1 tbsp paprika, 1 tbsp garlic powder, 1 tbsp onion powder, 1 tbsp salt, 1 tsp fresh ground black pepper. For sauce: 1 tbsp vegetable oil, 1 small onion (diced), 1 cup ketchup, 1/3 cup water, 2 tbsp tomato paste, 1/4 cup brown sugar, 1/4 cup apple cider vinegar, 2 tbsp molasses, 1/2 tsp cayenne pepper, salt and black pepper to taste. 2 racks pork spare ribs
instructions: Prepare the dry rub: remove the thin white membrane from the bone-side of the ribs by loosening a corner with a knife and pulling it off with a paper towel for better grip | In a small bowl, mix together brown sugar, dry mustard, cayenne, paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, salt, and pepper | Massage the dry rub thoroughly into both sides of the ribs | Let ribs sit for at least 1 hour at room temperature or overnight in the refrigerator | Make the Kansas City barbecue sauce: heat vegetable oil in a small saucepan over medium-high heat | Add diced onion and cook until translucent, about 3-4 minutes | In a bowl, combine ketchup, water, tomato paste, brown sugar, apple cider vinegar, molasses, cayenne, salt, and pepper | Add mixture to the saucepan with the onions, stir, and let simmer for 30 to 45 minutes until thickened and flavors meld, stirring occasionally ? makes about 3 cups of sauce | For grilling: place ribs meat-side down next to medium-hot coals at about 225?F using indirect heat | Cook for 1 hour, then turn ribs every half hour, basting with sauce each time | Cook until ribs are tender, about 3 to 4 hours total | For oven cooking: preheat oven to 350?F (175?C) | Place ribs on a rack in a roasting pan, slather with sauce, and tent with aluminum foil | Bake, basting with sauce every 30 minutes and removing the foil for the final 30 minutes | Cook until fork-tender, about 2 1/2 to 3 hours | Let ribs rest for 10 minutes before slicing between the bones | Serve with remaining sauce on the side

ingredients: 3 tbsp butter, 3 tbsp all-purpose flour, 2 cups whole milk, 1/2 cup Parmesan cheese (grated), 1/2 cup American cheese (shredded), 1/2 cup Colby cheese (shredded), 2 egg yolks, 1/4 tsp hot sauce, 4 thick slices bread (toasted), 200g sliced cooked chicken or turkey, 200g sliced ham, 2 medium tomatoes (sliced), 8 slices bacon (cooked crisp), 1/2 tsp paprika
instructions: Preheat oven to 400?F (200?C) | In a heavy 4-quart saucepan, melt butter over medium heat | Whisk in flour and cook until smooth and bubbling, about 1 minute | Slowly add milk, whisking constantly, and continue cooking until thickened and smooth, about 3-4 minutes | Add hot sauce and grated Parmesan cheese, then remove from heat | Place 1/2 cup of the sauce in a small bowl and set the remaining sauce aside | Whisk egg yolks into the 1/2 cup of reserved sauce, mixing well | Stir the egg mixture back into the main saucepan of sauce and return to heat, stirring constantly (do not let it boil or the eggs may curdle) | Add shredded Colby and American cheeses, stirring until fully melted and smooth | Remove from heat | Place toasted bread slices on individual heat-resistant plates or in oven-safe dishes | Cover each slice of bread with slices of chicken or turkey and ham | Pour a generous amount of cheese sauce over each serving, covering completely | Top each with a tomato slice and two pieces of crispy bacon | Sprinkle paprika over the top | Bake for 10 to 15 minutes until bubbly and lightly browned on top | Serve immediately while hot

ingredients: 3 cups water (for infusing), 1/4 cup fresh ginger (peeled and thinly sliced), 1/3 cup honey or pure maple syrup, 2 tbsp molasses, 1/4 cup fresh lemon juice, 2 tbsp apple cider vinegar, 6 cups cold water, fresh berries, mint sprigs, and lemon slices for garnish, ice cubes for serving
instructions: Combine 3 cups water with sliced fresh ginger in a small saucepan | Bring to a boil over medium-high heat and boil for 2 minutes | Remove from heat, cover, and let the ginger infuse for 15 minutes | Strain the ginger-infused water through a fine mesh sieve into a large pitcher, pressing on the ginger solids to extract all the liquid | Add honey or maple syrup and molasses to the warm liquid, stirring until completely dissolved | Stir in fresh lemon juice, apple cider vinegar, and the remaining 6 cups of cold water | Chill until very cold, at least 2 hours or overnight | Stir the switchel well and serve in tall glasses over ice cubes | Garnish with fresh berries, mint sprigs, or lemon slices if desired | Can be covered and refrigerated for up to 2 days

ingredients: 1/2 cup brown sugar (packed), 1/4 cup unsalted butter, 2 tbsp corn syrup, 1 large apple (peeled and finely chopped), 1 can refrigerated biscuits (8 count), 1/4 cup granulated sugar mixed with 1 tsp ground cinnamon
