instructions: Preheat oven to 375?F (190?C) | In a deep dish baker or oven-safe skillet, melt butter, brown sugar, and corn syrup together over medium heat, stirring until smooth and bubbly | Remove from heat and sprinkle the finely chopped apple evenly over the caramel mixture in the bottom of the dish | Separate the biscuits and coat each one generously in the cinnamon-sugar mixture, pressing gently to adhere | Arrange the coated biscuits on top of the apples in a single layer, with biscuits touching slightly | Bake for 18 to 20 minutes until the biscuits are golden brown and the caramel is bubbling around the edges | Remove from oven and let cool for 2-3 minutes | Carefully invert the dish onto a serving plate so the caramel apple topping is on top | Serve warm

ingredients: 300g cooked baby shrimp, 1 cup green seedless grapes (halved), 2 celery stalks (diced), 1/2 cup sliced almonds (toasted), 1 can (200g) water chestnuts (drained and chopped), 1 can (200g) lychees (drained and halved), 1 cup fresh pineapple (diced), 4 large lettuce leaves. For dressing: 1/3 cup mayonnaise, 1 tbsp honey, 1 tbsp reduced-sodium soy sauce, 1 tsp mild curry powder, 2 tbsp fresh lime juice
instructions: In a large bowl, mix together cooked shrimp, halved grapes, diced celery, toasted almonds, chopped water chestnuts, and halved lychees | Gently stir in diced fresh pineapple, being careful not to break up the fruit | In a separate small bowl, whisk together mayonnaise, honey, soy sauce, curry powder, and fresh lime juice until smooth and well combined | Pour the dressing over the salad and toss gently to coat all ingredients evenly | Set out 4 serving plates and line each with a clean crisp lettuce leaf | Portion the salad into neat mounds on top of the lettuce leaves | Drizzle any remaining dressing from the bowl over each serving | Serve immediately with extra dressing on the side

ingredients: 2 tbsp reduced-sodium soy sauce, 2 tbsp cold water, 1 tbsp cornstarch, 1 tsp sambal oelek (chili paste), 400g boneless pork loin chops (cut into thin strips), 1 tsp vegetable oil, 1 green onion (sliced), 3 cloves garlic (minced), 1 carrot (julienned), 100g fresh mushrooms (sliced), 1 tbsp fresh ginger (grated), 1 can (300g) mandarin oranges in light syrup (drained), 2 packs ramen noodles, 2 tsp sesame oil, 1 tbsp toasted sesame seeds
instructions: In a small bowl, whisk together soy sauce, cold water, cornstarch, and sambal oelek until smooth; set aside | Coat a cool nonstick wok with cooking spray and preheat over high heat | Add 1 teaspoon vegetable oil | When oil is hot, add pork strips and stir-fry for 3-4 minutes until browned and cooked through, stirring constantly | Remove pork from wok and set aside | Add sliced green onion, minced garlic, and julienned carrot to the wok and cook for 2-3 minutes until vegetables are crisp-tender, stirring constantly | Add sliced mushrooms and cook an additional 2-3 minutes, stirring constantly | Return the cooked pork back to the wok | Stir the soy sauce mixture well and pour it over the ingredients in the wok | Add grated ginger and stir constantly for 1 minute until the sauce thickens and bubbles | Add drained mandarin oranges and toss gently to coat without breaking them | Cook ramen noodles according to package directions, drain, and toss with sesame oil | Serve the stir-fry over the sesame noodles and garnish with toasted sesame seeds

ingredients: 4 boneless skinless chicken breasts, 2 cans (400g each) cream of chicken soup, 1 cup sour cream, 2 tbsp poppy seeds, 2 sleeves Ritz crackers (crushed), 1/2 cup unsalted butter (melted), salt and pepper to taste
instructions: Preheat oven to 350?F (175?C) | Place chicken breasts in a pan and cover with water | Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer until tender and no longer pink, about 10 minutes | Once cool enough to handle, cut chicken into bite-size pieces | In a 13x9-inch rectangular pan, mix the two cans of cream of chicken soup with sour cream until smooth and well combined | Sprinkle the cut chicken evenly over the soup mixture | Place Ritz crackers in a large plastic bag and gently crush them with a rolling pin until coarse crumbs form | Add poppy seeds to the bag and shake to combine | Pour melted butter into the bag and shake again until the crumbs are evenly coated | Sprinkle the buttery cracker mixture evenly over the chicken and soup layer | Bake for 30-40 minutes until the casserole begins to bubble around the edges and the crackers are golden brown | Let rest for 5 minutes before serving

ingredients: 1 large head green cabbage, 500g ground beef, 1 large egg, 1/4 cup fresh parsley (chopped), 1 medium onion (finely diced), 3 cloves garlic (minced), 1 cup cooked white rice, 1 tsp salt, 1/2 tsp black pepper, 2 cans (400g each) tomato soup, 2 tbsp sugar, 2 tbsp white vinegar, 1/2 cup water
instructions: Bring a large pot of water to a boil | Carefully place the whole head of cabbage in the boiling water and boil for 10-15 minutes until outer leaves are softened | Remove cabbage and let cool slightly, then carefully peel off the leaves one at a time, keeping them intact | In a large bowl, mix ground beef, egg, chopped parsley, diced onion, minced garlic, cooked rice, salt, and pepper until well combined | Take a portion of the meat mixture and form it into an oval-shaped ball | Place each meatball near the base of a cabbage leaf, fold the sides inward, and roll up tightly | Line the bottom of a 5-quart Dutch oven with any torn or extra cabbage leaves to prevent sticking | Arrange the cabbage rolls seam-side down in the pot in snug layers | In a separate bowl, mix together tomato soup, sugar, vinegar, and water until smooth | Pour the tomato mixture over the cabbage rolls, covering them completely | Cover the pot and cook over medium heat for 1 hour and 30 minutes, checking occasionally to ensure the liquid is simmering gently | Serve hot with a spoonful of the tomato sauce from the pot

ingredients: 1 tbsp sesame oil, 2 tbsp fresh ginger (grated), 1 red chili (finely chopped), 3 tbsp soy sauce, 3 tbsp honey, 2 tbsp dry sherry, 2 boneless pork fillets (about 300g each, halved), steamed white rice and green vegetables for serving
instructions: Place sesame oil, grated ginger, and chopped chili in a frying pan over high heat and cook for 1 minute until fragrant | Add soy sauce, honey, and dry sherry, stirring to combine, and cook for 2 minutes until the sauce is bubbling and slightly thickened | Cut each pork fillet in half crosswise to create 4 portions | Add the pork pieces to the pan, turning to coat them in the sauce | Reduce heat to medium and cook the pork in the pan sauce for 10-15 minutes, turning occasionally, until cooked to your liking and the sauce is thick and caramelized | If the sauce reduces too quickly, add a splash of water | Remove pork from the pan and let rest for 2-3 minutes before slicing | Slice the pork and arrange on serving plates | Spoon the remaining caramelized pan sauce over the top | Serve with plain steamed white rice and stir-fried or steamed green vegetables

ingredients: 3 cups all-purpose flour, 2 cups granulated sugar, 1 tsp baking soda, 1/2 tsp salt, 1 package unsweetened drink powder (such as Kool-Aid, for flavored cake), 1 cup vegetable shortening. For baking: 1 package cake mix (about 1/3 cup), 4 tsp water, 1/4 tsp vanilla extract (for white cake)
instructions: In a medium bowl, combine flour, sugar, baking soda, salt, and drink powder (if making flavored cake) | Stir with a wire whisk until thoroughly blended | Using a pastry blender or two knives, cut in vegetable shortening until evenly distributed and the mixture resembles coarse cornmeal | Spoon about 1/3 cup of the mix into each of 10 small containers or Ziploc bags | Seal containers tightly and label with date and contents | Store in a cool, dry place and use within 12 weeks | Makes 10 individual packages of cake mix | To use one package: if using a child's play oven, follow manufacturer's directions, or preheat a standard oven to 375?F (190?C) | Grease and flour a 4-inch miniature cake pan | In a small bowl, combine 1 package cake mix and 4 teaspoons water (add a drop of vanilla for white cake) | Stir with a fork or spoon until blended and smooth | Pour mixture into the prepared pan | Bake for 12 to 13 minutes in a standard oven or as directed for a play oven | Remove from oven and cool in pan on a wire rack for 5 minutes | Invert cake onto a small plate and remove the pan | Cool completely before frosting if desired | Serves 2 children

ingredients: 4 salmon steaks or fillets (about 150g each), 1 tsp garlic powder, 1/2 tsp salt, 1/4 tsp black pepper, 2 tbsp extra virgin olive oil, 3 tbsp fresh lime juice, 1/4 cup fresh cilantro (chopped), 1 tsp sugar or sugar substitute, lime wedges for serving
instructions: Sprinkle garlic powder, salt, and black pepper evenly over the top of each salmon steak or fillet | In a small bowl, whisk together olive oil, fresh lime juice, chopped cilantro, and sugar (or sugar substitute) until well combined | Place salmon in a nonstick skillet over medium-high heat, seasoned side down | Cook for 4-5 minutes until the bottom is golden and the salmon is about halfway cooked through | Turn the salmon over and pour the cilantro-lime mixture evenly over the top | Continue cooking for another 4-5 minutes until the salmon is cooked through and flakes easily with a fork | Spoon any pan sauce over the salmon before serving | Serve immediately with lime wedges on the side

ingredients: 400g spaghetti, 4 ripe tomatoes (chopped), 2 cups fresh arugula (roughly chopped), 1/4 cup fresh basil (torn), 1 tsp dried oregano, 1/4 cup Kalamata olives (pitted and sliced), 3 tbsp olive oil, 1 tbsp red wine vinegar, salt and black pepper to taste, Parmesan cheese for serving, crusty Italian bread for serving
instructions: Bring a large pan of generously salted water to a boil | Add spaghetti and cook until al dente, approximately 10 minutes | While pasta cooks, prepare the sauce: chop tomatoes into bite-size chunks, roughly chop fresh arugula, tear basil leaves, and slice olives ? whatever size and shape you prefer | Place chopped tomatoes, arugula, basil, and olives in individual serving bowls | Add olive oil, red wine vinegar, salt, and black pepper to each bowl | Taste and adjust seasoning until the balance is right | The pasta should be ready by now ? drain the spaghetti quickly, reserving a splash of pasta water | Immediately add the hot drained spaghetti to the serving bowls over the fresh ingredients | Stir everything together thoroughly ? the heat from the pasta will slightly wilt the arugula and release the tomato and herb flavors | Serve immediately with freshly grated Parmesan cheese and warm crusty Italian bread on the side | Any type of pasta can be used, though spaghetti works beautifully

ingredients: For crust: 1/2 cup unsalted butter (softened), 1/4 cup granulated sugar, 1 tbsp honey, 1/4 tsp salt, 2 large egg yolks, 1 1/4 cups all-purpose flour. For filling: 1 can (400g) sweetened condensed milk, 1/2 cup sour cream, 1/2 cup key lime juice, 1 tbsp lime zest, 3 large egg yolks, 1 tbsp honey. For topping: whipped cream, tuile cookies (optional)
instructions: Make the short dough crust: cream butter with sugar, honey, and salt until uniform | Add egg yolks one at a time until completely mixed | Add flour and mix just until incorporated ? do not overmix | Roll out the dough on a lightly floured surface, then cover and chill for 3-4 hours until very firm and easy to handle | Preheat oven to 350?F (175?C) | Press chilled dough into a 9-inch pie pan and trim edges | Bake the crust for 15 minutes until lightly golden | Make the filling: in a bowl, gently fold together sweetened condensed milk, sour cream, key lime juice, lime zest, egg yolks, and honey until smooth and well combined ? do not overbeat | Pour filling into the pre-baked crust | Bake for about 8 minutes until the filling is just set but still slightly wobbly in the center | Remove from oven and let cool completely, then refrigerate for at least 2 hours until fully set | Top with whipped cream and tuile cookies for decoration if desired | Slice and serve chilled

ingredients: 2 tbsp olive oil (divided), 2 green bell peppers (diced), 1 red bell pepper (diced), 2 medium onions (diced), 1 tsp salt (divided), 1/2 tsp black pepper, 500g ground pork, 3 cloves garlic (minced), 2 tbsp tomato paste, 1 tsp dried oregano, 1/2 cup Parmesan cheese (grated, divided), 2 tbsp unsalted butter, 2 tbsp all-purpose flour, 2 cups whole milk, 2 large eggs, 2 cups cooked long-grain rice
instructions: Heat 1 tablespoon olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat | Add diced peppers and onions, 1/2 teaspoon salt, and black pepper | Saut? until vegetables are just softened, about 10 minutes | Remove vegetables and set aside | Heat remaining 1 tablespoon oil in the same skillet over medium heat | Add ground pork and minced garlic | Cook, stirring to break up lumps, until meat loses all trace of pink, about 10 minutes | Add tomato paste, oregano, black pepper, remaining 1/2 teaspoon salt, and 1/4 cup of the Parmesan cheese | Stir well, remove from heat, and set aside | Preheat oven to 350?F (175?C) | Melt butter in a medium saucepan over medium heat | Stir in flour and reduce heat to medium-low, cooking and stirring constantly for 3 minutes | Increase heat to medium and whisk in milk | Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low and simmer, stirring frequently, until mixture is thickened and smooth, about 5 minutes | In a small bowl, beat eggs lightly | Gradually whisk about 1/2 cup of the hot milk mixture into the eggs, then gradually whisk the egg mixture back into the remaining milk mixture | Stir in 1/4 cup Parmesan cheese and season with salt and pepper to taste | Spread cooked rice in the bottom of a greased 1 1/2-quart casserole or 8-inch square baking pan | Spread a few spoonfuls of sauce over the rice | Spoon the vegetable mixture over the rice, then spoon the pork mixture over the vegetables | Pour the remaining sauce over the top and sprinkle with remaining cheese | Bake until the top is puffed and golden, about 1 hour | Let rest for 10 minutes before slicing and serving

ingredients: 500g boneless skinless chicken breasts (diced into cubes), juice of 1/2 lemon, 2 tbsp vegetable oil, 4 cloves garlic (minced), 1 serrano pepper (minced), 1 medium onion (diced), 2 tbsp curry powder, 1 tbsp Thai red curry paste, salt and pepper to taste, fresh cilantro for garnish, steamed rice for serving
instructions: Butterfly the chicken breasts first to make them thinner, then cut into bite-size cubes | Rinse chicken under cold water and drain well | Squeeze the juice of half a lemon over the chicken and set aside | In a saut? pan over medium heat, warm vegetable oil | Saut? minced garlic, minced serrano pepper, and diced onion for about 2 minutes or until softened and fragrant | Add curry powder to the pan and cook for 2 more minutes, stirring constantly to bloom the spices | Add Thai red curry paste and stir in well, cooking for a few more minutes until the paste is evenly distributed | Add the diced chicken along with the lemon juice to the curry mixture | Stir until chicken is completely coated with the curry | Saut? for 10-12 minutes, stirring occasionally, until chicken is fully cooked through | Season with salt and pepper to taste | Serve hot over steamed rice and garnish generously with fresh cilantro

ingredients: 2 beef steaks (filet mignon or ribeye, about 200g each), salt and black pepper, 8 jumbo shrimp (peeled and deveined, tails on), 200g lump crabmeat (checked for shells), 3 tbsp butter, 3 cloves garlic (minced), 2 tbsp fresh lemon juice, 1/3 cup dry white wine. For bearnaise sauce: 2 egg yolks, 1 tbsp lemon juice, 1/2 cup melted butter, 1 tbsp fresh tarragon, salt
instructions: Season steaks generously with salt and pepper on both sides | Allow steaks to sit at room temperature for at least 30 minutes before cooking | Prepare bearnaise sauce: whisk egg yolks and lemon juice in a double boiler until thick, then slowly drizzle in melted butter while whisking constantly until emulsified | Stir in fresh tarragon and season with salt, then set aside and keep warm | Ensure shrimp are peeled and deveined with tails left on | Check crabmeat carefully for any bits of shell | Grill or broil steaks to just under desired doneness, allowing for warming time while preparing the topping | In a saut? pan, heat butter and minced garlic over medium-high heat | Add prepared shrimp and lemon juice, saut? for 2 minutes | Add white wine and crabmeat, saut? until wine has reduced and shrimp are no longer pink, about 2-3 more minutes | Spread about 1/4 cup bearnaise sauce on each serving plate | Place steaks on the sauce and top generously with the shrimp and crab mixture | Double the ingredients for 4 servings | Serve immediately

ingredients: 1 medium onion (diced), 1 Granny Smith apple (peeled and diced), 2 cups cooked ham (diced), 1 tsp dry mustard, 2 cans (400g each) baked beans, 1/4 cup chili sauce, 2 tbsp brown sugar, 1 tbsp Worcestershire sauce
instructions: Preheat oven to 350?F (175?C) | Combine diced onion, diced apple, diced ham, dry mustard, baked beans, chili sauce, brown sugar, and Worcestershire sauce in a 1 1/2-quart buttered casserole dish | Stir everything together until well mixed | Cover the dish with a lid or foil | Bake for 45 to 60 minutes or until the mixture is hot and bubbly throughout | Remove cover during the last 10 minutes if you prefer a slightly thicker consistency | Serve hot as a hearty side dish

ingredients: 4 shortcake cups (store-bought or homemade), 1 cup fresh strawberries (sliced), 4 large marshmallows, chocolate sauce for drizzling (optional)
instructions: Fill two shortcake cups with sliced fresh strawberries, mounding them slightly | Roast marshmallows over an open flame or under a broiler until golden brown and gooey, watching carefully | Quickly assemble: top the strawberries with one or two hot roasted marshmallows | Invert the remaining shortcake cups so the cup side is facing down and place on top of the marshmallows, pressing down gently | The heat from the marshmallows will warm the strawberries slightly | Drizzle with chocolate sauce if desired | Serve immediately while the marshmallows are still warm and gooey

ingredients: 3 tbsp olive oil, 1 medium onion (diced), 1 tsp dried oregano or Greek seasoning, 4 large pita breads (cut into 1-inch pieces and toasted), 1 cup reduced-sodium chicken broth, 1/2 cup ready-made bruschetta spread, 1/4 cup Kalamata black olives (sliced), 1 tbsp fresh lemon juice, 1/4 cup Italian parsley (chopped), salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Preheat oven to 400?F (200?C) | Place pita bread pieces in a single layer on a large sheet pan and bake for 5 to 8 minutes until lightly toasted | Meanwhile, heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat | Add diced onion and cook, stirring, until lightly browned, about 5 minutes | Add oregano or Greek seasoning, toasted pita bread, and chicken broth | Stir until the bread is uniformly moistened and the broth is mostly absorbed | Stir in bruschetta spread, sliced olives, lemon juice, salt, pepper, and chopped parsley | Heat through, stirring gently to combine all ingredients | Keep warm or reheat immediately before serving | Serve as a flavorful stuffing alongside roasted meats or as a standalone side dish

ingredients: For dough: 1 cup warm milk, 2 large eggs, 1/3 cup margarine (softened), 4 cups all-purpose flour, 1 tsp salt, 1/2 cup white sugar, 2 1/4 tsp active dry yeast. For filling: 1 cup brown sugar (packed), 2 tbsp ground cinnamon, 1/3 cup margarine (softened). For icing: 4 oz cream cheese (softened), 1/4 cup margarine (softened), 1 1/2 cups icing sugar, 1/2 tsp vanilla extract, pinch of salt
instructions: Place all dough ingredients into a mixing bowl and mix until a smooth dough forms ? using a dough hook with a stand mixer works best, or knead by hand for 8-10 minutes | Cover dough and set aside in a draft-free area and allow to double in size, about 1 hour | In a small bowl, combine brown sugar and cinnamon for the filling, mixing well | After dough has doubled, punch it down and roll out on a lightly floured surface into a 16x21 inch rectangle | Spread softened margarine over the dough, then sprinkle the cinnamon-brown sugar filling evenly across the entire surface | Starting from the long edge, roll up the dough tightly into a log | Cut the log into 12 equal buns using a sharp knife or dental floss | Place buns cut-side up in a greased 9x13 baking pan, spacing them slightly apart | Cover and let rise until doubled, about 30-45 minutes | Preheat oven to 400?F (200?C) | Place buns in the oven and bake for approximately 15 minutes until golden brown | While buns are baking, beat together cream cheese, softened margarine, icing sugar, vanilla, and a pinch of salt until smooth to make the icing | Spread the icing generously over warm buns immediately after removing from the oven | Serve warm ? leftovers reheat nicely in the microwave

ingredients: 1 cup fresh parsley (finely chopped), 1/2 cup water, 1/2 cup unsalted butter, 1/4 tsp salt, pinch of white pepper, 1 tsp lemon juice (optional)
instructions: Bring water to a boil in a small saucepan | Add finely chopped parsley and cook for 2-3 minutes until the parsley is bright green and tender | Do not drain ? the water should be mostly absorbed | Add butter and stir gently until completely melted and hot throughout | Season with salt and a pinch of white pepper | Add a squeeze of fresh lemon juice if desired for brightness | Serve immediately as a warm sauce over fish, boiled potatoes, or vegetables

ingredients: 1 unbaked 9-inch pie crust, 8 oz cream cheese (softened), 4 large eggs (divided), 1 tsp vanilla extract, 1 1/2 cups pecan halves, 3/4 cup corn syrup, 1/2 cup brown sugar (packed)
instructions: Prepare or thaw pie crust according to package directions for a one-crust pie | Preheat oven to 425?F (220?C) | Beat softened cream cheese, 1 egg, and vanilla extract until smooth and creamy | Spread the cream cheese mixture evenly in the bottom of the pie shell | Sprinkle pecan halves evenly over the cream cheese layer | In a separate bowl, beat the remaining 3 eggs with corn syrup and brown sugar until well combined and smooth | Pour the egg mixture evenly over the pecans | Bake in the preheated oven for 10 minutes | Reduce heat to 375?F (190?C) and continue baking for 25-30 minutes longer until the filling is set in the center and the top is golden | Cool completely on a wire rack before slicing ? the cheesecake layer needs time to set | Refrigerate for at least 2 hours before serving for cleanest slices

ingredients: 1 cup sour cream, 1/4 tsp salt, 1/4 tsp fresh ground black pepper, 2 tbsp fresh dill (chopped), 1 tsp lemon zest, 1 tbsp fresh lemon juice, 1/2 tsp sugar (adjust to taste)
instructions: Combine sour cream, salt, black pepper, chopped fresh dill, lemon zest, and lemon juice in a mixing bowl | Stir everything together until well blended | Before adding sugar, taste the sauce ? the natural sweetness of the sour cream and dill may be sufficient | Add sugar a little at a time to suit your taste, balancing the tangy and sweet flavors | Cover and refrigerate until ready to serve, at least 30 minutes for the flavors to meld | Serve chilled as a dipping sauce for vegetables, a topping for fish, or alongside potatoes

ingredients: For crust: 1 1/2 cups whole wheat pastry flour, 1/2 tsp salt, 1/3 cup vegetable oil, 3 tbsp cold water, 1 egg white (for brushing). For filling: 6 medium apples (peeled, cored, and sliced), 1 tbsp lemon juice, 1 tbsp lemon zest, 1 tsp ground cinnamon, 1/4 tsp ground nutmeg, 1/4 tsp ground coriander, 1/4 cup apple juice concentrate, 1/4 tsp cream of tartar. For meringue: 2 egg whites, 1/2 tsp lemon zest, 1/4 tsp cream of tartar
instructions: Sift flour and salt together in a large bowl | Stir in vegetable oil and cold water, mixing until a dough forms | Knead dough 3-4 times until moist and elastic, then form into a ball | Cover and refrigerate for 10 minutes | Place chilled dough between 2 sheets of wax paper and roll into a 12-inch circle | Carefully transfer to an 8-inch pie plate, trim edges, and press with a fork to crimp | Poke a few holes in the bottom of the pie shell with a fork | Brush the crust with beaten egg white and bake at 350?F (175?C) for 5 minutes, then remove from oven | While crust bakes, peel, core, and slice apples | Drop apple slices into a bowl of cold water with 1 tablespoon lemon juice to prevent browning | Drain and pat dry before using | Mix apple slices with half the lemon zest, cinnamon, nutmeg, coriander, and apple juice concentrate | Turn the apple mixture into the pre-baked pie shell | Bake at 350?F for 12-15 minutes until apples are tender | While pie bakes, whip 2 egg whites until stiff peaks form | Add remaining lemon zest and cream of tartar, continuing to beat until thick and glossy | Remove pie from oven, pile the meringue on top in decorative swirls, and sprinkle with remaining lemon zest | Return to oven and bake for 5-7 minutes longer or until meringue is golden brown | Cool before slicing

ingredients: 500g lump crabmeat, 2 large eggs, 1/4 cup mayonnaise, 1 tsp Worcestershire sauce, 1 tsp Dijon mustard, 1/2 tsp baking powder, 1 cup panko breadcrumbs, 2 tbsp fresh parsley (chopped), 1 tsp Old Bay seasoning, lemon wedges for serving
instructions: Preheat oven to 350?F (175?C) and spray a baking sheet with non-stick spray | In a large bowl, mix together eggs, mayonnaise, Worcestershire sauce, Dijon mustard, baking powder, panko breadcrumbs, chopped parsley, and Old Bay seasoning until well combined | Gently fold in the lump crabmeat, being very careful not to break up the lumps ? the cakes should have visible chunks of crab | Form the mixture into cakes using a 2-tablespoon measuring spoon to scoop out heaping portions, gently shaping into patties about 2 1/2 inches in diameter | Place formed crab cakes on the prepared baking sheet, spacing them slightly apart | Bake for 15 minutes or until golden on top and cooked through | Serve immediately with lemon wedges and tartar sauce or remoulade on the side

ingredients: 2 tbsp olive oil, 2 tbsp all-purpose flour, 2 tsp Cajun seasoning, 2 cups bottled clam juice, 1 can (400g) diced tomatoes with sweet onions, 3 cups fresh spinach leaves, 1 tbsp fresh thyme leaves, 2 cloves garlic (minced), 250g lump crabmeat, salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Whisk olive oil and flour together in a heavy large saucepan over medium-high heat until smooth and golden brown, about 3 minutes | Add Cajun seasoning to taste and stir for 30 seconds until fragrant | Add clam juice and stir until smooth and well incorporated | Add diced tomatoes with their juices | Reduce heat to medium-low and simmer for 3 minutes | Add fresh spinach, thyme leaves, and minced garlic | Simmer until spinach is just wilted, about 1 minute | Gently add lump crabmeat and simmer until heated through, about 1-2 minutes, stirring very gently to avoid breaking up the crab | Season to taste with salt and black pepper | Ladle soup into warm bowls and serve immediately

ingredients: 2 cups almond flour, 1 cup granulated sugar, 2 large egg whites, 1 tsp almond extract, 1/4 cup whole amarena cherries in syrup (drained), powdered sugar for dusting
instructions: Preheat oven to 300?F (150?C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper or a silicone mat | In a mixing bowl, stir together sugar and egg whites until the sugar has mostly dissolved | Stir in almond flour and almond extract ? this mixture is very thick and may be too tough for a hand mixer; use a rubber spatula or pulse in a food processor until the dough is evenly mixed | Spoon the mixture into a cookie press to shape small round cookies, or use a small ice cream scoop to form little balls | Place cookies about 1/2 inch apart on the prepared baking sheet | Gently press one amarena cherry into the center of each cookie | Bake for approximately 30 minutes on the lowest rack setting for the first 10 minutes, then move to the middle rack | Cookies are done when they start to turn lightly golden around the edges | Remove from oven and let cool on the baking sheet ? they will be slightly chewy right after baking but will become very crisp as they cool overnight | Dust with powdered sugar before serving | Store in an airtight container

ingredients: 2 cups almond flour, 1 cup granulated sugar, 2 large egg whites, 1 tsp almond extract, 1/4 cup whole amarena cherries (drained), powdered sugar for dusting
instructions: Stir together sugar and egg whites in a mixing bowl until the sugar has mostly dissolved | Stir in almond flour and almond extract ? this mixture is very thick and may be too tough for a hand mixer; use a rubber spatula, a food processor, or mix thoroughly by hand until the dough is evenly combined | Spoon the mixture into a cookie press to shape small round cookies, or use a small ice cream scoop to form little balls | Place cookies about 1/2 inch apart on a greased cookie sheet or silicone mat | Gently press one amarena cherry into the center of each cookie | Bake for approximately 30 minutes at 300?F, placing on the lowest rack setting for the first 10 minutes | Cookies are done when they start to turn lightly golden around the edges | Remove from oven and let cool on the baking sheet ? they will be slightly chewy right after baking but will become very crisp overnight | Dust with powdered sugar before serving | Store in an airtight container

ingredients: 1 unbaked 9-inch pie crust, 1 cup light corn syrup, 3/4 cup granulated sugar, 1/4 cup unsalted butter (melted), 1 tsp vanilla extract, 3 large eggs, 1 cup semi-sweet chocolate chips, 1 1/2 cups pecan halves (plus extra for garnish), whipped topping for serving
instructions: Preheat oven to 325?F (160?C) and place pie crust in a 9-inch pie plate | In a large bowl, combine corn syrup, sugar, melted butter, vanilla, and eggs ? beat well until smooth and fully combined | Stir in chocolate chips and pecan halves until evenly distributed | Pour the filling into the unbaked pie crust, spreading evenly | Bake at 325?F for 55 to 65 minutes until the filling is set and deep golden brown ? the center should have a slight jiggle but not be liquid | Cool for 1 hour or until completely cool to room temperature | Top with whipped topping and garnish with additional pecan halves if desired | Keep refrigerated until ready to serve | Slice and serve chilled or at room temperature

ingredients: For apple mixture: 3 tbsp butter, 2 medium apples (peeled and diced), 1 tsp ground cinnamon. For dry ingredients: 1 cup all-purpose flour, 1 cup whole wheat flour, 1/2 cup rolled oats, 2 tsp baking powder, 1/2 tsp baking soda, 1 cup Swiss cheese (diced). For wet ingredients: 1/2 cup unsalted butter (softened), 3/4 cup brown sugar, 2 large eggs, 3/4 cup milk, 1 tsp vanilla extract
instructions: Preheat oven to 375?F (190?C) | Butter and flour a loaf pan, or line with parchment paper | In a frying pan over medium heat, melt 3 tbsp butter and cook diced apples until soft, about 5-6 minutes | Sprinkle with cinnamon, stir, and set aside to cool | In a large bowl, combine all-purpose flour, whole wheat flour, rolled oats, baking powder, baking soda, and diced Swiss cheese ? make a well in the center | In a separate bowl, cream 1/2 cup softened butter with brown sugar until light and fluffy | Beat in eggs one at a time | Gradually add milk, vanilla extract, and the cooled apple mixture, stirring to combine | Pour the wet ingredients into the well of dry ingredients and stir with a wooden spoon until just combined ? do not overmix | Spread batter evenly in the prepared loaf pan | If desired, arrange a few additional thin apple slices on top | Bake in the center of the oven for 1 hour or until a toothpick inserted in the center comes out clean | Let cool in the pan for 10 minutes, then turn out onto a wire rack | Sprinkle with powdered sugar after cooling if desired | Can also be baked as muffins for 15-20 minutes | Batter may be prepared the day before, refrigerated, and baked in the morning ? add 10-15 minutes extra baking time if cold | Freezes very well

ingredients: For crust: 1 cup all-purpose flour, 1/2 cup pecans (finely crushed), 1/2 cup unsalted butter (melted). For middle layer: 8 oz cream cheese (softened), 1 cup powdered sugar, 1 cup whipped topping (thawed). For top layer: 2 packages instant chocolate pudding mix, 3 cups cold milk, 2 cups whipped topping (for spreading), 1/4 cup pecan pieces (for garnish)
instructions: Preheat oven to 350?F (175?C) | Make the crust: combine flour, crushed pecans, and melted butter in a bowl, mixing until crumbly | Press the mixture firmly into the bottom of a 9x13-inch pan | Bake for 10-12 minutes until lightly golden | Allow crust to cool completely before layering | Make the middle layer: beat softened cream cheese and powdered sugar in a large bowl with an electric mixer on medium speed until well blended and smooth | Gently stir in 1 cup of whipped topping until incorporated | Spread the cream cheese mixture evenly over the cooled crust | Make the top layer: combine cold milk and instant chocolate pudding mix in a large bowl | Beat with a wire whisk for 2 minutes or until well blended and beginning to thicken | Spoon the pudding over the cream cheese layer and spread evenly | Refrigerate until set, at least 2 hours | Just before serving, spread remaining whipped topping over the top and sprinkle with pecan pieces | Refrigerate any leftovers | Chocolate pudding can be substituted with lemon pudding for a different variation

ingredients: For topping: 1 cup rolled oats, 1/2 cup dark brown sugar (packed), 1/3 cup all-purpose flour, 1/2 cup unsalted butter (cold, cubed), 1/2 cup gingersnap cookie crumbs, 1 egg yolk, 1/4 cup chopped nuts. For filling: 6 medium apples (peeled and sliced), 1 1/2 cups fresh cranberries, 1/2 cup granulated sugar, 1 tsp ground cinnamon, 1 tbsp lemon juice
instructions: Preheat oven to 350?F (175?C) and butter a 2-quart baking dish | Prepare the topping: mix together rolled oats, brown sugar, and flour in a bowl | Blend in cold butter with your fingers until coarse crumbs form | Add gingersnap crumbs, egg yolk, and chopped nuts, blending well until the mixture is crumbly | In a separate bowl, combine sliced apples, fresh cranberries, granulated sugar, cinnamon, and lemon juice ? toss to coat evenly | Spoon the fruit filling into the buttered baking dish | Sprinkle the topping evenly over the filling, covering completely | Bake for 30 minutes or until golden and bubbly | If the topping browns too quickly, cover loosely with foil for the last 10 minutes of baking | Serve warm with vanilla ice cream or a drizzle of warm caramel sauce

ingredients: 4 medium zucchini (sliced into rounds), 2 tbsp olive oil, 1/2 cup Parmesan cheese (grated), 1 tsp Italian seasoning, 1/2 tsp salt, 1/4 tsp black pepper, 1/4 cup breadcrumbs (optional, for extra crunch)
instructions: Preheat oven to 350?F (175?C) | Coat the bottom of a glass baking dish or metal pan with 1 tablespoon olive oil | Arrange sliced zucchini rounds in the dish in overlapping rows | Drizzle remaining olive oil evenly over the top of the zucchini | Sprinkle grated Parmesan cheese generously over all | Sprinkle Italian seasoning, salt, and black pepper on top | For extra crunch, add a light layer of breadcrumbs | Bake for 30 minutes until zucchini is tender and the cheese is golden and bubbly | Serve hot as a side dish

ingredients: 400g spaghettini or thin spaghetti, 1/4 cup olive oil, 3 large sweet onions (thinly sliced), 4 cloves garlic (minced), 1/2 cup chicken broth, 1/2 tsp dried thyme, 1/4 tsp black pepper, 1 cup frozen peas (thawed), 1 cup Swiss cheese (shredded), 1/4 cup fresh parsley (chopped), salt to taste
instructions: In a large skillet, heat olive oil over medium heat | Add sliced onions and minced garlic, tossing to coat with oil | Reduce heat to low, cover, and cook, stirring occasionally, until onions are very tender and a deep golden color, about 15 minutes | Stir in chicken broth, dried thyme, and black pepper, cooking for 2 more minutes | Meanwhile, cook spaghettini in a large pot of salted boiling water until al dente | Drain pasta and place in a large serving bowl | Add thawed peas and the smothered onions to the pasta | Toss everything together to combine evenly | Add shredded Swiss cheese and chopped parsley, tossing again until the cheese begins to melt | Season to taste with salt and additional pepper | Serve immediately in warm bowls

ingredients: 500g chicken tenders, 1 cup yellow cornmeal, 1 tbsp chili powder, 1 tsp dried oregano, 1 tsp salt, 1/4 tsp black pepper, 2 large eggs, 1/4 cup vegetable oil (for frying), ranch or honey mustard for dipping
instructions: In a shallow bowl, combine cornmeal, chili powder, oregano, salt, and pepper | In another shallow bowl, beat the eggs until well combined | Working with one at a time, coat each chicken tender in the cornmeal mixture, dip into the beaten egg, then coat again with the cornmeal mixture ? this double-coating ensures maximum crispiness | Transfer coated tenders to a large plate | For a healthier version: preheat oven to 450?F (230?C), place coated tenders on a greased baking sheet, and bake for 12 minutes, turning once | For pan-frying: heat 1/4 cup vegetable oil in a large skillet over medium heat | Add half the chicken tenders and cook, turning once, until golden brown and cooked through, about 5 to 6 minutes total | Transfer to a plate and tent with foil to keep warm | Repeat with remaining chicken tenders | Serve immediately with ranch dressing or honey mustard for dipping

ingredients: 500g minced beef, 1 medium onion (finely diced), 2 large eggs, 3 cloves garlic (minced), 1 tsp dried basil, 1 tsp salt, 1/2 tsp black pepper, 4 medium potatoes (peeled), vegetable oil for frying, lettuce leaves for serving, fresh dill and parsley (chopped), cucumber slices for garnish
instructions: Mix minced beef with one beaten egg, diced onion, minced garlic, basil, salt, and pepper until well combined | Form the meat mixture into small thin patties and set aside | Peel potatoes and grate them using the large holes of a box grater | Add a pinch of salt to the grated potatoes and mix well | Roll the grated potatoes into small balls ? each latke requires two potato balls and one meat patty | Flatten one potato ball with a fork or spoon on a clean surface, place a meat patty on top, then cover with another flattened potato ball, sealing the edges | Heat vegetable oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat | Fry each potato and meat latke for 3-4 minutes per side until golden brown and crispy on both sides | Drain on paper towels | Serve on lettuce leaves and garnish with cucumber slices and chopped fresh dill and parsley

ingredients: 16 oz cream cheese (softened), 3/4 cup granulated sugar, 1 tsp vanilla extract, 3 large eggs, 1 prepared graham cracker crust (9-inch), fresh fruit pur?e or pie filling for topping
instructions: Preheat oven to 350?F (175?C) | With an electric mixer at medium speed, beat softened cream cheese, sugar, eggs, and vanilla extract until well blended and smooth ? do not overbeat | Pour the filling into the prepared graham cracker crust and spread evenly | Bake for 40 minutes or until the center is almost set but still slightly jiggly | Turn off oven and let cheesecake cool inside with the door slightly open for 30 minutes | Remove from oven and cool completely at room temperature | Refrigerate for at least 3 hours or overnight until fully set | Top with your favorite pur?e of seasonal fruit or pie filling before serving | Slice and serve chilled

ingredients: 2 lbs pickling cucumbers (sliced into 1/4-inch thick rounds), boiling water, 1 cup cider vinegar, 1 cup water, 1 cup sugar substitute, 1 tsp canning salt, 1 tsp mustard seeds, 1 tsp whole allspice, 1 tsp celery seed, 2 cinnamon sticks
instructions: Wash and rinse pint canning jars and keep hot until ready to use | Prepare lids according to manufacturer's directions | Wash cucumbers and slice 1/16-inch off the blossom ends, then discard | Slice cucumbers into 1/4-inch thick rounds | Pour boiling water over the cucumber slices and let stand for 5 to 10 minutes | Drain off the hot water and run cold water over the cucumbers until they are completely cooled | Drain slices well | In a 10-quart Dutch oven or stockpot, mix vinegar, 1 cup water, sugar substitute, and all spices | Bring to a boil and carefully add drained cucumber slices to the boiling liquid | Return to a boil | Place one cinnamon stick in each jar if desired | With a slotted spoon, fill hot pickle slices into clean hot pint jars, leaving 1/2-inch headspace | Cover with boiling hot pickling brine, leaving 1/2-inch headspace | Remove air bubbles and adjust headspace if needed | Wipe rims of jars with a dampened clean paper towel and apply two-piece metal canning lids | Process in a boiling water canner for 10 minutes | Let cool undisturbed for 12 to 24 hours and check for seals

ingredients: 2 tbsp olive oil, 3 cloves garlic (minced), 1 tsp lemon zest, 1 tsp dried herbs (thyme or rosemary), 200g green beans (trimmed), 200g asparagus spears (trimmed), 1/2 cup breadcrumbs, 1/2 cup mozzarella cheese (shredded), 1/4 cup Swiss cheese (shredded), 1 tbsp olive oil (for topping)
instructions: Preheat oven to 425?F (220?C) | Line a baking sheet with parchment paper | In a small bowl, combine 2 tablespoons olive oil, minced garlic, lemon zest, and dried herbs | Spread trimmed green beans and asparagus spears evenly on the prepared baking sheet | Toss vegetables with the oil mixture until evenly coated | Roast for 15 minutes, turning vegetables halfway through | Meanwhile, combine breadcrumbs, mozzarella, Swiss cheese, and remaining 1 tablespoon olive oil in a small bowl | Remove vegetables from oven and set broiler to high | Transfer roasted vegetables to an ovenproof gratin dish | Sprinkle the cheese and breadcrumb mixture evenly over the top | Broil until the cheese melts and bubbles, about 1-2 minutes ? watch carefully to prevent burning | Serve immediately

ingredients: 2 cups cooked chicken (shredded), 8 oz cream cheese (softened), 1 cup salsa (red or green), 1 cup shredded Mexican blend cheese, 1/4 cup red onion (diced, optional), 1/4 cup black beans (optional), 2 tbsp fresh cilantro (chopped), tortilla chips for serving
instructions: In a microwave-safe bowl, microwave the cooked chicken until it is heated through, about 1 to 2 minutes | Shred the hot chicken with two forks until finely pulled | Add cream cheese on top of the chicken and microwave in 10-second intervals until the cream cheese is softened and easy to stir | Stir in the salsa until well combined | Stir in the shredded cheese until melted and fully incorporated | Stir in any additional ingredients you choose ? diced red onion, black beans, cilantro, or whatever you like | You can serve this dip hot or cold | Serve with sturdy tortilla chips or scoops for dipping | This makes a small batch of appetizer portions ? double or triple the recipe if feeding a crowd

ingredients: 8 oz cream cheese (softened), 1 tbsp prepared horseradish, 1 clove garlic (minced), 1/4 tsp kosher salt, 1/4 tsp cracked black pepper (plus extra for garnish), 200g sliced turkey pastrami, green leaf lettuce leaves (cut into small strips), toothpicks for securing
instructions: Mix the softened cream cheese, horseradish, minced garlic, salt, and pepper together until well blended and smooth | Lay the pastrami slices on a flat surface | Spread a small amount of the cheese mixture evenly on each pastrami slice | Cut the pastrami slices into approximately 1-inch by 3-inch strips (or similar size depending on what your deli provides) so that when rolled they will be bite-size pieces | Cut small pieces of green leaf lettuce to fit one side of each pastrami strip | Place the lettuce on the cream cheese mixture so that when rolled, a small portion of the curly lettuce extends beyond the pastrami | Roll up each pastrami strip from the opposite end of the lettuce and secure with a toothpick | You should have a roll of pastrami with the leaf lettuce peeking out | Arrange on a serving plate and sprinkle with freshly cracked black pepper | Serve immediately or refrigerate until ready to serve

ingredients: 200g dark chocolate (70% cocoa, broken into pieces), 1 tsp instant coffee or espresso powder, 3 tbsp boiling water, 4 large eggs (separated), pinch of salt, whipped cream for serving (optional)
instructions: Break up the chocolate into a small heavy saucepan | Dissolve the coffee or espresso powder in the boiling water and pour it over the chocolate | Place over low heat and stir occasionally with a small wire whisk until the mixture is completely smooth | Remove from heat and set aside for about 5 minutes to cool slightly | In the bowl of an electric mixer at high speed, beat the egg yolks for 3 to 4 minutes until pale lemon-colored and thick | With a spatula, add the chocolate mixture to the yolks and mix until smooth ? do not overmix | In a separate clean bowl, add a pinch of salt to the egg whites and beat until they hold a definite shape but are not dry | Gently fold the beaten whites into the chocolate mixture in thirds, folding only until no white streaks remain | Pour gently into serving glasses or bowls, filling about 3/4 full | Cover with plastic wrap and refrigerate for 3 to 6 hours ? can be refrigerated for up to 24 hours though the texture becomes more spongy over time | Serve with whipped cream on top if desired

ingredients: 1 1/2 cups icing sugar, 1/2 cup unsalted butter (softened), 1 tsp lemon zest, 1 vanilla bean (seeds scraped) or 1 tsp vanilla extract, 1/4 tsp salt, 1 cup all-purpose flour, 1/2 cup ground hazelnuts, 1 tsp baking powder, 1/2 cup raisins, 1 1/2 cups carrots (grated), 1/4 cup heavy cream (whipped), 1/2 cup walnuts (whole, for topping)
instructions: Preheat oven to 180?C (350?F) | In a large bowl, whip together icing sugar, softened butter, vanilla, and lemon zest until light and fluffy | Sift the flour and baking powder together in a separate bowl | Add the ground hazelnuts to the flour and mix well | Mix the flour-hazelnut mixture into the butter mixture until just combined | Fold in the whipped cream (this replaces eggs for moisture) and mix well | Stir in the raisins and grated carrots until evenly distributed | Grease and flour a 7-inch cake tin, or use well-greased and dusted individual muffin molds | Pour the prepared batter into the tin and spread evenly | Arrange whole walnuts over the top of the cake | Bake for 25 minutes or until a wooden toothpick inserted in the center comes out clean | Turn out onto a wire rack and allow to cool completely | Dust with icing sugar before serving | If using muffin molds, you can dip the cooled tops in melted chocolate to retain moisture

ingredients: 3 large eggs, 1/4 cup shredded cheese (cheddar, Swiss, or Gruy?re), 1 tbsp butter, salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Whisk the eggs in a bowl until light and fluffy ? the more air incorporated, the fluffier the omelette | Stir in shredded cheese and season with salt and pepper | Mix well | Heat a 7-inch non-stick skillet over medium heat and add butter | As the butter begins to foam but before it browns, lower the heat to medium-low | Pour the beaten egg mixture into the pan, tilting to spread evenly | Cook covered for 1 minute until the eggs are set on the bottom but still slightly glossy on top | Using a spatula, gently fold one half of the omelette over the other | Slide onto a warm plate and serve immediately

ingredients: 4 paua (New Zealand abalone, cleaned and shucked), 3 tbsp butter, 1 Spanish onion (diced), 1 tbsp fresh ginger (grated), 1/2 tsp fresh ground black pepper, 1 cup champagne or sparkling wine, 1/2 cup fish stock, 1/4 cup heavy cream, 1 tsp balsamic vinegar, steamed white rice for serving
instructions: Drown paua in fresh water for a minimum of 6 hours and a maximum of 8 hours until the flesh is limp to the touch | Shuck the flesh from the shells and trim off the skirt and gut, placing the cleaned flesh to one side | Heat butter in a large frypan over medium heat | Saut? diced onion and grated ginger until golden brown, about 6-8 minutes | Add black pepper at the last minute and saut? for a further 30 seconds | Pour in champagne with the heat at a very very low simmer ? do not allow to boil at any time, this is critical for tender paua | Add the paua, cover, and cook at a very low simmer for 1 to 1 1/2 hours ? remember, do not let it boil or the paua will toughen | Remove paua and place to one side, covered to keep warm | Add fish stock and cream to the remaining liquid in the pan | Bring to a boil and reduce the liquid to a warm honey consistency ? this should take only a minute | Add balsamic vinegar and stir | Turn off the heat, return the warm paua to the pan, and stir to coat in the sauce | Serve arranged over steamed plain white rice with a lettuce and tomato salad

ingredients: 4 boneless skinless chicken breasts, 1/2 cup mayonnaise (or Italian dressing, or honey mustard), 1 1/2 cups breadcrumbs (Italian or panko), 1/2 tsp salt, 1/4 tsp black pepper
instructions: Preheat oven to 425?F (220?C) and lightly grease a baking sheet | Thaw chicken breasts if frozen and pat completely dry with paper towels | Coat each raw chicken breast generously with your chosen base ? mayonnaise, Italian dressing, or honey mustard all work beautifully | Roll the coated chicken in breadcrumbs, pressing firmly so the crumbs adhere evenly on all sides | Season with salt and pepper | Place coated chicken on the prepared baking sheet | Bake for 20 minutes or until the chicken is golden brown and the internal temperature reaches 165?F (74?C) | Let rest for 3-5 minutes before serving | Serve with a side salad or steamed vegetables

ingredients: 450g dried navy beans (soaked overnight), 6 slices bacon (diced), 1 medium onion (diced), 2 celery ribs (diced), 2 carrots (diced), 1 tsp salt, 1/2 tsp black pepper, 6 cups water
instructions: Soak dried navy beans in plenty of water overnight, then drain and rinse | The next day, cook diced bacon in a large pot over medium heat until crisp | Remove bacon with a slotted spoon and drain on paper towels, then slice into small pieces and set aside | Put 1/2 cup of the soaked beans aside | Add the remaining beans to a large pot of fresh water along with diced onion, carrots, and celery | Place the reserved 1/2 cup of beans in a blender with a splash of water and blend for 30-60 seconds until smooth | Add the blended beans to the pot ? this acts as a natural thickener | Bring to a boil, then add the crispy bacon pieces | Reduce heat and cook on medium for 1 hour and 15 minutes, or until the beans are soft and tender | For a thicker soup, use a potato masher to mash some of the beans during cooking | Season with salt and black pepper to taste | Serve hot in bowls

ingredients: 200g turkey sausage, 200g pork sausage, 2 tbsp extra virgin olive oil, 2 potatoes (peeled and diced, or 2 cups frozen hash browns), salt and black pepper, 2 tbsp butter (divided), 4 scallions (sliced, white and green parts separated), 2 tbsp all-purpose flour, 2 cups low-fat milk, 2 tomatoes (diced), 6 large eggs (beaten), 1/2 cup sharp cheddar cheese (shredded)
instructions: In a large nonstick skillet, cook turkey and pork sausage over medium-high heat, breaking it up with a wooden spoon, until browned, about 5 minutes ? remove from heat and set aside | In a medium cast-iron skillet, heat olive oil over medium heat | Add diced potatoes or frozen hash browns, season with 1/4 teaspoon salt and pepper, and cook, turning infrequently, until browned, about 15 minutes | Meanwhile, in a small saucepan, melt 1 tablespoon butter over medium heat | Add white parts of scallions and cook until softened, about 2 minutes | Stir in flour and cook for 1 minute, then gradually whisk in milk | Cook until thickened, season with salt and pepper, cover, and keep warm | Return the nonstick skillet with sausage to medium-high heat and add remaining 1 tablespoon butter | Add diced tomatoes and beaten eggs with a couple pinches of salt and pepper | Cook, scrambling, until eggs are just set, about 2-3 minutes | Divide the egg mixture among 4 plates | Top with the browned potatoes, drizzle with white sauce, and sprinkle with cheddar cheese | Garnish with reserved scallion greens and serve immediately

recipe_name: Chicken with White Beans and Spinach
ingredients: 3 boneless skinless chicken breasts (cut into strips), 1 tsp dried thyme, 1/2 tsp fresh ground black pepper, 2 tbsp butter (divided), 1/2 medium onion (diced), 3 cloves garlic (minced), 1/2 cup chicken broth, 1/4 cup dry white wine, 1 can (400g) cannellini beans (rinsed and drained), 3 cups baby spinach leaves, salt to taste
instructions: Cut chicken breasts into strips and season with dried thyme and black pepper | Melt 1 tablespoon butter in a large skillet over medium-high heat | Add chicken strips and brown over medium-high heat, about 3 to 4 minutes, stirring occasionally | Move chicken to one side of the skillet and add remaining 1/2 tablespoon butter | Add minced garlic and diced onion and saut? for 1 minute until fragrant | Pour in chicken broth and white wine | Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 5 minutes | Stir in rinsed and drained cannellini beans and baby spinach leaves | Simmer for 5 more minutes until chicken is cooked through and spinach is wilted | Season with salt to taste | Serve immediately in shallow bowls

ingredients: 400g sushi-grade ahi tuna (cut into 1/2-inch cubes), 3 tbsp soy sauce, 1 tbsp sesame oil, 1 tsp sriracha, 2 green onions (thinly sliced), 1 tbsp toasted sesame seeds, 1 avocado (diced), 1 tsp grated ginger, steamed white rice or wonton chips for serving
instructions: Ensure tuna is sushi-grade and very fresh ? it should be bright red with no fishy odor | Cut tuna into uniform 1/2-inch cubes using a very sharp knife | In a bowl, gently combine diced tuna with soy sauce, sesame oil, and sriracha | Add grated ginger and sliced green onions, folding gently to combine | Gently fold in diced avocado, being careful not to mash it | Cover and refrigerate for 15 minutes to allow flavors to meld | Sprinkle with toasted sesame seeds | Serve immediately over steamed white rice or with wonton chips for scooping

recipe_name: Scallops with Crumb Topping and Herb Butter
ingredients: For crumb topping: 1/3 cup yellow cornmeal, 2 tbsp pine nuts, 1 clove garlic, 1 1/2 tsp lemon peel (divided). For herb butter: 3 tbsp butter (softened), 2 tbsp fresh cilantro (chopped), 2 tbsp fresh parsley (chopped), 1 tsp fresh lemon juice. For scallops: 12 large sea scallops, 2 plum tomatoes (sliced), olive oil, salt and pepper. For salad: 1/4 cup olive oil, 1 tbsp fresh lime juice, 1 tsp honey, 1 tsp lime zest, 4 cups arugula, 1/4 cup fresh mint leaves
instructions: Finely grind cornmeal, pine nuts, garlic, and 1 teaspoon lemon peel in a food processor; set crumb mixture aside | In a small bowl, mix softened butter, cilantro, parsley, lemon juice, and remaining 1/2 teaspoon lemon peel | Season herb butter to taste with salt and pepper | Preheat oven to 450?F (230?C) | Brush a rimmed baking sheet with oil and place scallops on the sheet | Sprinkle scallops with salt and pepper | Top each scallop with a tomato slice, then divide the crumb mixture equally among them | Top each scallop with 1 teaspoon of herb butter | Bake until scallops are just opaque in the center, about 8 minutes | Meanwhile, whisk 1/4 cup olive oil, lime juice, honey, and lime zest in a small bowl to make the dressing | Season with salt and pepper | Toss arugula and mint in a bowl, adding dressing to taste | Divide dressed greens among 4 salad plates | Top with the baked scallops and serve immediately

ingredients: 4 boneless skinless chicken breasts, 2 cans (400g each) condensed cream of chicken soup, 1 can (400g) condensed cream of mushroom soup, 1/2 cup milk, 1/2 tsp garlic powder, 1/2 tsp black pepper, steamed rice, noodles, or mashed potatoes for serving
instructions: Preheat oven to 350?F (175?C) | Mix condensed soups together with milk, garlic powder, and black pepper in a baking dish large enough to hold the chicken | Add chicken breasts on top of the mixed soups, pressing them down slightly into the sauce | Bake at 350?F for about 45 minutes or until chicken juices run clear when pricked with a fork | If using bone-in chicken pieces, cooking time will be longer and you may want to cover the dish with foil so the sauce doesn't reduce too much | Serve the creamy sauce over steamed rice, buttered noodles, or mashed potatoes alongside the chicken

ingredients: 1 cup white chocolate baking bars (chopped), 1/4 cup nonfat milk, 2 tbsp light corn syrup, 12 large pretzel rods, assorted decorations (sprinkles, crushed candy canes, chopped nuts)
instructions: Line a baking sheet with waxed paper and set aside | Melt white chocolate baking bars in a small saucepan over low heat, stirring constantly until smooth | Stir in nonfat milk and corn syrup until well combined ? do not remove saucepan from heat | Holding each pretzel rod with a fork, dip one side of the pretzel into the melted mixture to coat | Place coated side up on the prepared baking sheet and immediately sprinkle with desired decorations | Repeat with remaining pretzel rods | Refrigerate for 15 to 20 minutes or until firm | Once set, serve or store in an airtight container | For chocolate twisters: substitute 1 cup semisweet chocolate chips for the white baking bars | For caramel dipping sauce: heat 1 cup fat-free caramel sauce with 1/3 cup finely chopped pecans until warm and serve alongside for dipping

ingredients: 3 tbsp extra virgin olive oil, 4 cloves garlic (minced), 1/2 tsp crushed red pepper flakes, 1 kg littleneck clams (scrubbed and rinsed), 1/2 cup dry white wine, 1 cup tomato sauce, 3 scallions (thinly sliced), 1/4 cup fresh basil leaves (torn), salt to taste, crusty bread for serving
instructions: In a large wide heavy casserole or Dutch oven, heat 3 tablespoons olive oil over a medium flame | Add minced garlic and cook until golden brown, stirring for approximately 2 minutes | Add crushed red pepper flakes and stir briefly | Add clams and white wine | Place a lid on the pot, turn flame to high, and cook shaking the pot occasionally for approximately 7 minutes or until clams begin to open | Pour in tomato sauce, add sliced scallions and torn basil | Stir well and bring the mixture to a boil | Using a slotted spoon, transfer clams to a serving platter and discard any clams that did not open | Spoon the sauce over the clams and serve immediately with crusty bread on the side for dipping

ingredients: For dressing: 2 tbsp Dijon mustard, juice of 2 lemons, 1/3 cup olive oil, 1/4 tsp cayenne pepper, 1/2 tsp salt. For salad: 500g red potatoes (scrubbed), 300g asparagus spears (trimmed), 2 tbsp fresh chives (chopped)
instructions: Make the dressing: in a small bowl, combine Dijon mustard and fresh lemon juice | Whisk in olive oil gradually until smooth and emulsified | Season with salt and cayenne pepper, then set aside | Clean potatoes and asparagus very well | Cook potatoes in a large pot of boiling salted water until just tender, about 20-30 minutes depending on size | Strain and rinse with cool water, then set aside to cool | Cook asparagus in a large pot of boiling salted water until just crisp-tender, about 5 minutes | Strain and rinse with cool water to stop the cooking process | Once cool, cut potatoes in half and asparagus into bite-sized pieces | Toss potatoes and asparagus together in a large bowl and add chopped chives | Pour the dressing over the mixture and toss gently to coat evenly | Serve at room temperature

ingredients: 1 pizza dough (12-14 inch), 1/2 cup ricotta cheese, 1/4 cup prepared Italian marinade (divided), 1 red bell pepper (sliced), 1 yellow bell pepper (sliced), 1/2 red onion (sliced), 1 medium zucchini (sliced), 2 tbsp olive oil, 1 1/2 cups mozzarella cheese (shredded, divided)
instructions: Mix ricotta cheese with 1 tablespoon of the prepared marinade in a small bowl | Refrigerate until ready to use | Place sliced bell peppers, red onion, and zucchini in a large resealable plastic bag or glass dish | Add remaining marinade and toss to coat well | Refrigerate for 15 minutes or longer for extra flavor | Remove vegetables from marinade, reserving the marinade | Grill vegetables over medium-high heat for 2 to 4 minutes per side until tender-crisp, brushing with reserved marinade halfway through | Cut grilled vegetables into bite-size pieces | Stretch or roll pizza dough on a floured baking sheet to a 12 to 14-inch round, about 1/4-inch thick | Brush the top of the dough with olive oil | Place oiled-side down on the grill and close the lid | Grill over medium heat for 1 to 2 minutes until grill marks appear on the bottom | Carefully flip crust over using tongs or a spatula | Layer crust with the ricotta mixture, half of the mozzarella, grilled vegetables, and remaining mozzarella | Close the lid and grill for 3 to 4 minutes longer until cheese is melted and crust is browned, checking frequently to avoid burning | Slide pizza onto a baking sheet, slice, and serve immediately

ingredients: 500g breakfast sausage, 1 green bell pepper (diced), 1 medium onion (diced), 100g fresh mushrooms (sliced), 1/2 tsp garlic powder, 1/4 tsp black pepper, 8 large eggs, 1 cup Monterey Jack and cheddar cheese blend (shredded), 4 large flour tortillas, 2 packets country gravy mix (prepared), 2 tbsp vegetable oil
instructions: Prepare gravy mixes as directed on package in a medium saucepan and keep warm | In a medium skillet, brown breakfast sausage over medium-high heat, crumbling while cooking | Remove sausage with a slotted spoon and set aside | Pour off excess fat, reserving 2 tablespoons in the skillet and adding 2 tablespoons to the gravy if desired for extra sausage flavor | Saut? diced peppers, onions, and mushrooms in the reserved fat until tender, about 5-6 minutes | Stir in garlic powder, black pepper, and the cooked sausage | Separate the mixture into 4 sections in the pan, turn off the burner, and cover with a lid to keep warm | To prepare eggs: whisk 2 eggs at a time and cook each set in an omelet pan sprayed with cooking spray to form a thin crepe-like omelet ? you should have 4 thin omelets | Warm tortillas as directed on package to make them pliable | To assemble: place one omelet on each tortilla | Spread the sausage mixture down the center of each tortilla on top of the eggs | Sprinkle each with shredded cheese | Roll into burritos and place one on each plate seam-side down | Cover with warm gravy and serve immediately

ingredients: 1 tbsp olive oil, 2 medium yellow onions (diced), 6 medium carrots (peeled and chopped), 1 tbsp curry powder, 1 tsp garam masala, 1/2 tsp ground cumin, 1/4 tsp ground cinnamon, 1/2 tsp salt, 4 cups vegetable broth, 1 cup light coconut milk, 1 red bell pepper (roasted and diced, optional), cooked chickpeas or rice for serving (optional)
instructions: In a medium or large stock pot, heat olive oil over medium heat | Saut? diced onions until they become translucent, about 5 minutes | Add chopped carrots, salt, curry powder, cumin, garam masala, and cinnamon | Continue to saut? until onions are soft, about 5 more minutes | Stir vegetable broth into the onion, carrot, and spice mixture | Bring to a boil, then cover and simmer until carrots are tender, about 20-25 minutes | Add roasted red peppers to the pot if using and simmer on low until peppers are tender, about 5 minutes | Remove from heat and blend with an immersion blender until smooth, or carefully transfer to a blender in batches | Add coconut milk and continue to blend until silky smooth and creamy | Serve hot with garbanzo beans or rice added to the soup for extra heartiness

ingredients: 1 can (354ml) evaporated milk (well chilled), 1/3 cup granulated sugar, 1 packet unsweetened Kool-Aid drink mix (any flavor), 1 prepared graham cracker crust (9-inch), vanilla wafer cookies for lining (optional), whipped topping for garnish
instructions: Pour very cold evaporated milk into a small metal or glass mixing bowl and add beaters to the bowl | Cover and chill in the refrigerator for at least 2 hours ? the milk must be extremely cold to whip properly | Coat a 9-inch pie plate with cooking spray and line the bottom and sides with vanilla wafers if desired | Beat the chilled evaporated milk with an electric mixer until soft peaks form, about 5 minutes | Add sugar and Kool-Aid drink mix | Beat until thoroughly mixed and the color is uniform, about 2 more minutes | Spoon the mixture over the prepared crust or wafers and spread evenly | Freeze for at least 4 hours until firm | Garnish with whipped topping if desired before serving | Slice and serve frozen

ingredients: 1 kg pickling cucumbers (small, scrubbed), 4 sprigs fresh dill (divided), 4 cloves garlic, 2 tbsp pickling salt, 2 cups white vinegar, 2 cups boiling water
instructions: Sterilize canning jars and keep hot until ready to use | Place 1/2 sprig of fresh dill and 1 clove of garlic at the bottom of each jar | Fill the jars tightly with whole pickling cucumbers, packing them in vertically | Place remaining 1/2 sprig of dill on top of the cucumbers in each jar | Combine pickling salt, vinegar, and boiling water in a large pot, stirring until salt is fully dissolved | Pour the hot brine over the cucumbers, filling each jar to within 1/2-inch of the top | Remove air bubbles, wipe rims clean, and seal with sterilized lids and bands | Process in a boiling water bath for 10 minutes | Let cool undisturbed for 12-24 hours and check for proper seals before storing

ingredients: 1 pound cake (store-bought or homemade, sliced 1/2-inch thick), 2 cans (400ml each) coconut milk, 1/2 cup unsalted butter, 1/2 cup granulated sugar, 4 large eggs, 1 tsp vanilla extract, 3 tbsp cornstarch mixed with 3 tbsp water, 1 cup sweetened shredded coconut, 1/2 tsp ground cinnamon
instructions: Slice pound cake into 1/2-inch thickness | Line the entire bottom of a 9 x 13-inch dish with cake slices, cutting pieces to fit around corners and between larger slices | Pour coconut milk into a large pot over medium-high heat | Add butter and sugar, stirring occasionally, and bring to a gentle boil | Lower heat slightly if necessary to maintain a gentle bubble | While waiting for the milk to heat, beat eggs and vanilla in a medium bowl and set aside | Mix cornstarch and water in a small bowl and set aside | When the milk comes to a boil, pour the egg mixture a little bit at a time into the milk, whisking quickly and constantly | Stir continuously and let the egg and milk mixture come back to a gentle boil | Stir the cornstarch slurry again, then pour into the gently boiling custard | Add shredded coconut ? be careful as the custard will splatter | Stir vigorously and cook for two minutes until thickened | Pour the hot custard evenly over the pound cake layer | Sprinkle with ground cinnamon | Cool uncovered at room temperature for 30 minutes, then continue cooling uncovered in the refrigerator | This coconut latiya is exceptional after two days of refrigeration

ingredients: 2 cups all-purpose flour, 1 1/2 cups white sugar, 1/2 cup powdered sugar, 1 tsp baking soda, 1 tsp baking powder, 1/2 tsp salt, 3 large eggs, 1/4 cup amaretto liqueur, 1 cup coconut milk, 1/2 cup buttermilk, 1/2 cup vegetable oil, 1 tsp vanilla extract. For frosting: cream cheese frosting with a splash of coconut milk
instructions: Preheat oven to 350?F (175?C) | Grease and flour two 9-inch round cake pans or one 9x13-inch pan | In a large bowl, combine flour, white sugar, powdered sugar, baking soda, baking powder, and salt | Make a well in the center of the dry ingredients | Add eggs, amaretto liqueur, coconut milk, buttermilk, oil, and vanilla extract | Beat for 2 minutes on medium speed ? batter will be thin | Pour batter into prepared pans | Bake for 30 to 40 minutes until a toothpick inserted into the center of the cake comes out clean | Cool for 10 minutes in the pans, then remove from pans and finish cooling on a wire rack | Fill and frost as desired ? cream cheese frosting with a splash of coconut milk works beautifully | Slice and serve at room temperature

ingredients: 4 large eggs, 200g breakfast sausage, 1 cup water, 1 cup half-and-half, 1 cup stone-ground corn grits, 1/2 cup Gruy?re cheese (grated), 1 tbsp rendered sausage fat (for greasing), salt and black pepper to taste, fresh chives for garnish
instructions: Preheat oven to 400?F (200?C) | Brown sausage in a pan over medium heat, crumbling as it cooks | Drain sausage on paper towels and reserve the grease | While sausage is browning, bring 3 cups of water and 1 cup of half-and-half to a boil in a medium saucepan | Pour 1 cup of grits into a bowl of water and tilt the bowl to pour off any floating bits into the sink | Scoop drained grits into the boiling milk mixture | Whisk boiling grits for 5 minutes, then reduce to a simmer for 20 minutes, continuing to whisk occasionally | Season with salt and several grinds of black pepper | Use the rendered sausage fat to grease 4 large individual ramekins or gratin dishes and arrange them on a rimmed sheet tray | Divide creamy grits between the prepared baking dishes | Top each with crumbled sausage and grated Gruy?re | Make a small divot in the center of the mixture to nest the egg | Crack one egg into a small bowl, then carefully slide it into the divot | Repeat with remaining eggs | Bake until the egg whites are almost but not fully set, about 10 to 15 minutes ? for more well-done eggs, bake until whites are fully set | Garnish with fresh chives and serve immediately

ingredients: 500g asparagus spears (trimmed), 3 tbsp unsalted butter, 1/2 tsp kosher salt, 1/4 tsp fresh ground black pepper, 1 tbsp fresh tarragon (chopped)
instructions: Bring a large saucepan of water to a boil | Add asparagus and cook for 3 minutes until crisp-tender and bright green | Drain and immediately rinse under cold water to stop cooking | Drain well and set aside | Melt butter in a large skillet over medium heat | Cook the butter for 3 minutes, swirling the pan occasionally, until it turns golden brown and gives off a nutty fragrance | Stir in salt and black pepper | Add the blanched asparagus and chopped tarragon | Cook for 1 minute, tossing to coat the asparagus evenly in the browned butter | Transfer to a serving plate and serve immediately

ingredients: 6 medium apples (peeled, cored, and sliced), 1/3 cup maple syrup, 1/4 tsp salt, 1/4 tsp ground nutmeg, 1/2 tsp ground cinnamon, 1 tbsp cornstarch mixed with 2 tbsp apple juice or water
instructions: Place sliced apples, maple syrup, salt, nutmeg, and cinnamon in a medium saucepan | Bring to a simmer over medium heat, then cover and simmer until apples are tender, about 10-15 minutes, stirring occasionally | In a small bowl, combine cornstarch and apple juice (or water) and stir until smooth | Pour the cornstarch mixture into the stewed apples and stir gently | Continue cooking for 1-2 minutes until the sauce thickens and coats the apples | Remove from heat and serve warm over pancakes, oatmeal, ice cream, or on their own

ingredients: 8 cups sweet apple cider, 1/4 cup fresh lemon juice, 1/4 cup granulated sugar, 3 cinnamon sticks, 1 tsp whole cloves, 1 orange (sliced into rounds, optional), 1/4 tsp ground nutmeg
instructions: Combine apple cider, fresh lemon juice, sugar, cinnamon sticks, whole cloves, orange slices (if using), and nutmeg in a large pot | Bring to a boil over medium-high heat, stirring to dissolve the sugar | Reduce heat to low and simmer for 15-20 minutes to allow the spices to infuse | Strain through a fine mesh sieve to remove whole spices if desired, or ladle directly into mugs leaving spices behind | Serve hot in heatproof mugs or glasses

ingredients: 4 boneless skinless chicken breast halves, 1/2 tsp salt, 1/4 tsp black pepper, 4 slices Swiss cheese, 1 can (400g) cream of chicken soup, 1 can (400g) cream of mushroom soup, 1/2 cup milk, 1 cup chicken broth, 2 cups Stove Top stuffing mix (dry), 1/4 cup unsalted butter (melted)
instructions: Place chicken breasts in the bottom of a crock pot or slow cooker | Pour chicken broth over the chicken breasts | Season chicken with salt and pepper | Place one slice of Swiss cheese on top of each chicken breast | In a separate bowl, combine both cans of soup and milk, mixing well | Pour the soup mixture evenly over the chicken breasts | Sprinkle the dry stuffing mix over the entire top of the dish | Drizzle melted butter evenly over the stuffing | Cover and cook on low for 6-8 hours or on high for 4 hours until chicken is cooked through | Serve hot, scooping down through the layers

ingredients: For sauce: 1/2 cup Swiss cheese (shredded), 1/4 cup Parmesan cheese (grated), 1/2 cup half-and-half, 1/4 cup whole milk, 1 tbsp butter, 1 tbsp all-purpose flour, pinch of nutmeg. For chicken: 2 boneless skinless chicken breast halves (flattened slightly), 1 tbsp butter, 200g broccoli florets (steamed), salt and pepper
instructions: Make the Mornay sauce: melt 1 tbsp butter in a saucepan over medium heat | Whisk in flour and cook for 1 minute | Gradually whisk in half-and-half and milk | Heat over low heat, stirring frequently, until the sauce is hot and begins to thicken | Add Swiss cheese and Parmesan cheese, stirring until fully melted and smooth | Season with a pinch of nutmeg, salt, and pepper, then keep warm | Meanwhile, flatten chicken breasts slightly to an even thickness | Season with salt and pepper | Melt 1 tbsp butter in a skillet over medium heat and saut? chicken until golden brown and cooked through, about 8 to 10 minutes | While chicken cooks, steam broccoli florets until crisp-tender, about 3-4 minutes | Arrange cooked chicken and steamed broccoli on serving plates | Spoon the warm Mornay sauce generously over all | Serve immediately

ingredients: 6 Bartlett pears (peeled, cored, and finely chopped), 1 orange (peel reserved and slivered, fruit chopped), 1 lemon (peel reserved and slivered, fruit chopped), 1 can (400g) crushed pineapple in juice, 1/4 cup maraschino cherries (chopped), 5 cups granulated sugar, 1 package (57g) fruit pectin, 1 tsp butter
instructions: Peel and core pears, then finely chop or grind the fruit | Measure 4 cups of chopped pears into an 8-quart saucepan | Remove the colored part of the peel from the orange using a vegetable peeler and set aside | Remove and discard the remaining white pith from the orange | Chop the orange fruit, reserving any juice, and add to the saucepan | Repeat the procedure with the lemon and add to the saucepan | Cut the reserved orange and lemon peels into thin slivers or finely chop and add to the saucepan | Add crushed pineapple with its juice and chopped maraschino cherries to the saucepan and mix thoroughly | Measure sugar into a separate bowl | Mix 1/4 cup of the measured sugar with the pectin in a small bowl | Stir the pectin-sugar mixture into the fruit in the saucepan and add butter | Place over high heat and bring to a full boil, stirring constantly | Immediately stir in the remaining sugar | Bring back to a full rolling boil and boil for exactly 1 minute, stirring constantly | Remove from heat and ladle quickly into hot sterilized jars, filling to within 1/8 inch of the tops | Wipe jar rims and threads clean | Cover with two-piece lids and screw bands tightly | Place jars in a boiling water bath and process for 10 minutes | Makes about 7 one-cup jars

ingredients: 1/2 cup unsalted butter, 1/2 cup semi-sweet chocolate chips, 2 large eggs, 1 tsp pure vanilla extract, 3/4 cup granulated sugar, 1/2 cup purple fruit and vegetable pur?e (blueberry, beet, or spinach blend), 1 cup all-purpose flour, 1/4 cup unsweetened cocoa powder, 1/2 cup rolled oats, 1/4 tsp salt
instructions: Preheat oven to 350?F (175?C) | Butter or spray only the bottom (not the sides) of a 13-by-9-inch or 9-inch square baking pan | Melt butter and chocolate chips together in a double boiler or metal bowl over simmering water (or in a microwave, checking every 15 seconds) | Remove from heat and allow the mixture to cool slightly | Meanwhile, in another bowl, stir together eggs, vanilla, sugar, and the fruit/vegetable pur?e | Combine this mixture with the cooled chocolate mixture | In a mixing bowl, stir together flour, cocoa powder, oats, and salt | Add the dry mixture to the chocolate mixture and blend thoroughly until smooth | Pour the entire batter into the prepared baking pan and spread evenly | Bake for 30 to 35 minutes until a toothpick inserted comes out clean | Allow to cool completely in the pan before cutting into squares | Store in an airtight container

ingredients: 2 packages (85g each) strawberry jelly crystals, 2 cups boiling water, 2 cups cold water (divided), 2 cups fresh strawberries (halved), cream or ice cream for serving
instructions: Place jelly crystals in a large heatproof bowl | Pour 2 cups boiling water over the crystals | Whisk until the crystals have completely dissolved | Stir in 1 cup cold water | Pour 1/2 cup of the liquid jelly into a 7cm-deep rectangular dish | Place in the freezer for 5 to 10 minutes or until set | Arrange a single layer of halved strawberries, cut side down, onto the set jelly | Pour over another 1 cup of liquid jelly | Return to the freezer for 10 minutes or until set | Repeat the layering process twice more with remaining strawberries and liquid jelly | Refrigerate for 30 minutes or until completely firm | To serve, dip the base of the dish into hot water for 30 seconds and invert onto a serving platter | Serve with cream or ice cream

ingredients: 1 cup Parmesan cheese (freshly grated), 1 red apple (thinly sliced), 4 cups rocket (arugula), 2 tbsp olive oil, 1 tbsp balsamic vinegar, 1/2 tsp sea salt, 1/4 tsp black pepper, 100g goat cheese (crumbled, optional)
instructions: Preheat oven to 180?C (355?F) | Line a baking tray with non-stick baking paper | Arrange 8 portions of Parmesan cheese (about 1 1/2 tablespoons each) in circles on the prepared tray, spacing them apart | Bake for 10 minutes or until the cheese is melted, golden, and crispy | Remove from oven and set aside to cool ? the wafers will crisp up as they cool | In a large bowl, whisk together olive oil, balsamic vinegar, salt, and pepper | Toss sliced apple and rocket (arugula) in the dressing until lightly coated | Arrange the dressed salad on serving plates | Top with crumbled goat cheese if using and the crispy Parmesan wafers | Serve immediately

ingredients: 2 cups all-purpose flour, 2 tsp baking powder, 1/2 tsp salt, 1 tsp ground cinnamon, 1/4 tsp ground nutmeg, 3/4 cup nonfat milk, 3 tbsp canola oil, 1/4 cup honey, 3/4 cup raisins
instructions: Preheat oven to 425?F (220?C) and coat baking sheets with cooking spray | In a large bowl, combine flour, baking powder, salt, cinnamon, and nutmeg ? stir well | In a small bowl, combine milk, canola oil, and honey | Add the wet ingredients to the dry ingredients and stir just until moistened ? do not overmix | Gently stir in raisins | Drop the batter by tablespoonfuls onto the prepared baking sheets, spacing them about 2 inches apart | Bake for 8-10 minutes or until lightly browned on top | Remove from baking sheets and transfer to wire racks to cool slightly | Serve warm or at room temperature
